a03-haplography-source-gate.title: Does the A-03 image audit bound missed doubled runes?
a03-haplography-source-gate.question: Could missed doubled runes explain the repeat deficit?
a03-haplography-source-gate.finding: The classifier reports 99.4146% agreement against a 99.5% gate. Its source code loads 13,381 component rows but does not process them in the K control. The saved counts give 108−82=26 excess image pairs and a stated threshold of 93 additional pairs; without a measured error bound, the first number cannot cap the latter.
a03-haplography-source-gate.limitations: This is an audit of saved source receipts and inference, not an independent reading of the source images or a test of every autokey variant. A constructed error assignment shows logical possibility, not empirical plausibility.

scope.representation: Pinned Dukotah Round10 classifier output, log and Round16/A-03 source receipt, not original image pixels.
scope.procedure: Hash-check six source files, parse classifier agreement and count log, recompute the source threshold and arithmetic K control, inspect whether source code actually reprocesses glyph rows, and give a finite nonnegative error assignment with the same observed surplus.
scope.parameters: Source image agreement gate 99.5%; source comparison floor 1.38%; source counts as preserved at f08b20b.
scope.exclusions: No fresh image transcription, no measured classifier error rate for merged glyphs, no general autokey exclusion.

alberti-branch-arithmetic.title: Alberti branch proposal: LP2-39 row and modulo-31 arithmetic
alberti-branch-arithmetic.question: Do the source's identified LP2-39 row, 4–5–4 shift sums and claimed modulo-31 matches reproduce as written?
alberti-branch-arithmetic.finding: The identified row has 19 runes in groups of 3, 4, 6, 5 and 1. Left raw short sums −13 and −17 and right raw short sums −33 and −39 reproduce. The right pair reduces modulo 31 to 29 and 23, not the source's +2 and +8; obtaining the positive pair requires an additional direction reversal. The proposed deciphering rule cannot be checked from these arithmetic inputs.
alberti-branch-arithmetic.limitations: The transcript states the arrays but does not supply a complete fixed disk configuration and transition table. Its group and target choices were made during an evolving exploration, so the 13-rotation check is sensitivity analysis, not a statistical null. It cannot validate or refute the purported LP2-39 plaintext.

scope.representation: Archived LP2-39 UTF-8 rune transcription and the source's two explicit 13-number plant arrays, short overlay and posted final arrays, copied into a fixed plan. Source transcript identified by SHA-256, not republished.
scope.procedure: Recount the source-identified row's rune groups; calculate the two four-element overlaid short sums and all posted 4–5–4 final-array sums; reduce the signed values using standard nonnegative modulo-31 residues. Repeat short sums at all 13 cyclic starts for each plant array as a sensitivity diagnostic.
scope.parameters: One LP2-39 row; two posted 13-number arrays; one posted four-number overlay; fixed groups 4, 5, 4; 13 starting positions for each array; modulus 31. No fitted key, symbol mapping or selected plaintext.
scope.exclusions: Complete Alberti disk alphabets, rule-state transitions, branch inheritance, letter assembly, word-selection search, full-page reading, or a chance probability for the source's selected interpretation. The separate method files and diagrams referred to in the discussion are not available as pinned inputs here.

alternating-alphabet-interruption-clocks.title: Alternating alphabets with two interruption clocks
alternating-alphabet-interruption-clocks.question: Could F pause the key, the alphabet, or both?
alternating-alphabet-interruption-clocks.finding: Neither way of pausing at an F rune produced any of the nine predicted twelve-rune beginnings on the 55 tested pages. One rule paused just the key; the other also paused the switch between alphabets.
alternating-alphabet-interruption-clocks.limitations: A real reading could begin differently from all nine predictions. Other keys and interruption rules remain untested; the successful roundtrip controls show the rules work as specified, not that Cicada used them.

scope.representation: First twelve GP29 runes, including headings, of LP2-00–55; omit runeless LP2-50. Page-local state. Other characters do not advance it.
scope.procedure: Alternate ordinary/reversed cipher alphabets, each with its own known repeating key. Decode F normally but hold the selected key position there. Compare always-toggling versus F-paused alphabet clocks; compare each head with nine fixed twelve-rune known-reading openings.
scope.parameters: 2 key assignments × 104 phase pairs × 2 first alphabets × 2 signs × 2 clock policies = 1,664 settings; 55 pages; 823,680 exact comparisons. 1,664 roundtrips on 87 prescribed runes plus 1,664 forced-marker controls.
scope.exclusions: Other keys, cipher alphabet permutations, literal/removed F, other interruption runes, word resets, additional layers, noninitial starts and unknown plaintext openings. No historical exact-method replay is claimed.

artifact-stream-skip-grid.title: Puzzle numbers and sequences as keys
artifact-stream-skip-grid.question: Can numbers from the puzzle act as keys when key values may be skipped?
artifact-stream-skip-grid.finding: None of the 194 full-page results passed the source’s English-score test. The search used 21 fixed keys; most settings stopped after the first 50 runes.
artifact-stream-skip-grid.limitations: Only these fixed keys and this conditional-skip rule were tested. The score can accept incorrect text, and most settings received only a 50-rune check.

scope.representation: 55 exact source GP29 page arrays, LP2-00–49 and LP2-51–55; canonical GP Latin labels scored with the pinned source English quadgrams.
scope.procedure: Execute the source numeric2 Part A catalog and unmodified conditional-skip beam in a recording wrapper; all 50-rune screens, then only strict survivors receive full-page decoding. Independently reconstruct every returned full survivor and ten best screens. Separately frozen post-target audit normalizes every retained terminal hypothesis and independently validates its best witness.
scope.parameters: 21 labelled artifact/mathematical streams at exact length1172 x 55 pages x signs -1/+1 x Atbash off/on x offsets0-4 =23,100 screens. Screen50/beam60/strict>-6.5; survivor full beam300/strict>-5.5; max3 conditional key skips.
scope.exclusions: Source numeric2 Parts B/C, the baseline33 numeric streams, other offsets/clocks/languages and joined pages; no full decoding of rejected screens, intermediate normalized-score beam ranking, global-null calibration, general key-family exclusion or proof of plaintext.

autokey-skip-family.title: Autokey with skipped key positions
autokey-skip-family.question: Can recovered or encrypted runes continue a key when positions may be skipped?
autokey-skip-family.finding: None of the 9,900 full-page outputs passed the English-score gate. But 247 of 360 known-message tests used different rules in the source encoder and decoder, so this does not rule out autokey.
autokey-skip-family.limitations: All 113 valid known-message cases recovered exactly. Scores also accepted wrong text. Only these starting keys and source rules were tested; discarded beam paths and other autokey mechanisms remain outside the result.

scope.representation: Pinned GP29 indices,55 source segments/12,956 runes; page-local forward order. P key is primer plus that hypothesis recovered plaintext; C key is primer plus complete observed ciphertext, padded with zeros as source. Exact transcription remains external.
scope.procedure: Execute run_full_new.run_autokey semantics with unchanged P/C decoder rules. Stable cumulative-score beam returns first winner; gate its source normalized English score. Separately find first normalized maximum among retained terminal hypotheses, without changing the returned source output. Preserve all cases and control failures.
scope.parameters: 29 singleton indices plus 16 literal source words =45 distinct primers; P/C models x signs -1/+1 x 55 segments =9,900 full calls. Beam 450/max_skip 3/strict score > -5.5; no target short screen or Atbash. P frontier total skips <= primer length-1, so 3,190 singleton-P labels are rigid. Source encoder controls suppression 0.83,360 fixed seeded cases/two known readings; all outcomes retained.
scope.exclusions: Other primers/offsets/alphabets, resets inside pages, joined pages, other languages, altered encoder/frontier rules or ranking, paths discarded by the source beam and global-null significance. No general cipher-family exclusion; 247 source-generated known truths are invalid under their matching decoder.

b04-source-seeds-opening-cribs.title: B-04 cryptographic seed streams against fixed LP2 openings
b04-source-seeds-opening-cribs.question: Were the published cryptographic seed streams checked against LP2 openings?
b04-source-seeds-opening-cribs.finding: The longest structurally feasible opening is six runes; zero of 1,385,600 configurations match all 12 runes. This is a new fixed-crib test of source-defined candidates, separate from the source English-score sweep.
b04-source-seeds-opening-cribs.limitations: It assumes one of nine known-reading 12-rune openings begins at one of 55 nonempty page starts. It tests zero key offset, the source B-04 keystream candidates and skip bound; it does not test other plaintexts, word resets, altered transcriptions, new seeds, or a general decryption mechanism.

scope.representation: Current Liberpedia GP29 rune transcription; the first 12 runes of every nonempty LP2-00–55 page, read separately. Nine fixed 12-rune openings from published reading CSVs.
scope.procedure: Regenerate the pinned source seed bytes through 16 source generators and five reductions. For every forward/reverse stream, sign and ciphertext-Atbash setting, exactly test whether any key-skip path can produce a fixed opening; no English score or beam pruning.
scope.parameters: 2,165 seeds × 16 generators × 5 reductions × two directions × two signs × two Atbash states = 1,385,600 configurations; zero offset; at most three rejected draws per emitted rune; all 55 nonempty LP2 page starts; nine fixed 12-rune cribs.
scope.exclusions: No different seeds or hashes, nonzero offsets, independent page keys, word resets, alternative transcriptions, other plaintexts or original source English-scoring claims.

block-boundary-doublets.title: LP2 doublets at proposed block boundaries
block-boundary-doublets.question: Do repeated neighboring runes mark the ends of fixed-size blocks?
block-boundary-doublets.finding: The 86 adjacent repeats do not gather unusually at the boundaries of five-, seven- or thirteen-rune blocks. Searching 434 combinations of block size and starting offset also found no stronger pattern than the shuffled comparisons commonly produced.
block-boundary-doublets.limitations: Counting restarts on each page, with one offset shared across pages. Different offsets for individual pages or interruptions in the count were not tested.

scope.representation: Archived LP2-00–55 transcription, filtered to 29 alphabet runes separately within each page.
scope.procedure: Mark adjacent equal-rune edges; count phase-zero hits for block sizes 5, 7 and 13; search every size 2–29 and shared phase; compare the maximum standardized excess with 3,000 per-page fixed-event-count randomizations.
scope.parameters: 86 event edges among 12,901 edges; page-start clock; 434 size/phase configurations; 3,000 seeded controls.
scope.exclusions: Page-specific unknown phases, variable block sizes, interruptions, changed transcription, low total doublet count, and a complete block-cipher decoder.

block-lookahead-feedback.title: Block-start lookahead feedback: zero-key completion
block-lookahead-feedback.question: Does feedback from the next block reveal a known opening?
block-lookahead-feedback.finding: With the unspecified key set to zero, neither five- nor seven-rune blocks produced any of the 15 known beginnings on 55 LP2 pages. The rule did recover all 15 planted reading controls, confirming that the tested decoder reverses its own encryption.
block-lookahead-feedback.limitations: The key and out-of-page lookahead value were both fixed to zero because the proposal left them unspecified. Other keys, block alignments and plaintext beginnings remain untested.

scope.representation: Zero-based GP-29 indices from archived LP2-00–55 rune text; 15 decoded LP1 pages as planted round-trip controls.
scope.procedure: For b in {5,7}, encode and exactly recover each known LP1 reading. Decode LP2 pages under the fixed future-plaintext block-start equation; save full-page digests, IoC, F count and 12-rune known-opening comparisons.
scope.parameters: k[i]=0; b=5 or 7; page-local phase zero; terminal future plaintext=0; modulo 29; 55 nonempty LP2 targets times 15 fixed known openings per case.
scope.exclusions: Unspecified original key k[i], phrase prelayer, other block sizes or phases, inter-page state, interrupts, alternate alphabet, and unfixed plaintext targets.

c2-extension-generator-controls.title: Does a matching decoder recover the planted message?
c2-extension-generator-controls.question: Can a decoding tool miss the right message even with the right key?
c2-extension-generator-controls.finding: With the right key supplied, a decoder that matches the planted rule recovered 98–100% of runes at the median; the comparison decoder recovered 10–33%.
c2-extension-generator-controls.limitations: This checks a decoding tool on planted messages. It does not search manuscript keys, test nonzero offsets, or establish native generator runtime parity.

scope.representation: Source-derived English GP29 plaintext, correct generator streams, planted ciphertext and decoded rune paths; no manuscript candidate.
scope.procedure: Regenerate all 56 exact source fixtures, run unchanged matching/baseline source beams, compare every archived score and recovery, independently count rune matches and rescore all paths.
scope.parameters: Eight generator-and-plant pairs × seven seeds 3301–3307 × two decoders; 240 runes; width 400; sign -1; offset 0; suppression .83; paired skips or q=.05 / ten fixed drifts; median recovery gate .90.
scope.exclusions: Manuscript sweep, wrong-key calibration, native runtime parity, nonzero-offset recovery, other lengths or languages and general cipher exclusion.

cc-roman-matrix-replay.title: LP2-15–22: digit spirals and Roman/HALFMAN selector
cc-roman-matrix-replay.question: Do the reported digit-grid contacts and seven-number Roman/HALFMAN result reproduce from archived rune text, and what happens under nearby orientation and window choices?
cc-roman-matrix-replay.finding: LP2-15 body has 150 runes and 289 GP digits; LP2-16–22 has 1,744 runes and 3,481 GP digits. Under the specified registration, alternating rune-boundary contacts match 12/16 and 16/16. Transposed labels 5–11 give LXLLLXV, rearranged as LLLLXXV by direct HALFMAN ranking; symbol values sum to 225. Exactly 2/80 local orientation-window trials also meet sum 225 and descending order, but both contain the identical seven panel values.
cc-roman-matrix-replay.limitations: The representation, source grouping, proposed words, Roman extraction and coordinate map were chosen during exploration. Contacts sharing a rune are dependent. The 80 nearby choices are not the full search space and cannot be read as a p-value. Matching arithmetic does not identify a cipher or decrypt any text.

scope.representation: Archived LP2-15 body runes with nine-rune header excluded, plus all LP2-16–22 runes; each GP prime expanded to ordinary decimal digits. The printed LP2-15 number panel is an independent fixed input for the Roman selector.
scope.procedure: Build center-out right–down–left–up 17² and 59² digit spirals; register the printed 4×4 labels through 1→2, 2→3, 3→N−1, 4→N; check odd-label starts and even-label ends. Transpose the printed panel, take labels 5–11, convert final two digits to Roman numeral first symbols and apply direct HALFMAN ranking. Enumerate eight symmetries and ten consecutive seven-label windows as nearby controls.
scope.parameters: 17×17 and 59×59 streams; sixteen contacts per grid; direct rank order 4,1,5,3,6,2,7; Roman symbols I,V,X,L; target symbol-value sum 225 and descending values. The 80-case scan does not include other word readings, numeric extractions, registrations or permutations.
scope.exclusions: No independent derivation of the five candidate plaintext words; no cipher execution, held-out plaintext, calibrated chance probability or claim that the supplied grids are authorial instructions.

cc-section-representation-census.title: Numerical matrix lengths across LP2 sections
cc-section-representation-census.question: Do the proposed numerical matrices fit the manuscript's section lengths?
cc-section-representation-census.finding: Several proposed grid areas reproduce exactly, but they switch between whole runes, GP-prime digits and zero- or one-based index digits. Across 820 contiguous LP2-00–39 intervals, square lengths occur 11, 8, 3 and 4 times respectively in those four representations. The LP2-15 17×17 case requires excluding its header; the proposed 54×54 and 15×67 cases require additional, unverified selections.
cc-section-representation-census.limitations: Counts are from one archived transcription. They do not identify grid routes, prove that page groups or representations were selected in advance, verify ink colors, yield plaintext, or supply a chance probability. The 820 intervals overlap and omit partial-page, reordered and alternative-encoding searches.

scope.representation: Archived GP rune transcription on LP2-00–39, including headings and excluding non-rune marks; each rune optionally expanded to decimal GP prime or zero-/one-based position digits.
scope.procedure: Verify the existing source count audit; compute all four lengths for eleven supplied groups and all 820 contiguous page intervals; identify square lengths and exact recurrence of the selected target lengths; independently compare page-JSON raw rune streams with text files.
scope.parameters: 40 LP2 pages; four representations; 820 page intervals per representation; page-15 body is a declared separate partial-page exception. No matrix paths or plaintext scores.
scope.exclusions: No image color classification, inserted printed number as a rune, partial-page search beyond LP2-15 body, rearranged page order, grid traversal, decryption or inferential null model.

compass-shared-radii.title: LP2-33 and LP2-39: shared three-circle radii at native scale
compass-shared-radii.question: Can the same three compass radii locate a point on both LP2-33 and LP2-39?
compass-shared-radii.finding: No, under this construction. Circles centered on the three horizontal dots cannot all meet at a point inside each page when the same radius is assigned to the corresponding dot on both pages.
compass-shared-radii.limitations: This uses the original image scale and keeps the dots in left-to-right order. Rescaling, swapping radii, points outside the pages and other compass constructions were not tested.

scope.representation: Original 2400x3600 JPEGs; four-connected grayscale components; exact pixel-centroid fractions.
scope.procedure: Measure three ordered horizontal dots per page at three thresholds; derive exact residual corner bounds and compare with the lower bound imposed by shared radii.
scope.parameters: Thresholds 100,140,180; explicit crop boxes; area>200; 0.7<width/height<1.3; fill>0.6. Targets inside [0,2399]x[0,3599]. Same radii at A,B,C across pages.
scope.exclusions: Rescaling; page-dependent radii; reassigned radius order; outside-page targets; different dots; pairwise intersections; compass stepping; rune selection and plaintext.

corpus-prefix-census.title: Word lengths across the complete historical reference corpus
corpus-prefix-census.question: Where does the reconstructed 2902-token manuscript summary fall among every eligible prefix in the pinned historical corpus?
corpus-prefix-census.finding: The census and all 46 comparison rows are independently reproduced. Of 25565 eligible paths, 138 have a smaller length-two proportion than the manuscript and one ties it; all other measures and both weights are retained.
corpus-prefix-census.limitations: A fixed nonrandom collection of prefixes with undocumented conversion and edition provenance. Corpus code points and manuscript runes plus digits are different units. Descriptive ranks do not identify language or cipher. Human review pending.

scope.representation: Reconstructed manuscript rune tokens plus six isolated digits; corpus Unicode-code-point lengths under strict UTF-8 and literal-space tokenization.
scope.procedure: Audit every pinned files/ path and its first 2902 nonempty tokens when eligible; calculate all 23 exact descriptive ranks under path and distinct-blob weighting; independently check source bytes and ranks.
scope.parameters: 25906 paths; 25844 distinct source blobs; 25565 eligible paths and 25563 eligible blobs; 2902 tokens per prefix; bins 1..14 and 15+; n-1 variance and linear quartiles.
scope.exclusions: No language identification, random passage sampling, header removal, alphabet filtering, edition deduplication, calibrated p-values or reproduction of the unavailable corpus converter.

crib-difference-stream-search.title: LP2-39: do crib-difference triplets recur elsewhere?
crib-difference-stream-search.question: Can differences from a guessed header word point to a key elsewhere in Liber Primus?
crib-difference-stream-search.finding: Subtracting 17 candidate header readings produced nine matching three-rune sequences elsewhere in the manuscript. That was not unusual: 1,499 of 2,000 shuffled comparisons had at least as many matches. These short matches establish neither a key nor a reading.
crib-difference-stream-search.limitations: Only LP2-39’s three-rune header, a fixed candidate list and forward adjacent matches were tested. Longer guesses, reversed or gapped searches and actual decryption remain untested.

scope.representation: Zero-based indices of the stored 29-rune GP alphabet; all other LP1 and LP2 rune-text pages as source streams.
scope.procedure: Generate every length-three exact GP segmentation of the 20 fixed header-crib words; subtract plaintext indices from the LP2-39 red prefix modulo 29; search exact forward adjacent triplets elsewhere and repeat on 2,000 within-page shuffles.
scope.parameters: 17 eligible triplets; 71 source pages; punctuation removed; page boundaries retained; seed 330139; inclusive plus-one Monte Carlo tails.
scope.exclusions: Other cribs, prime-value differences, reverse or gapped searches, source text outside LP, key-layer decipherment and withheld-text prediction.

crib-inferred-feedback-table.title: What a crib fixes in a feedback table
crib-inferred-feedback-table.question: Does a short feedback-table fit actually constrain the key?
crib-inferred-feedback-table.finding: Ciphertext feedback gives 31 consistent page-opening pairs out of 495, each with 18 or 19 free entries. Plaintext feedback gives one consistent pair out of 495, with 20 free entries. The consistent cases determine at most five of the next twelve ciphertext-feedback positions or one sequential plaintext-feedback position; none is a validated reading.
crib-inferred-feedback-table.limitations: A compatible partial table is not evidence of a true decryption. The first rune needs an external primer, future plaintext is unknown, and only the fixed page starts, proposed openings and two feedback states are covered.

scope.representation: First 24 recognized GP29 runes including headings from each of 55 rune-bearing LP2-00–55 pages.
scope.procedure: For each fixed 12-rune opening, infer f(previous ciphertext) or f(previous plaintext) from C_i−P_i modulo29 at i=1..11. Reject conflicting assignments, count 29^(29−r) full extensions for r assigned inputs, and measure coverage on the next twelve ciphertext positions without a truth label.
scope.parameters: 2 feedback modes × 55 page starts × 9 fixed openings = 990 partial-table inferences; 11 constraints per proposed opening; 29 possible input slots.
scope.exclusions: First-rune primer inference, unknown plaintext and continuations, language scoring, alternate alphabet orders, later positions, changing tables, and other cipher layers.

cross-section-index-inversion.title: LP2-00–02: audit the 729 ÷ rune-index proposal
cross-section-index-inversion.question: Does the posted 729 divided by GP-index rule reproduce its worked first word and specify a complete output on the 729-rune section?
cross-section-index-inversion.finding: All three pages contain 729 runes, but the claimed first-word index for prime 107 is 28 rather than its canonical zero-based 27. Literal arithmetic with the archived rune gives Y rather than the report's AE at that position. The 34 F runes have index zero and no quotient. Without wrapping, 335 of 695 non-F outputs fall outside the alphabet under global line counting; global and page-reset wrapped outputs differ at 396 of 695 positions.
cross-section-index-inversion.limitations: The supplied post names no complete F handling, wrap rule, global-versus-page line clock or deterministic selection from its neighboring letters. Its excerpted image is unavailable; this audit identifies the post by hash and uses the archived transcription. The chosen full-stream conventions are declared extensions and do not recreate all manual postprocessing in the discussion. Human review pending.

scope.representation: Every archived rune of LP2-00–02 in printed line order, GP prime values and zero-based 29-rune indices. The source's eight first-word indices are fixed in the plan, including its 28 for prime 107.
scope.procedure: Verify the 729-rune count, then for every nonzero index j calculate floor(729/j), remainder, base index modulo 29, and the posted fractional threshold with both global and page-reset line counts. Keep both raw and wrapped candidate indices; mark zero-index F undefined. Compare the first eight source indices and labels with the claimed worked example.
scope.parameters: Three pages, 33 source rune rows, exact rational fractional comparisons, line numbering from one, no word rearrangement or removal. Modulo-29 wrapping is an explicitly additional convention for comparison, not a source claim.
scope.exclusions: A fixed rule for F; chosen neighboring letters; letter rearrangement or dummy-word removal; image-level review of every rune; a full plaintext or a statistical language claim; other 729-based constructions.

cross-source-word-boundaries.title: Two LP2 transcriptions: word-boundary sensitivity
cross-source-word-boundaries.question: Do any of the 33 non-rune differences between preserved seventh-onion and wiki texts on LP2-00–55 change the published joined-page rune-token positions or lengths?
cross-source-word-boundaries.finding: All 33 one-gap substitutions and the complete alternate transcription preserve every one of the 2,896 token-start positions, the full length histogram, the 109 tokens of length ten or more, and the single 11–11–10 window. The ordered 12,956-rune stream is identical.
cross-source-word-boundaries.limitations: This is exact agreement under one parser, not an image audit or a test of all boundary-sensitive ciphers. Different punctuation and number-grid content can matter when a method explicitly uses those marks. The two sources share historical transcription lineage rather than providing independent photographic verification.

scope.representation: Preserved combined seventh-onion LP2-00–55 rune text, 56 wiki page text files, and the stored 29-rune alphabet. Ordered rune streams are identical; non-rune gaps may differ.
scope.procedure: Split combined text at its 55 percent-mark page separators. Remove slash/CR/LF wraps, concatenate pages, and apply the published rune-token parser with optional internal apostrophes. Compare complete source versus wiki and swap each of 33 differing gaps into the wiki text individually. Compare exact token-start rune ordinals and length metrics.
scope.parameters: 56 pages in numeric order; headings retained; 33 one-gap variants; rune-token starts zero-based; no image-driven correction or tuned punctuation rule.
scope.exclusions: LP2-56–57 and their three additional gap differences; punctuation-sensitive key resets, printed-number consumption, alphanumeric-grid bytes, visual adjudication, and any claim that the two texts are interchangeable for all methods.

cumulative-autokey-literal.title: Literal cumulative-sum autokey on LP2
cumulative-autokey-literal.question: Does the supplied cumulative plaintext-sum rule yield a plaintext-like rune stream across LP2?
cumulative-autokey-literal.finding: Reversing the specified cumulative-sum rule did not establish a readable message. The transformed text still had much flatter rune frequencies than the established LP1 readings.
cumulative-autokey-literal.limitations: This was a frequency comparison, not a complete decryption test. Extra keys, skipped runes, other alphabets and plaintext languages were not tested.

scope.representation: Inverse differences on LP2-00–55, page-local starts, and 2,797 known LP1 reading runes.
scope.procedure: Apply the stated cumulative formula, verify each reconstructed prefix, and compare 29-bin profiles with raw LP2 and solved LP1.
scope.parameters: No fitted parameters; 55 nonempty pages, 12,956 runes; first rune retained per page.
scope.exclusions: Across-page state, alternate rune mappings, skips, key layers and manuscript-reading claims.

cypherpunk-manifesto-running-key.title: Cypherpunk Manifesto as an LP2 running key
cypherpunk-manifesto-running-key.question: Does any contiguous offset of Eric Hughes's manifesto, converted by either of two fixed key mappings and subtracted modulo 29, produce a convincing complete LP2 page?
cypherpunk-manifesto-running-key.finding: The manifesto did not stand out from shuffled keys on the three tested pages. Every best-score result was matched or beaten by several shuffled-key searches.
cypherpunk-manifesto-running-key.limitations: Only LP2-00, 31 and 54 were tested, at every fitting offset under two fixed mappings and uninterrupted subtraction. English scoring and the preserved source edition limit the result.

scope.representation: Pinned 1993 manifesto page fetched 2026-10-23; 4,072 normalized ASCII letters from the essay body. Separate A=0..25 and greedy GP-rune key sequences; canonical 29-index ciphertext and Latin labels.
scope.procedure: At every no-wrap contiguous offset that covers the complete target page, subtract one key unit per rune modulo 29. Rank full-page English quadgram scores. Repeat the entire offset search on sixteen seeded value-shuffled keys per mapping/page. Plant an LP1-04 known reading with each mapping at offset 3301 and require rank one before LP2 scoring.
scope.parameters: Two named source mappings; LP2-00 (262 runes), LP2-31 (269), LP2-54 (232); 3,804–3,841 A–Z offsets and 3,625–3,662 GP offsets per page; 16 complete shuffled-key searches for every mapping/page; one fixed subtraction direction and scorer.
scope.exclusions: Other source editions or passages, preserving source word boundaries during GP parsing, reverse arithmetic, skip/feedback clocks, wraps, other LP2 pages, arbitrary internal starts, non-English scoring and any general rejection of running keys.

d04-remaining-page-feedback.title: Can earlier ciphertext runes supply the key?
d04-remaining-page-feedback.question: Do weighted earlier runes turn the remaining pages into English?
d04-remaining-page-feedback.finding: None of the tested rules produced a supported English reading on the remaining 52 pages. The strongest output, on LP2-49, scored like results commonly found in shuffled pages. Known-message tests recovered every rune.
d04-remaining-page-feedback.limitations: Only the named coefficient grid, constant seeds 0/1, two signs and English scorer; no general feedback-cipher exclusion.

scope.representation: Exact source GP29 ciphertext on the remaining 52 nonempty LP2-00–55 pages, excluding baseline LP2-00/05/20. Full-page canonical GP Latin-label outputs.
scope.procedure: Evaluate the exact 5,072 source coefficient vectors with constant seeds 0/1, both signs and offset 0. Exploit identical plaintext across constant-seed beam paths after native-source parity; score with original source quadgram table. Add full-grid known-reading and 32 complete shuffled-grid controls.
scope.parameters: 52 pages × 5,072 vectors × 2 constants × 2 signs = 1,054,976 settings. Source initial-k feedback zeros, beam250/maxskip3-equivalent constant domain. Source signal line -5.2. Null seed330120261028, 32 trials.
scope.exclusions: Baseline three pages; arbitrary third-tap coefficients, other seed values, varying reference keys, nonzero offsets, plaintext-history feedback, other languages and general cipher-family exclusion.

d4v1-column-unigram-key-recovery.title: A column solver with a short-key limit
d4v1-column-unigram-key-recovery.question: Has a program tried to infer a short repeating key from rune frequencies?
d4v1-column-unigram-key-recovery.finding: This short-key solver produced no English-like LP2 output. It recovered the planted passage in 107 of 165 page-and-key-length settings; the other 58 did not recover it. Shuffled searches often scored higher than the best manuscript result.
d4v1-column-unigram-key-recovery.limitations: The test uses key lengths 2, 3 and 5, one planted passage, and the source’s exact rule for removing possible interrupters. It does not rule out repeating-key ciphers or longer keys.

scope.representation: Archived GP29 rune order including headings; source pages17–72 aligned to site LP2-00–55, with LP2-50 excluded because its pinned transcription has no runes.
scope.procedure: For each page and fixed KL2,3,5, remove source-listed possible-interrupter positions for column inference only; select each of29 shifts by source solved-page unigram target; apply the inferred key to the original page, then apply the separately pinned English quadgram score. Plant exact known texts and repeat the full 165-setting search on199 pagewise shuffled controls.
scope.parameters: 3 fixed periods ×55 rune-bearing pages =165 outputs; 9 complete-reading plants, 165 page-length plants, 199 full-search shuffle replicates, English line −5.5.
scope.exclusions: No other fixed periods, KL0 target verdict, source alternate patched/rune/Latin key transforms, modified interrupter list, other languages or key layers.

d4v1-missing-prime-anchor-gate.title: Missing-prime keys and routes: checking the score
d4v1-missing-prime-anchor-gate.question: Can the missing-prime and grid-key score distinguish a reading from shuffled text?
d4v1-missing-prime-anchor-gate.finding: The source’s score accepted all 199 shuffled controls for each key. Rearranging the runes cannot change this score, so it cannot select a route. A high score here does not establish a readable message.
d4v1-missing-prime-anchor-gate.limitations: This checks the scoring rule on one known passage. It does not test the keys on unsolved pages or rule out the proposed keys and routes.

scope.representation: Pinned source secrets.cpp 256-pair stream and 180 missing primes; one 157-rune known direct reading from source Page 5. Synthetic three-word anchor and 199 shuffled conditional score controls; no unsolved LP2 target search.
scope.procedure: Verify source constants and five grid case differences; test three-word trigger, invert two key streams and six source route positions on a known reading; scan all 29 source Atbash shifts on 199 seeded shuffles for each key and use unigram invariance for routes.
scope.parameters: Missing-prime sums 73,79,83; keys of lengths 256 and 180; source strict score thresholds >0.91 (keys) and >0.90 (routes); route widths 3 and 7; 199 deterministic controls seeded 3301..3499.
scope.exclusions: No claim that an unsolved page contains an anchor, that either key/route decodes LP2, that other passages have the same control behavior, or that source letter-case ambiguities are resolved.

d4v1-positional-totient-streams.title: Positional totient shifts on complete LP2 pages
d4v1-positional-totient-streams.question: Has a totient shift based on each rune’s position been checked?
d4v1-positional-totient-streams.finding: None of the 100 position-based totient shifts produced English-like text on any of the 55 tested pages. The strongest result was no better than many shuffled searches. All nine deliberately encrypted controls were decoded correctly.
d4v1-positional-totient-streams.limitations: This checks one positional rule and offsets 0–99, using an English scorer. It does not rule out other totient rules or the separate word-sum proposal.

scope.representation: Archived GP29 rune order including headings, page-local rune clock; LP2-50 excluded because pinned transcription has no runes.
scope.procedure: Apply P_i=(C_i−φ(i+offset)) mod29 for offsets 0–99 to each full page, score canonical GP Latin output with a pinned English quadgram model, calibrate with nine readings and offset-17 planted encryptions, and compare the global best with 199 full-search pagewise shuffles.
scope.parameters: 100 offsets × 55 pages = 5,500 outputs; −5.5 English line; nine solved readings; 199 full-search shuffled trials.
scope.exclusions: No current-word prime-sum totient branch, offsets outside 0–99, other signs or resets, other languages, key layers or general totient mechanism.

dead-tree-alignment.title: LP2-55 tree: reflected photograph alignment
dead-tree-alignment.question: Under one frozen crop, grayscale response and scale/translation search, does the horizontally reflected Commons tree photograph fit LP2-55 better than its original orientation?
dead-tree-alignment.finding: Under the declared search, reflection improves whole-region correlation from 0.377 to 0.623; fitting upper branches yields lower-region correlations 0.456 reflected versus −0.095 original.
dead-tree-alignment.limitations: Image, crop and response parameters were chosen after visual inspection. The lower-region check is within the same selected images and is not a blind independent holdout. It does not establish the author’s exact compositing steps or the probability of a coincidental match among other photographs.

scope.representation: Original 1894x2606 Commons JPEG and archived 2400x3600 LP2-55 JPEG; declared grayscale crop responses.
scope.procedure: Search 23 scales and all in-crop integer translations for two orientations. Compare full-region normalized correlation, then fit the upper 60% and score the lower 40% at that same transform.
scope.parameters: Source crop [100,500,1750,1950]; manuscript crop [550,1300,1850,2550]; clipped darkness levels 170/130 and 250/45; Gaussian sigma 7; scales 0.370–0.700 step 0.015; no rotation or shear.
scope.exclusions: Other source photographs, other crops, rotations, warps, tonal recipes, LP2-32, the 2016 message, any rune/decryption operation, and a chance probability over candidate images.

dead-tree-cross-carrier.title: Shared tree across LP2-32 and the 2016 message
dead-tree-cross-carrier.question: Do the LP2-32 and 2016 tree renderings align with the already identified tree source under bounded scale, translation and orientation comparisons?
dead-tree-cross-carrier.finding: LP2-55→LP2-32 whole-region correlation is 0.623 same orientation versus 0.483 reflected; lower-region checks after upper fits are 0.600 versus 0.353. Commons→2016 whole-region correlation is 0.854 reflected versus 0.566 original; lower-region checks are 0.858 versus 0.442.
dead-tree-cross-carrier.limitations: The sources, crops, contrast mappings and scale ranges were chosen after viewing the images. Lower-region checks are within the same selected carriers, not blind holdouts. Correlations are descriptive and do not recover the compositing process or probability against unrelated trees.

scope.representation: Original LP2-32 and LP2-55 JPEGs; original Commons DeadTree.jpg and archived 2016 message JPEG; two declared grayscale-response comparisons.
scope.procedure: For each source-target pair, search specified scales and every in-crop integer translation in two orientations; maximize normalized correlation over the full crop or upper 60%, then score the lower 40% without refitting.
scope.parameters: LP2-55→LP2-32 crops [600,1450,1800,2500] and [550,2000,1850,3500], darkness levels 250/45 and 230/160, sigma 15, 24 scales 0.650–1.225. Commons→2016 crops [100,500,1750,1950] and [145,270,425,475], source darkness 170/130, message lightness 2/28 with pixels >100 masked, sigma 1.5, 26 scales 0.065–0.140.
scope.exclusions: Other source photographs and processing choices; rotation, shear, warps, exact authoring recipe; any cipher, rune or decryption operation; a calibrated chance probability.

decimal-chain-opening-cribs.title: Five-digit chain-addition keys
decimal-chain-opening-cribs.question: Could a five-digit chain-addition key reveal a known opening?
decimal-chain-opening-cribs.finding: Zero of 99,000,000 exact 12-rune comparisons match; the longest shared prefix is five. Two planted recovery controls and an independent complete-prefix census pass.
decimal-chain-opening-cribs.limitations: This is the decimal chain stream alone, not full GROMARK. It tests only page starts, nine fixed readings, both signs and canonical GP29 arithmetic; unknown openings and other cipher layers remain.

scope.representation: First 12 recognized GP29 runes per LP2-00–55 page, including headings; LP2-50 is runeless. Non-runes do not advance the key.
scope.procedure: Enumerate five-digit decimal primers 00000..99999. Extend each by d_i=(d_(i-5)+d_(i-4)) mod10, decode with C_i plus or minus digit modulo29, and compare nine predeclared 12-rune openings at each page start.
scope.parameters: 100,000 primers × two signs × 55 rune-bearing pages × nine openings = 99,000,000 logical exact comparisons; complete prefix histogram; zero key offset; page-local reset.
scope.exclusions: Full ACA GROMARK mixed alphabet/keyword/check digit, nondecimal or 29^5 rune primers, later positions, unknown readings, interruptions and language scoring.

decoder-skip-controls.title: Can a correct key fail under the wrong alignment rule?
decoder-skip-controls.question: How do rigid and skip-aware decoders recover known rune sequences under four declared encoder mechanisms?
decoder-skip-controls.finding: Correct-key ordinary addition recovers exactly throughout. Skip limits exclude some true alignments; a wider beam cannot repair them. Rewriting often passes the language threshold without exact rune recovery. All wrong-key controls fail exact recovery and the threshold.
decoder-skip-controls.limitations: Artificial encoders and dependent known-text controls, not a fitted manuscript model. Exact alignment and exact plaintext are distinct. Cumulative and normalized scores have different objectives. Human review pending.

scope.representation: First min(240, available) output rune indices from all nine known-reading traces; canonical GP labels only for scoring.
scope.procedure: Plant ordinary addition, probabilistic collision skipping, value rewriting and one unrelated advance plus skipping; decode with correct/wrong deterministic key fixtures using rigid subtraction and four bounded beams.
scope.parameters: Nine traces, three seeds, key-value repetitions 1 and 4, 10000 slots; beam widths 16/64 crossed with skip limits 1/3; cumulative quadgram selection, normalized acceptance -5.5; 216 plants and 2160 decoder results.
scope.exclusions: No manuscript cipher identification, general recovery guarantee, language identification, uniform-pad assumption, key search or calibrated false-positive probability.

direct-hill-key-feasibility.title: Direct Hill keys at LP2 page starts
direct-hill-key-feasibility.question: Could a single Hill-cipher key turn a page opening into a known passage?
direct-hill-key-feasibility.finding: No key works for any of the 55 tested page starts and nine known twelve-rune openings, using blocks of two or three runes. The check covers every invertible key under that fixed rule.
direct-hill-key-feasibility.limitations: Blocks start at the first rune and use the usual 29-rune indices. Other openings, starting positions, added offsets and keys that change between blocks remain untested.

scope.representation: First twelve recognized GP29 runes, including headings, from each of 55 rune-bearing LP2-00–55 pages.
scope.procedure: Split into consecutive 2- or 3-rune column blocks; test whether one invertible matrix maps all ciphertext blocks to one of nine fixed opening vectors. Verify dependencies and equal span rank; count rank-deficient invertible extensions.
scope.parameters: 2 block dimensions × 55 page starts × 9 openings = 990 complete-key feasibility cases over F29.
scope.exclusions: Unknown readings, later positions, shifted or reversed block origins, affine offsets, padding, transposition, nonlinear schedules and magic-square interpretations.

direct-polynomial-streams.title: LP2-00–55: direct polynomial streams, degree at most eight
direct-polynomial-streams.question: Could a low-degree polynomial directly produce a page’s rune values?
direct-polynomial-streams.finding: No polynomial with integer coefficients and degree at most eight can directly generate any of the 55 tested pages under the fixed-step rule, even allowing any fixed integer modulus greater than one. Both rune indices and GP prime values fail the required check.
direct-polynomial-streams.limitations: This tests the polynomial as the entire output, not as a key mixed with plaintext. Higher degrees, skipped positions, resets and extra symbol mappings remain untested.

scope.representation: Archived alphabet runes only, headings retained, each page separate; zero-based indices and literal GP prime values.
scope.procedure: Compute forward differences of orders 2–9 and their integer gcd for each nonempty page and representation; independently verify using binomial sums from page JSON.
scope.parameters: 56 page files; 55 nonempty streams; two representations; eight degree bounds; arbitrary integer origin and fixed signed stride; all integer moduli m>1 by divisibility argument.
scope.exclusions: Unknown plaintext or keystream mixing, degree above eight, extra output maps, skipped clock positions, internal resets, alternative transcriptions and LP2-56–57.

dju-bei-cross-page.title: DJU-BEI on LP2-27 and LP2-55
dju-bei-cross-page.question: Does the reported six-rune DJU-BEI sequence occur at the stated rune offsets on LP2-27 and LP2-55?
dju-bei-cross-page.finding: LP2-27 has exactly one occurrence at zero-based rune offset 28 (line 2, columns 11–17); LP2-55 has exactly one at offset 70 (line 4, columns 4–10). Both source slices are ᛞᛄᚢ-ᛒᛖᛁ.
dju-bei-cross-page.limitations: The two target pages and sequence were supplied after the pattern was noticed. This is a transcription-bound location check, not a prospectively selected statistical test or a demonstration of a decoding mechanism.

scope.representation: The archived raw rune transcription on each of the two specified pages. The stream keeps only the 29 Gematria Primus runes, including headings, and resets the offset at each page.
scope.procedure: Scan all six-rune windows on each specified page for the exact rune sequence ᛞᛄᚢᛒᛖᛁ; record zero- and one-based positions and the original source slice including separators.
scope.parameters: One fixed six-rune target; no matching across a page boundary; punctuation and line breaks excluded from the offset.
scope.exclusions: Other manuscript pages, image-level transcription adjudication, plaintext or cipher inference, significance testing and a causal relation to doublet suppression.

dot-constellation-candidate-fit.title: Five-star catalogue patterns against the five dots
dot-constellation-candidate-fit.question: Do fixed five-star patterns match the five dots?
dot-constellation-candidate-fit.finding: Volans fits most closely among the 88 fixed five-entry patterns, but still misses the measured dot centres with a typical mismatch of about 35 pixels (RMS). The specified Orion, Aquila and Bootes patterns fit less closely.
dot-constellation-candidate-fit.limitations: This compares one fixed five-brightest-entry rule and projection. It does not identify a constellation, test every asterism or explain a cipher; the other two page appearances repeat the same artwork.

scope.representation: Existing threshold-140 five-dot centroids in original-image pixels, and fixed J2000 gnomonic projections of the five brightest eligible HR entries in each of 88 constellations. Distinct close components retained and flagged.
scope.procedure: After the reviewed synthetic gate and frozen execution-code hashes, fit every correspondence and both orientation branches by exact 2D similarity. Treat LP2-07 as primary, other appearances as dependent robustness. Repeat the whole search for two fixed 4095-query geometric reference generators. Independently check every target score/witness with SVD and recount all saved comparisons.
scope.parameters: 88 candidates × 120 bijections × 2 determinant branches = 21120 labelled registrations per query; translation, arbitrary rotation and positive uniform scale; tie tolerance 1e-12. Three target queries; 4095 uniform-disk queries (PCG64 330120261025) and 4095 within-constellation catalogue-set queries (330120261026). Synthetic gate: 96 math fixtures, 88 exact and 1408 noisy plants; no omitted failures.
scope.exclusions: Other star subsets, traditional line maps, merging close components, proper-motion or epoch tuning, alternative projections, anisotropic scale/shear, star omission, new dot measurements, interpreting repeated artwork as independent evidence, confirmatory astronomy probabilities and decryption.

doublet-boundaries.title: LP2-00–55: doublets across words, wraps and stored corrections
doublet-boundaries.question: How many of the 86 filtered within-page equal-rune pairs cross stored separators, and do published LP2 reviewed-text edits change them?
doublet-boundaries.finding: The archived 86 pairs split 60/3/0/22/1 across contiguous, wrap-only, apostrophe/soft-wrap, hyphen and other-separator classes. The seven stored LP2 reviewed layers leave both pair identities and class totals unchanged.
doublet-boundaries.limitations: Only seven LP2 pages have a separate reviewed layer, and those layers all retain the same rune sequence. Results are conditional on archived text and its separator notation; human source-image review pending.

scope.representation: Archived LP2-00–55 text, 29 alphabet runes and seven separately stored LP2 reviewed-text layers.
scope.procedure: Find overlapping within-page equal-rune pairs after filtering; inspect source characters between the rune positions and compare the same pairs after stored corrections.
scope.parameters: Five exclusive separator classes; headings included; no page-edge pairs; slash and CR/LF treated as soft row wraps for within-token counting.
scope.exclusions: Second complete independent transcription, new glyph corrections, manual scan verification, alternate word-separator interpretations and cipher identification.

doublet-collision-edits.title: Collision edits for scarce adjacent doublets
doublet-collision-edits.question: Can the proposed deletion and filler-insertion rules suppress doublets, and do their outputs uniquely determine the original stream?
doublet-collision-edits.finding: All three declared edits suppress repeats mechanically: 86→0 by deletion, 86→8 by fixed F insertion, and 86→0 by a nonmatching filler. The forward outputs can have multiple known-length inputs, so reverse recovery needs additional rules.
doublet-collision-edits.limitations: Applying edits to the already-sparse LP2 ciphertext does not show how the manuscript was encrypted. The nonmatching filler is an explicit control, not a documented historical glyph rule. Toy-alphabet ambiguity is a proof of non-injectivity, not an LP2 candidate count.

scope.representation: Archived rune transcription, filtered to the 29 GP glyphs; pages treated independently.
scope.procedure: Apply three fully specified forward edits to all 56 page streams; count adjacent equality and length; enumerate every length-1–5 string over a three-rune toy alphabet to test inversion even with original length known.
scope.parameters: Collapse each maximal equal run; insert fixed F on each original equal edge; insert the cyclic next GP rune on each original equal edge. Source attachment SHA-256 and all fixed rules in plan.json.
scope.exclusions: No secret edit clock, filler search, original plaintext, reordering rule, before/after key layer or claimed LP2 decryption.

doublet-context.title: Ciphertext symbols and differences around LP2 doublets
doublet-context.question: Do doublet symbols or their neighboring ciphertext differences show extra local ordering beyond the observed zero mask and each page difference inventory?
doublet-context.finding: There are 123 same-symbol event pairs and a before/after imbalance of 27.786; both sit within their declared conditional ranges. The 29 event-symbol counts span 0 to 7, and 85 nonzero differences are available on each side. The hyphen-versus-within-token whole-label score is 51.321; 6,495/10,000 global and 8,626/10,000 page-stratified conditional shuffles reach at least that score.
doublet-context.limitations: Conditioning fixes the 86 zero positions and pagewise difference inventories, so these controls cannot explain the low doublet count or test triple rarity. Boundary-label exchangeability is also only a descriptive benchmark; only 40 events can move in the page-stratified control. Metrics respond to earlier observations and do not supply prospective p-values. The input is archived text, not a new image review.

scope.representation: Archived LP2-00--55 ciphertext rune indices and within-page differences; zero positions and each page nonzero-difference multiset retained.
scope.procedure: Measure doublet-symbol collision pairs and before/after difference imbalance, then shuffle only nonzero differences separately within each page while keeping the observed zero mask and first ciphertext rune. In a companion audit, join boundary categories to event positions and compare complete before/after ciphertext-rune distributions under global and within-page boundary-label shuffles.
scope.parameters: 29-rune modulus; 5,000 difference permutations with seed 330122; 10,000 global and within-page boundary-label permutations with seed 33012217; no cross-page transitions.
scope.exclusions: Plaintext recovery, key inference, probability of the 86-event zero mask, independent full image transcription, English context scoring and post-selection significance.

doublet-event-lags.title: LP2-00–55: distances between doublet events
doublet-event-lags.question: Do the extracted repeat symbols reproduce the claimed number pattern?
doublet-event-lags.finding: Not exactly. Comparing each repeated-rune symbol with the one three events later gives ten +4 shifts in 83 comparisons (12.05%), not the reported 12.9%. The average shortest distance around the 29-rune alphabet for neighboring events is 8.6353, not 8.81.
doublet-event-lags.limitations: This recount follows one fixed event-extraction rule and includes comparisons across pages. The original code is unavailable, and no statistical-significance test was run.

scope.representation: One zero-based GP index per overlapping within-page doublet, headings included; remove non-runes and concatenate events in page order.
scope.procedure: Compare events at lags 1, 2 and 3; record all forward mod-29 differences and minimum circular distances.
scope.parameters: 86 events; 85, 84 and 83 comparisons; cross-page comparisons retained; no end wrap; 29 directed bins per lag.
scope.exclusions: Other transcriptions, collapsed runs, word-only extraction, page-reset comparisons, other lags, permutation tail probabilities and cipher searches.

doublet-event-shuffle.title: Doublet events: global versus within-page shuffle controls
doublet-event-shuffle.question: Do the reported doublet-event distances survive controls that preserve the page-specific event inventory and account for selecting an attractive bin?
doublet-event-shuffle.finding: For the observed lag-one sum 734, 31/20,000 global shuffles and 3,910/20,000 within-page shuffles meet or exceed it. The observed +4 count 10 has 13 and 23 narrow exceedances, but allowing selection of any directed bin at lags 1–3 gives 1,123 and 3,510 exceedances.
doublet-event-shuffle.limitations: The reported statistics and bins were selected after looking at data. These two randomizations are conditional reference models, not models of every plausible encryption process; source p-values cannot be exactly recovered without its inputs and implementation.

scope.representation: One zero-based GP index per overlapping within-page doublet, headings included; remove non-runes and concatenate events in page order.
scope.procedure: Compare three source-specified statistics on the 86-event sequence with 20,000 seeded global shuffles and 20,000 within-page shuffles; also score the largest directed bin and largest three circular bins across lags 1–3.
scope.parameters: Seed 33012026; 20,000 draws per control; one-sided greater-or-equal tails; lags 1–3; 29 directed and 15 circular bins; page event multisets held fixed in the conditioned control.
scope.exclusions: Original unpublished event list and code, other transcriptions, unseen page subsets, all unreported model searches, cipher inference and confirmatory significance claims.

doublet-lag-profile.title: LP2-00–55: equal rune pairs at lags one through five
doublet-lag-profile.question: Does the low count of adjacent equal runes extend to distances two through five under fixed-count page shuffles?
doublet-lag-profile.finding: The observed adjacency deficit is not a comparable deficit at rune lags two through five under this specified page-shuffle reference.
doublet-lag-profile.limitations: Exploratory: lag-one suppression was already known. Fixed-count page shuffles are not a model of English or a specific cipher. The source is an archived transcription; human review pending.

scope.representation: Archived LP2-00–55 29-rune streams, including headings; remove other characters within pages.
scope.procedure: Count equal forward pairs at lags one through five, then independently shuffle each page's fixed rune multiset 2,000 times.
scope.parameters: No page crossing or circular wrap; 2,000 seeded shuffles; exact expected counts and nearest-rank central intervals.
scope.exclusions: Alternative transcriptions, word-internal only pairs, other lags, cipher-key simulations, plaintext inference, corrected multiple-testing claims.

doublet-placement.title: LP2-00–55: placement of the 86 doublets
doublet-placement.question: After fixing the observed total of 86 equal-rune events, do their page counts and positions differ from explicit length-aware placement controls?
doublet-placement.finding: Observed page-count variance and 13 empty pages are ordinary under length-aware fixed-total placement. The shortest gap of six is near the reference edge, but neither placement control models all linguistic or cipher constraints.
doublet-placement.limitations: Both controls condition on a doublet total already seen, choose event slots without modeling rune identities or overlap constraints, and were specified after the event list was known. Human review pending.

scope.representation: Archived LP2-00–55 29-rune streams, headings included, filtering non-runes within pages.
scope.procedure: Extract all within-page equal-neighbor events, measure page counts and positions, then sample event slots under fixed-total and fixed-page-count controls.
scope.parameters: 86 events among 12,901 within-page edge slots; 55 nonempty pages; 10,000 seeded draws per control; first/last five slots and global rune-coordinate gaps.
scope.exclusions: Cipher or plaintext simulation, alternate transcriptions, image verification, word-only event definitions, page-reset gap definitions and confirmatory post-selection probabilities.

doublet-section-residues.title: Do doublets fall at particular section positions?
doublet-section-residues.question: Do repeated neighboring runes favor a position within manuscript sections?
doublet-section-residues.finding: The 86 adjacent repeats do not favor any of the tested repeating positions within the nine manuscript sections. The strongest pattern from cycles of two through eight was matched or exceeded in 4,316 of 5,000 shuffled comparisons.
doublet-section-residues.limitations: Counting starts again at each section, and the comparison keeps each section’s repeat count fixed. It does not explain why repeats are rare or test other boundaries or cipher rules.

scope.representation: All 12,956 rune positions in the nine LP2 unsolved sections; each doublet event is located by the second rune’s zero-based position within its section.
scope.procedure: Recount adjacent equal-rune events, tabulate the second-rune positions modulo 2–8, compute chi-square divided by m−1 against opportunity-weighted expectations, and retain the largest of seven scores. In 5,000 seeded controls, preserve doublet counts per section but sample their eligible positions uniformly; apply the identical seven-way selection. Add a planted mod-seven placement check.
scope.parameters: Nine fixed sections; 86 doublets; moduli 2–8; 5,000 random.Random(3301) controls; one-sided upper tail, ties counted.
scope.exclusions: Sentence-relative residues, alternative section boundaries, doublet identities, runs or clusters of events, other moduli and cipher-specific position laws.

doublet-sentence-residues.title: Do doublets favor positions within sentences?
doublet-sentence-residues.question: Do repeated neighboring runes favor a position within sentences?
doublet-sentence-residues.finding: The 86 adjacent repeats show no unusual pattern when sentence positions are grouped in cycles of two through eight. The strongest pattern was matched or exceeded in 2,068 of 5,000 shuffled comparisons.
doublet-sentence-residues.limitations: The test uses one source’s sentence boundaries and does not model a cipher. Other punctuation rules or position patterns remain untested.

scope.representation: All 12,956 runes of the nine LP2 unsolved sections, with source-derived sentence reset rune ordinals from the pinned relikd text. A doublet event is placed at its second rune.
scope.procedure: Recount all 86 doublets; measure sentence-relative positions modulo 2–8; compare the largest chi-square/df score with the same seven-way maximum in 5,000 placements retaining each section's number of events and the punctuation boundaries. Verify a concentrated planted modulo-seven pattern.
scope.parameters: Nine fixed sections, 86 events, seven moduli, random.Random(3301), 5,000 controls; ties counted in the upper tail.
scope.exclusions: Different punctuation or source text, word-relative and section-relative coordinates, moduli outside 2–8, event identities, cipher-specific nulls and plaintext recovery.

dukotah-b04-full-source-replay.title: Cryptographic seed streams across the unsolved pages
dukotah-b04-full-source-replay.question: Can a short Cicada-related seed generate the manuscript's key?
dukotah-b04-full-source-replay.finding: This search found no English reading using its fixed list of Cicada-related seeds and key generators. A planted message ranked first, while none of 6.22 million short-text decodes passed the same score threshold. The 150 selected settings also failed that threshold on a whole page and the joined manuscript.
dukotah-b04-full-source-replay.limitations: The result covers this seed list, decoder and English scorer. Reversed keys can change when the requested key length changes, so those longer tests do not always continue the same opening key. Other seed constructions and languages remain open.

scope.exclusions: Other seeds, salts, key stretching, generators, boundary resets, text layers, languages, scoring rules and skip models; full held-out detector-power calibration.
scope.parameters: 2,165 A seeds, 504 B/C core seeds, 16 generators, source reduction/sign/Atbash/direction/offset axes, beam width 400, max three skips per rune, fixed score bar −5.5; 6,224,000 opening decodes and 300 D cells.
scope.procedure: Run G1/G2 source controls, full A/B/C seed-generator grids with English quadgram scorer and soft key-skip beam, then replay the source-selected 150 settings on both long targets. Independent checker validates saved merge, hashes and direct source-decoder comparisons.
scope.representation: Pinned GP29 rune indices in source reading order. A/B use first 120 joined unsolved runes; C uses up to 100 runes at each of 55 source page starts; D uses the 262-rune first page and 12,956-rune joined stream.

dukotah-book-matrix-hill.title: Number panels as Hill-cipher keys
dukotah-book-matrix-hill.question: Could the manuscript’s number panels be matrices that decrypt the runes?
dukotah-book-matrix-hill.finding: The selected number matrices, including a correction to one printed cell, produced no candidate passing the English-language check. Each of the 28 matrix operations did recover the complete short known message planted to check it.
dukotah-book-matrix-hill.limitations: Only the specified matrices and starting position were tested, and incomplete blocks at the ends were dropped. Passing or failing the language score does not establish a correct reading or rule out other matrix ciphers.

scope.representation: Source krisyotam GP29 rune indices: 55 nonempty unsolved page streams matching site text, plus their joined stream; LP2-50 is rune-free and omitted.
scope.procedure: Replay the pinned source, independently score all source matrices and a one-cell printed-panel correction, recover LP2-56 known reading under each operation, and repeat whole-grid selection on 199 shared pagewise shuffles.
scope.parameters: Six literal source matrices × four M/transpose/inverse/inverse-transpose operations × 56 targets = 1,344 outputs; one corrected 4×4 matrix × four operations × 56 targets = 224 outputs; modulus 29, block origin zero, final partial block dropped. The amended full-reading plant uses explicit zero padding removed after decoding.
scope.exclusions: Other matrices, block origins, affine offsets, key changes, plaintext languages, scoring models, interpretations of number panels and the unverified generation of the source phi variants.

dukotah-c8-timestamp-join.title: Do archived LP2 texts supply signature dates for a public pad?
dukotah-c8-timestamp-join.question: Do these archived texts give a signature date for each encrypted page?
dukotah-c8-timestamp-join.finding: Eight signature blocks contain seven distinct clock values, and all eight occur in LP1. The two LP2 text inputs supply no per-page signature date.
dukotah-c8-timestamp-join.limitations: This checks the preserved texts, not every historical image or distribution. It performs no pad decoding; signature clock values are not independently authenticated release dates.

scope.representation: Exact pinned Git bytes of C8 Step 0 and its two textual inputs, then Markdown indentation removal and explicit LP1/LP2 heading boundaries.
scope.parameters: 8 signature blocks; 7 distinct creation seconds; 24 grouped LP2 headings; 57 percent-delimited rune segments.
scope.procedure: Run source Step 0 unchanged in a temporary input tree, compare complete saved JSON, independently parse packet lengths and creation subpackets and attribute blocks to explicit book-part headings.
scope.exclusions: Historical image-wide signature absence, authorship and release-date authentication, random-pad retrieval, I2 adjudication, source 630-test claims and LP2 decryption.

dukotah-ciphertext-feedback-coefficients.title: Do ciphertext-feedback coefficients decode these pages?
dukotah-ciphertext-feedback-coefficients.question: Could earlier ciphertext runes supply the next key?
dukotah-ciphertext-feedback-coefficients.finding: None of 60,864 decodes reached the English-score threshold on the three tested pages. The search did recover both planted examples that used its allowed starting values.
dukotah-ciphertext-feedback-coefficients.limitations: Only LP2-00, 05 and 20 were tested, using up to three earlier ciphertext runes and constant starting values 0 or 1. Those constant values cannot reveal whether the decoder handles key skips correctly.

scope.representation: Source GP29 transcription of page ordinals 0, 5 and 20; 262, 263 and 269 rune indices respectively.
scope.procedure: Run unchanged D-04 source full default grid, parse source stdout and independently reconstruct/rescore each winning feedback term. Separately search all 112 one-tap configurations for each of two declared in-domain plants.
scope.parameters: 28 one-tap, 840 two-tap and 4,204 three-tap coefficient vectors; const0/const1 seeds, signs +/-1, offset0, source English-scored beam width250 and max three skips; 60,864 page decodes total.
scope.exclusions: 52 other nonempty pages, const5 and referenced-text seeds in default LP2 grid, other starts/taps/functions, variable-seed skip power and held-out plaintext verification.

dukotah-fixed-numeric-keys.title: Rotation, hash and cuneiform keys
dukotah-fixed-numeric-keys.question: Could the rotation sequence, LP2-56 hash or cuneiform numbers serve as keys?
dukotah-fixed-numeric-keys.finding: None of the twelve fixed numerical key streams produced a candidate passing the English-language check on the 55 tested pages or their joined text. The keys came from the specified Mayan numbers, printed hash and digit strings.
dukotah-fixed-numeric-keys.limitations: The language check missed three correctly recovered planted messages. Some controls required replacing known runes with F. This does not rule out other numerical keys, starting positions or rules for handling F.

scope.representation: Pinned krisyotam rune streams match 55 site page records exactly; LP2-50 contributes no rune stream. A 56th target joins all 12,956 runes. The B4 source hash matches the five printed hex rows on LP2-56.
scope.procedure: Run the unmodified B1, B4 and C2 source scripts from one isolated copy. Independently reconstruct their fixed GP29 key streams, both signs, Atbash and F-null clocks, and every complete quadgram score/output hash. Inverse-plant three known message lengths per key and clock branch, checking exact expected text and the source score bar separately.
scope.parameters: 12 named streams (2 B1, 5 B4, 5 C2) × 56 targets × 2 signs × 2 Atbash settings × 2 F clocks = 5,376 manuscript cases. Key phase zero per page or for the joined stream. Three control messages × 96 setting branches = 288 complete-message controls. Source score bar >−5.2.
scope.exclusions: No other sequence candidates, key phases, manuscript text layers, altered F behavior, dynamic key schedules, languages, or choice among a large unbounded key space. Historical attribution of the literal numeric values was not independently tested.

dukotah-g02-signature-corpus.title: Which archived Cicada signatures verify?
dukotah-g02-signature-corpus.question: Which archived messages have a valid Cicada signature?
dukotah-g02-signature-corpus.finding: Of 133 archived files, GnuPG verifies 115 under the specified Cicada key. The source program counted 114 because it skipped a signed PGP MESSAGE. One separate malformed copy fails; its repaired copy and the original JPEG extraction verify.
dukotah-g02-signature-corpus.limitations: This checks preserved bytes against a specified public key. The bad copy cannot be treated as a validly parsed signed message until its header is repaired. The check does not prove who owned the key or cover all historical files.

scope.exclusions: Files outside this pinned revision, unarchived signed messages, authorship beyond the public key, and any LP2 decryption hypothesis.
scope.parameters: 135 committed .asc paths, 2 source-scratch exclusions, 133 cases; canonical key fingerprint 6D854CD7933322A601C3286D181F01E57A35090F; source controls C1-C4. Supplemental 2013 opening comparison: four files, one exact header-line repair, and identical signature packets.
scope.procedure: Run the pinned source verifier unchanged in an isolated corpus. Separately submit all 133 exact files to GnuPG under a fresh canonical-key-only home, including armored PGP MESSAGE packets; compare source versus independent verdicts and the two source snapshots by path and bytes.
scope.representation: Every .asc Git blob at pinned revision f08b20b, excluding the source verifier's own two work/ control files; exact raw bytes reconstructed from 89 content-addressed blobs at 133 paths. A 1,459-byte extraction from the separately preserved 2013 JPEG is a supplemental comparator, not a 134th source-scan case.

dukotah-g3-pointer-framings.title: Base32 and coordinate pointer checks
dukotah-g3-pointer-framings.question: Do rune-derived number streams reveal an address?
dukotah-g3-pointer-framings.finding: Longest low-entropy runs were 16, 10 and 16 against 200-shuffle maxima 22, 15 and 22. A planted 32-symbol run was detected. All 15 measurements and 3,000 source null calls reproduce, but this only tests a narrow repeated-symbol signal.
dukotah-g3-pointer-framings.limitations: Every modulo-32 character is valid base32, making the 809 and 231 regex counts fixed by stream length, not address evidence. The digit concatenation supplies no period or separator for the lat/long regex. Coordinate-pair rate never triggers a flag. The source implementation omits additional framings mentioned in its preregistration. Plan timing is retrospective.

scope.representation: Source 12,956-rune unsolved stream equals site LP2-00–49 and LP2-51–55 rune for rune; index-zero F retained.
scope.procedure: Map GP rune indices to prime value, one-based prime index or prime totient. Apply source modulo-32 base32 and decimal concatenation metrics, then compare 200 seed-3301+k histogram-preserving shuffles for every stream/metric. Replay original saved outputs and an independent low-entropy detector.
scope.parameters: 3 streams × 5 metrics × 200 source null calls = 3,000 source measurements, plus 15 real measurements and one planted low-entropy control.
scope.exclusions: No real onion address validation, alternate base32/byte grouping, punctuation insertion, other moduli, page resets, turtle paths or undeclared pointers.

dukotah-grid-as-key-campaign7.title: Grid and onion bytes as LP2 keys
dukotah-grid-as-key-campaign7.question: Could the LP2 number grid or 2014 onion hex be the key to the runic pages?
dukotah-grid-as-key-campaign7.finding: The archived grid list, raw-token alternative bases and onion-XOR streams score at best −6.720, −6.745 and −6.597, below the source’s −5.2 flag. Four no-interrupter controls recover all 120 known runes; four interrupter controls recover 120-rune constructed messages with 3–6 literal-F substitutions each.
dukotah-grid-as-key-campaign7.limitations: The archived hard-coded byte list differs from decoding raw tokens in base 60. The source score screens English-like text under repeated modulo-29 keys only; other grid readings, offsets, nonrepeating keys and languages are outside this result. Planted F-interrupter controls alter 3–6 positions of the fixed source message. The plan is retrospective; the fuller control audit was added after review. The source’s base-59 formula permits four out-of-base x digits; fitting the results into bytes does not make it valid positional base 59.

scope.representation: 55 rune-bearing LP2 segments = site LP2-00–49 and LP2-51–55; concatenated WHOLE has 12,956 runes. F is index zero. Archived hard-coded grid values, raw two-character tokens and three onion hex strings are separately preserved.
scope.procedure: Replay three pinned Campaign VII scripts and independently reconstruct 33 named streams, mod-29 repeating-key decode in both signs, optional Atbash and F-interruption, source quadgram scoring, base range checks and byte XOR forensics.
scope.parameters: 33 source-named streams × 56 targets × 2 signs × 2 Atbash states × 2 F-clock states = 14,784 score cases. Strict source threshold > −5.2. Eight 120-rune known-message controls.
scope.exclusions: No other cell adjudications, byte order or key offsets; no arbitrary onion source, variable key clock, skipped symbols, other scoring models or non-English solutions.

dukotah-grid-cell-adjudication.title: Which bytes are printed in the base-60 grid?
dukotah-grid-cell-adjudication.question: Can we check the disputed bytes against the printed cells?
dukotah-grid-cell-adjudication.finding: All six source-contested cell tokens reproduce (3I, 0I, 2l, 0l, 1O, 0W), matching source-majority bytes 198, 18, 167, 47, 84, 32 rather than the competing decimal column. The automated leave-one-out symbol control scores 236/237 among testable glyphs, and the saved 40-cell human calibration scores 40/40.
dukotah-grid-cell-adjudication.limitations: A source-known replay of one image instrument. The saved human reads can be rescored but their claimed historical blindness cannot be audited. Singleton decisive glyph classes lack leave-one-out controls. This checks printed tokens, not payload decoding.

scope.representation: Exact source-hashed archived JPEGs and two source 256-byte candidate payloads; 256 table cells.
scope.procedure: Run pinned A-04 projection grid, saved-read gate, glyph metric, native-pixel matcher and all-conflict adjudicator on exact images in a disposable source-shaped directory; compare five saved outputs and independently recompute base-60 bytes.
scope.parameters: Six predeclared contested cells 25,175,182,199,215,237; source calibration gate at least 38/40 saved readings; source post-hoc all-eleven extension retained separately.
scope.exclusions: Human reading blindness, other image witnesses or rendering pipelines, changes to cryptographic methods, decipherment of the 256-byte payload.

dukotah-grid-token-roles.title: Grid bytes as ciphertext or rune pointers
dukotah-grid-token-roles.question: Could the grid bytes themselves be encrypted, or point to runes elsewhere in the book?
dukotah-grid-token-roles.finding: Across three declared byte readings, 4,245 byte-cipher outputs yielded no candidate over 85% printable ASCII; the best was 46.2%. Twelve rune-index outputs scored at best −7.183, below the source’s −5 English bar. Full planted byte and three index controls recovered known text; the fourth index rule lacks a full known-reading plant.
dukotah-grid-token-roles.limitations: The source’s page-local pointer rule references rune-only segments 49/50/51, not a verified physical neighbourhood of the printed grid. That segment 49 cannot express one rune of the known-reading control. Thresholds and fixed byte readings do not cover other encodings, offsets, transcriptions or books.

scope.representation: Three 256-byte readings in printed grid order: archived P49/P50/P51 arrays (80+104+72); six-cell image-adjudicated canon; all-eleven-cell resolved. Pointer methods use 57 rune-bearing source segments, omitting rune-free LP2-50, whose rune sequences match site pages.
