The five-column visual-indent extension was disclosed after the bare-block negative. Short four-digit motifs were report-only and do not establish a decoded message.

scope.representation: The three original backslash-continued P.S. digit lines (40+45+46=131 digits) from the pinned 2012 signed-message text; second variant preserves the five-column visual indent of P.S. and a following space.
scope.procedure: Read bare lines in four column directions, concatenation and reversal; repeat four column directions with a five-column indent on the first line. For each, test both two-digit pair alignments for printable ASCII fraction >=95%, longer pinned constants and report-only short motifs/compositeness.
scope.parameters: Six bare and four indented readings; two pair alignments; ten planted readable blocks; 200 random 131-digit three-line controls. The source raised its initial 80% cutoff to 95% after the negative control failed and before real-data screening.
scope.exclusions: Arbitrary column widths, digit substitutions/reordering, other encodings, running keys, additional source messages and any interpretation of a four-digit motif alone as a hit.

haplography-diagonal-bound.title: Can missing duplicate runes hide an autokey pattern?
haplography-diagonal-bound.question: Could missing repeated runes be hiding an autokey pattern in LP2?
haplography-diagonal-bound.finding: The pinned transcription yields 9,640 within-word pairs, 60 doublets and nonzero difference CV 0.0608. Physical duplicate restoration leaves that CV invariant for any number of insertions. An exact upper bound allowing 20 freely allocated nonzero-diagonal additions is 0.0656; at 40 it is 0.0717. A separate checker confirms every count and the insertion identity for all 29^3 three-rune contexts.
haplography-diagonal-bound.limitations: This bounds only exact adjacent-duplicate deletion/restoration and the specified ciphertext-autokey difference statistic. The pinned source omits pride.txt, so its English-corpus planted-control numbers and surrogate null are not exactly replayed; a declared synthetic lumpy control passes instead. The source amended its chi-square clause after its first run; the physical invariance does not depend on that clause. Other feedback rules, correlated multi-rune errors and nearly flat plaintext distributions remain outside scope.

scope.representation: First 55 nonempty '%' segments of the pinned krisyotam_runes.txt, matching source LP2-00–54 labels; within-word adjacent rune indices modulo 29.
scope.procedure: Compute nonzero difference-diagonal counts and CV; insert exact adjacent duplicates algebraically and via exhaustive three-rune contexts. Give an artificial adversary k=0..40 arbitrary additions to the 28 nonzero counts and compute its exact maximal CV. Plant a separate synthetic lumpy ciphertext-autokey versus uniform control.
scope.parameters: 9,640 adjacent pairs, 60 doublets; 28 nonzero diagonals; k=0..40, with the source decision at k=20; CV signal bar 0.40, safe bar 0.30.
scope.exclusions: Source Pride & Prejudice-based control numbers, source surrogate null distribution, plaintext-autokey variants, other feedback equations, off-diagonal transcription errors, and plaintext distributions that are nearly uniform.

heldout-rune-prediction.title: Predicting runes against filtered-random controls
heldout-rune-prediction.question: Can other segments help predict the next rune?
heldout-rune-prediction.finding: None of the fixed measurements passed its threshold. Thirty-five of 1,000 filtered-random controls scored at least as strongly in the combined comparison.
heldout-rune-prediction.limitations: These selected models cannot establish randomness or exclude a cipher. Packed LZMA detected none of the twelve strong synthetic patterns; its ordinary score does not support an exclusion.

scope.representation: Pinned GP29 stream: 12,956 runes in 55 source segments through LP2-55; segment ordinals differ from physical pages. Exact transcription external. Contexts reset per segment; compression/provenance use the joined stream.
scope.procedure: Two static training/test folds by segment-ordinal parity; no test updates, common scoring offsets >=8. Enumerate eight KT and eight PPM-C orders, two whole-stream LZMA views and eight balance/drift metrics. Compare all 26 against 1,000 shared continuous XI one-resample filtered-uniform streams.
scope.parameters: Orders 1–8: KT Dirichlet-1/2; PPM-C count exclusion, closed-alphabet normalization and uniform order−1. 12,516 held-out positions. LZMA preset9+extreme, raw1/minimal big-endian base29. Dispersion widths 29/58/116/232/464; 4/8-bin drift plus 8-bin linear trend. Suppression 0.83; seeds 3301241024000–3301241024999. Joint max-Z scales all 1,001 rows symmetrically, exact constants→0, ties>=; gate fraction<0.01 plus strict marginal 1% tail. Uniform gain display tolerance 1e-10.
scope.exclusions: Not a historical replay, all PPM variants, adaptive test updates, cross-segment prediction, optional transformer or held-out LZMA likelihood. Nulls match counts in expectation only. Packed LZMA flags 0/12 strong patterns (0/18 overall examples). No OTP, randomness, plaintext-absence or cipher-family verdict.

historical-prime-and-ps-keys.title: Earlier puzzle numbers as LP2 rune keys
historical-prime-and-ps-keys.question: Could unused numbers from earlier Cicada puzzles be LP2 keys?
historical-prime-and-ps-keys.finding: None of 4,032 exact-source decodes crossed the English-score bar of −5.2. The best scored −6.757. Two planted messages were recovered, including an F-interrupted case.
historical-prime-and-ps-keys.limitations: The original source reports maxima, not a selection-adjusted null or proof that every true English plaintext would pass its score bar. This does not test onion-cookie hashes, raw PGP packets, other offsets, nonrepeating uses, or different languages. The telnet transcript is a later preserved copy.

scope.representation: Nine source-defined numeric streams reduced mod 29 and repeated over each target. The 2013 missing-prime run is 73–1223, separately from the CicadaOS prime_echo output.
scope.procedure: For each stream, source rune-bearing segment and joined stream, decode with both arithmetic signs, Atbash on/off and F interruption on/off; rank using the pinned English quadgram model.
scope.parameters: 9 streams × 56 targets × 8 settings = 4,032 cases; 12,956 runes in 55 separate source segments; threshold score_norm > −5.2.
scope.exclusions: Other historical artifacts, onion-cookie hashes and raw PGP packet bytes, key offsets, nonrepeating streams, alternate rune transcriptions, other languages and a selection-adjusted null.

im-near-f-markers.title: I/M rune proximity to F interruptions
im-near-f-markers.question: Are I or M runes unusually close to F runes under a fixed local-marker reading?
im-near-f-markers.finding: 132 F runes have an I or M within two rune positions; 34 of 999 page-preserving shuffles equal or exceed that count.
im-near-f-markers.limitations: The forum proposal gives no marker distance or direction. The chosen pair and radius are post hoc; this is not a cipher or resynchronization test.

scope.representation: LP2-00–55 29-rune page streams, without punctuation or cross-page neighborhoods.
scope.procedure: Count F runes with I or M in a +/-2 rune neighborhood and repeat after 999 seeded within-page shuffles.
scope.parameters: F=0, I=10, M=19; radius two; 999 shuffles, seed 33014055.
scope.exclusions: Other marker labels, radii, section splits, F skip behavior, collision rules and key generation.

image-row-coverage.title: Can image-only detection find every rune row?
image-row-coverage.question: Does a fixed image-only horizontal-projection detector recover every individually annotated rune row across eight selected page layouts?
image-row-coverage.finding: The fixed detector does not recover all individual rune rows: 43 of 65 match. Its 83 proposals comprise 43 individual rune rows, 24 other text rows, seven merged rune-row bands and nine artwork bands.
image-row-coverage.limitations: Selected layouts and approximate manual intervals, not independent random trials. Both implementations use Pillow decoding. Prior page familiarity is disclosed; human annotation review remains pending.

scope.representation: Original JPEG grayscale horizontal projections and frozen manual half-open rune-body intervals; no canonical transcription input.
scope.procedure: Fixed image-only proposals; maximum-cardinality one-to-one interval matching; each annotated rune row separately omitted from a hypothetical candidate inventory while the image stays unchanged.
scope.parameters: Central 22–78% width; grayscale <128; active ink >1%; discard active heights <20 before merging gaps <12 pixels; interval IoU >=0.5; eight selected images and 65 rune reference rows.
scope.exclusions: No rune recognition, actual omitted archive line finding, classifier accuracy claim, whole-book certification, random-sample inference or threshold tuning.

instar-narrowband-lines.title: Instar's high-frequency line and low hum
instar-narrowband-lines.question: Do the reported ~15 kHz and ~60 Hz features appear in the archived Instar recording under a fixed spectrum measurement?
instar-narrowband-lines.finding: The pinned Instar MP3 has a persistent high-frequency line at 15,645.89 Hz (+39.72 dB) and a low-band peak at 59.22 Hz (+14.89 dB) under the declared spectral measurement. Neither identifies a watermark, device, location or cipher.
instar-narrowband-lines.limitations: A frequency line is not a decoded watermark or evidence of the recording hardware.

scope.representation: Two preserved MP3 carriers decoded to 44.1 kHz stereo float samples; channels averaged.
scope.procedure: Full-track Hann Welch PSD, 65,536-sample windows, 50% overlap; select largest bin in 50–70 Hz and 14–17 kHz; compare to local median; check fixed peak in nonoverlapping 20-second windows.
scope.parameters: Bands 50–70 Hz and 14–17 kHz, local margins 20 and 300 Hz respectively; exclude ±3 Hz around peak; window prominence counts use a 10 dB descriptive cut, not a watermark decision threshold.
scope.exclusions: Watermark extraction, device attribution, recording geography, 500 Hz gap events and LP decryption.

jpeg-byte-mode-replay.title: JPEG byte histograms: the four-page split
jpeg-byte-mode-replay.question: Does the reported four-page JPEG byte-frequency class reproduce, and does it correspond to grayscale encoding?
jpeg-byte-mode-replay.finding: LP2-00, 04, 24 and 26 have modal byte 44; the other 54 LP2 files have modal byte 00. Both classes include one- and three-component JPEGs. LP1-00 and 02 have modal byte 28; the other 15 LP1 files have modal byte 00.
jpeg-byte-mode-replay.limitations: The test uses current archived JPEGs; the source's exact October 2023 repository revision and missing histogram screenshots are unavailable. File-byte mode does not establish randomness, a payload, a date code or an encoding cause.

scope.representation: All 58 archived LP2 and 17 archived LP1 original JPEG files; full encoded-file bytes, not pixels or rune values.
scope.procedure: Count all 256 possible byte values in each file; read baseline JPEG frame component counts; locate zero bytes relative to the first scan header.
scope.parameters: A file's class is determined only by its modal whole-byte value; ties are reported explicitly; no threshold or page exclusion.
scope.exclusions: Historical repository revision matching, screenshots, randomness testing, steganographic extraction, visual artifact interpretation and inferred author intent.

jpeg-modal-reencode-control.title: Are the JPEG byte classes stable?
jpeg-modal-reencode-control.question: Does the four-page nonzero modal-byte set persist after a fixed JPEG re-encode of the same LP2 page images?
jpeg-modal-reencode-control.finding: The originals have four nonzero-mode files (00, 04, 24, 26). Re-encoding yields 23, 23 and 5 nonzero-mode files at qualities 75, 85 and 95 respectively; none of the original four remain at quality 95.
jpeg-modal-reencode-control.limitations: The encoding control cannot identify the original encoder or test a hidden-message extraction.

scope.representation: Complete encoded JPEG bytes of archived originals and in-memory Pillow re-encodes; no rune or pixel histogram.
scope.procedure: Count the modal byte of each original; decode and re-encode each page at three fixed JPEG qualities with subsampling disabled; recount and compare membership.
scope.parameters: 58 archived LP2 pages; Pillow 11.3.0; qualities 75, 85, 95; subsampling=0; no resize.
scope.exclusions: Other encoders and quality settings, isolated scan data, original-file production, payload extraction and claims of randomness.

keyword-skip-family.title: Keyword search with skipped key positions
keyword-skip-family.question: Can these repeating keyword keys decode pages when key positions may be skipped?
keyword-skip-family.finding: None of the short checks passed the first English-score gate. No full-page manuscript decode was run. In the controls, 617 scores passed but only 575 known readings were recovered completely.
keyword-skip-family.limitations: This checks the listed keywords and the source selection rule. Passing scores can be wrong, and rejected starting positions received no full-page test; it does not exclude this cipher family.

scope.representation: Pinned GP29 indices from the source percent-separated transcription; 55 nonempty segments / 12,956 runes. Page-local forward order; optional ciphertext Atbash c->28-c. Exact raw transcription remains external.
scope.procedure: Unchanged source attack_page_keyword_fast: all canonical phases at each keyword/sign/Atbash; stable cumulative-score beam, then normalized returned-path phase selection. Strict first best phase only; promote if screen > -6, full confirm > -5.5. Accelerated representation has native ordered-terminal parity. Separate normalized-terminal diagnostic only for promoted fulls; none occurred.
scope.parameters: 623 labels/617 encoded arrays/2,814 labelled phases x55 segments x2 signs x2 Atbash=619,080 screens/137,060 phase selections. Screens min(90,L), beam 300;full L, beam 500; max 3 conditional skips. Source tiling L*4+64 and finite zero-padding preserved. All duplicate labels/phases retained. Source encoder controls use supp 0.83 and frozen seeds;665 own-key/endpoint cases plus4 complete 623-label searches.
scope.exclusions: Other vocabularies, noncanonical offsets, generic prefilter/smoke branch, alternate score/ranking, full decoding of rejected phases, other languages, joined pages and search-wide significance. Score passage is not exact recovery; controls fail some phase/ranking recovery checks. No broad cipher-family verdict.

known-key-reset-prefix-gate.title: When a key reset cannot fix an opening
known-key-reset-prefix-gate.question: For the fixed second-koan key and 12-rune Warning opening, which saved mismatches occur before a word or line reset could change them?
known-key-reset-prefix-gate.finding: For this fixed key and Warning opening, line resets are already ruled out on all 55 rune pages. Word resets are ruled out on 54; only LP2-54 needs a run. A reset cannot fix a mismatch that occurs before it.
known-key-reset-prefix-gate.limitations: This covers the second-koan key, phase-zero subtraction and the 12-rune Warning opening in the archived text, with headings retained. Other settings and plaintexts remain untested. LP2-54 is eligible, not a match.

scope.representation: Exact raw LP2-00–55 transcriptions including headings, canonical GP29; separators retained to locate word and CR/LF boundaries. LP2-50 has no runes and is excluded from the 55 nonempty-page gate counts.
scope.procedure: Verify the saved second-koan/phase 0/subtract full outputs against direct canonical-input equations, then compare each first Warning12 mismatch with the first possible word or line reset. Exclude only strict-before mismatches. Decode reset variants only on synthetic controls, never manuscript targets.
scope.parameters: One fixed 13-rune second-koan key; phase 0; subtraction mod29; one fixed 12-rune Warning opening;55 nonempty pages; two deterministic reset gates; four synthetic boundary controls. All55 saved arrays/12,956 runes independently checked.
scope.exclusions: No new reset-target decode, all-phase search, other keys/signs/openings, skips, later positions, heading removal, corrected text, general language test or full-plaintext conclusion. LP2-54 surviving the word gate is not a positive reading.

known-reading-languages.title: Language comparison checked against known LP readings
known-reading-languages.question: Does the eight-language length comparison recognize the established English readings of Liber Primus?
known-reading-languages.finding: The pooled 739 native rune tokens rank closest to English in every comparison, but some individual known-English sections do not. Removing 38 non-rune alphabetic characters from LP2-56 changes its literal-profile comparison; the hash had doubled its apparent word count from 25 to 50.
known-reading-languages.limitations: Sections contain 18–208 native tokens and are not independent random samples. The pool reuses the sections. Literal spelling, symbol units and embedded material affect rankings. The amendment followed inspection of the first run; human review pending.

scope.representation: All nine known reading sections; headings included; slash/CR/LF wraps removed within sections. Unfiltered literal labels retained as diagnostic; amended rune-derived labels and native rune lengths; sections pooled without boundary joining.
scope.procedure: Replay fixed known readings exactly. Compare all section/pool length histograms with all eight FLORES dev language profiles under letter, folded and GP grouping models. Check independently using archived traces, regex tokenization and rational distances.
scope.parameters: Nine sections, 17 pages; 10 targets including the pool; 70 profiles, 90 eight-language rankings; bins 1–15 and 16+; all 997 development sentences per language. Original plan plus post-diagnostic amendment.
scope.exclusions: No blind decryption, posterior, accuracy inference from independent random trials, new language labels for solved sections, or authentication of source readings. No new unknown-page results. GP grouping is an orthographic sensitivity.

l7-score-recovery-controls.title: Can one score cutoff judge every decode?
l7-score-recovery-controls.question: Could a good-looking score hide an incorrect decode?
l7-score-recovery-controls.finding: Four synthetic decodes passed the score cutoff while recovering less than 90% of the known text. The score ranges also changed across text registers and decoder settings, so a score alone cannot certify a correct reading.
l7-score-recovery-controls.limitations: These controls do not identify LP2’s language or cipher. The null samples are too small to validate a cutoff for a large key search.

scope.representation: Fixed source-derived GP29 plaintext/ciphertext/key fixtures, English quadgram counts and a source ciphertext prefix used only for order-destroying conditional controls.
scope.procedure: Replay the unchanged source beam on fifteen paired register plants and twenty-eight mechanism plants; generate 120 fixed-seed shuffled-prefix nulls per setting; independently recalculate rune recovery, quadgram scores and null summaries.
scope.parameters: Five registers × three L120 trials with correct and wrong keys; four mechanisms × seven L240 plants; source beam width 400/max_skip 3; score cutoff −5.5 and recovery reference 90%; three null settings L31/bw120,L120/bw400,L400/bw120 × 120 draws.
scope.exclusions: Full 67-case L7 envelope; original missing EN_MODERN/CY and derived vowel panels; six-model archive rescoring; G3 difference-floor census; independently preregistered corpus selection; large-search tail calibration; real LP2 keys or cipher exclusions.

large-gap-file-size-replay.title: The reported big-gap page file sizes
large-gap-file-size-replay.question: Does the claimed 74 KB average JPEG-size difference between the reported big-gap pages and comparison pages survive an arithmetic replay on the archived originals?
large-gap-file-size-replay.finding: The printed big-gap sizes average 582.8125 KiB; the 15 comparison sizes average 542.8667 KiB, not 508.9375 KiB. Their corrected difference is 39.9458 KiB. The archived precise-byte difference is 39.83 KiB; 17,278 of 100,000 seeded fixed-label reshuffles are at least as large in the same direction.
large-gap-file-size-replay.limitations: The supplied post's 109-, 73- and 129-pixel gap claims cannot be reconstructed without its missing image coordinates. The source-selected page labels and non-random comparison group make the shuffle descriptive only. JPEG file size is confounded by image content and encoding.

scope.representation: Complete encoded byte lengths of all 58 archived LP2 original JPEGs; frozen 16-page and 15-page lists from the supplied discussion.
scope.procedure: Recalculate the two printed size-list means, match each printed integer KiB label to its archived JPEG using ceiling(bytes/1024), measure the precise-byte group difference, then compare it with 100,000 fixed-label permutations of the 31 listed files.
scope.parameters: 16 reported big-gap pages; 15 reported comparison pages; all 58 LP2 image sizes listed; random seed 20261022 and 100,000 shuffles.
scope.exclusions: No independent classification of image gap widths or punctuation, no causal inference from file size, and no cipher test.

large-gap-mark-alignment.title: Marked lines and the gaps below them
large-gap-mark-alignment.question: In fixed source-guided LP2 image regions, do apostrophes, quotation marks and digits occur on the lines immediately above unusually wide gaps?
large-gap-mark-alignment.finding: The six marked lines all have 108–110 blank pixels below; 28 unmarked measured lines have 73–75. Raw text detects only five marked wide gaps because its LP2-35 line 4 omits the apostrophe that the image and reviewed text contain.
large-gap-mark-alignment.limitations: Pages and lines were selected from an existing hypothesis, so perfect local alignment is not a population-level test or an independent significance estimate. The upright LP2-35 mark is visually adjudicated in the site's reviewed layer; the original report's image coordinates are unavailable.

scope.representation: Aligned rows from original 2400×3600 JPEG crops and the archived raw/reviewed text fields in their structured page records.
scope.procedure: Predeclare six source-guided image rectangles; count fully blank horizontal rows between printed lines at three thresholds; align each gap with the raw and reviewed text line above; compare punctuation/digit marks with the following gap.
scope.parameters: Six pages, 34 measured interline gaps, ASCII apostrophe/double-quote/digit markers, wide-gap descriptive cutoff 100 pixels, grayscale cutoffs 100/160/200, five dark pixels per row, merge across at most 14 blank rows.
scope.exclusions: Whole-book mark/gap association, independent sampling, causality, original author screenshot coordinates, typesetting mechanism and binary decryption.

large-gap-pixel-replay.title: Measured large gaps between rune lines
large-gap-pixel-replay.question: Do fixed original-image measurements reproduce the reported 109-pixel large gap, ordinary 73-pixel gaps, and 129-pixel parable exception?
large-gap-pixel-replay.finding: At all three thresholds, LP2-04 has one 109-pixel gap and ten 73–75-pixel gaps; LP2-35 one 110-pixel gap and ten 73–75-pixel gaps; LP2-57 one 129-pixel gap and three 73–74-pixel gaps; and LP2-14 six 73–75-pixel gaps.
large-gap-pixel-replay.limitations: The four image regions are source-guided selections, not a random or whole-book census. The original post's screenshot coordinates are unavailable, so exact agreement with its measurement method cannot be established. Different page layouts prevent a causal conclusion from the spacing alone.

scope.representation: Fixed rectangles in four hashed 2400×3600 source JPEGs, measured as wholly blank horizontal pixel rows between runic ink-row bands.
scope.procedure: Declare source-labeled pages and rectangular rune regions, threshold grayscale rows, merge within-line ink bands, count every intervening blank-row run, and repeat at three darkness thresholds. Verify with an independent flat-pixel projection.
scope.parameters: Rectangles in plan.json; five dark pixels to activate a row; at most 14 blank rows joined within a printed line; grayscale cutoffs 100, 160 and 200.
scope.exclusions: Full 16-page source classification, original Canva crop coordinates, punctuation causation, source typesetting software, bitstream or decipherment.

later-message-f-omission.title: 2016 and 2017 message lengths after omitting F
later-message-f-omission.question: Do both preserved signed messages become prime-length GP rune streams after F is omitted?
later-message-f-omission.finding: The original lengths are 177/45. Each has four F runes, so F removal gives 173/41, both prime. W removal also yields two primes, 173/43; these are the only two of 29 single-symbol omissions with that property under this encoding.
later-message-f-omission.limitations: The signed sources are Latin text, and rune counts depend on a chosen GP encoding and body boundary. The 2-of-29 comparison is conditional and not a probability of intent or an LP2 cipher result.

scope.representation: Signed Latin-letter message bodies encoded into GP rune indices by unique shortest aliases with V mapped to U; PGP signature armor excluded.
scope.procedure: Verify preserved message bytes, encode both bodies, count original and F-omitted lengths, then repeat one-symbol omission for each of all 29 GP rune indices.
scope.parameters: 2016 and 2017 manifest body boundaries; fixed GP alphabet; one symbol type removed from each body at a time; primality by trial division.
scope.exclusions: Other transliterations, sentence segmentations, key-layer behavior, unsolved manuscript text or inference of author intent.

layout-count-streams.title: Do line or word lengths carry a message?
layout-count-streams.question: Have we tried reading the line and word lengths as a message?
layout-count-streams.finding: The best reading used visible-word rune count minus one with page-local scoring (−6.697). In 78 of 256 matched shuffled-count searches, the best of the same eight readings scored at least as high (global add-one 79/257≈0.307).
layout-count-streams.limitations: Only direct English under count or count-minus-one GP-index mappings and the stated line/word boundaries was tested. A further cipher, other numeral mapping or visual layout signal remains open. The source catalog lists an idea, not a verified historical attempt.

scope.representation: Physical rune-bearing line counts and hyphen-delimited visible-word rune counts from all 55 rune-bearing LP2-00–55 transcription pages.
scope.procedure: Compute 594 line and 2,776 word counts; interpret each as n mod29 or (n−1) mod29, score canonical GP Latin labels page-locally or joined. Compare the best of eight scores with best-of-eight maxima in 256 shared within-page count shuffles. Plant decoded GP readings in synthetic count streams.
scope.parameters: Eight declared readings; 256 shared shuffles seeded 33017125–33017380. Every arm clears the frozen 100-English-quadgram eligibility gate.
scope.exclusions: Other separators or transcription variants, enciphered or non-English count streams, visual spacing in source images, alternate numeral encodings and historical-attempt claims.

leo-chain-key-alignment.title: Do number sequences fit the rune-difference chain?
leo-chain-key-alignment.question: Did primes or Fibonacci numbers reveal the rune chain?
leo-chain-key-alignment.finding: The pinned 21-effective-sequence × 14-bijection × 300-offset × 2-sign × 2-clock grid reproduces all nine source maxima. Both planted prime-chain controls recover their clock and score 1.663. On the source-highlighted pages 54–55, 20/39 full-grid shuffles reach the observed maximum 1.146.
leo-chain-key-alignment.limitations: The section control is conditional on the source-highlighted maximum and uses only 39 shuffled complete searches. IoC is not plaintext recovery. Other sequences, mappings, section choices and ciphers remain outside this finite grid.

scope.representation: Nine pinned unsolved relikd LP2 rune sections, each analyzed through its first 500 adjacent rune changes (307 on pages 54–55).
scope.procedure: Replay source-named numerical streams under 14 nonzero-change bijections, 300 offsets, signs ±1 and both doublet key clocks; compare all nine source maxima and planted controls; rerun full grid on 39 within-section shuffles of source-selected pages 54–55.
scope.parameters: 21 effectively eligible sequence entries, including duplicate prime/primeidx; 352,800 evaluated settings per section, 39 selected-section shuffles; 2 planted prime-chain controls.
scope.exclusions: Other generators, more offsets, different key boundaries or maps, language scoring, full decryption and unselected-section null tails.

leo-chain-sequence-keys.title: Number-sequence keys in direct and chain views
leo-chain-sequence-keys.question: Could prime, Fibonacci or totient numbers be the key?
leo-chain-sequence-keys.finding: Familiar number sequences yielded no established reading. The strongest rune-frequency pattern was also reached by 3 of 99 shuffled sections and did not clear the comparison after allowing for the nine sections searched.
leo-chain-sequence-keys.limitations: This compared symbol frequencies, not readable sentences, using 24 named sequences, offsets 0–199 and five fixed ways of representing the runes. Other key sources, offsets and section boundaries remain open.

scope.representation: Nine pinned relikd unsolved sections, their generated Leo dataset indices, forward and reverse nonrepeat chain increments and original or Atbash GP29 runes.
scope.procedure: Replay the named 24-sequence, 200-offset, two-sign grid on five source streams; retain three best rows per section and stream. Replay the source solved-text running-key arm. For each section, select the grid maximum and compare with the same selection on 99 rune-order shuffles. Gate on planted raw and chain prime-key streams first.
scope.parameters: Source sequence rules from pinned tests4.py; GP29 and chain Z28/Z29; random.Random(330104/330105) planted controls and 330104 section shuffles; plus-one selected-grid tails.
scope.exclusions: Other key sources, offsets outside 0–199, alternative section joins or boundaries, English scoring, held-out plaintext and every cipher outside the declared source grid.

leo-cipher-model-fingerprints.title: Can a simple cipher imitate LP2's rare repeated runes?
leo-cipher-model-fingerprints.question: Does a matching repeat rate reveal the cipher?
leo-cipher-model-fingerprints.finding: The source chain has 20 equal adjacent pairs among 2,978 versus LP2's 86 among 12,955. For c_i=c_(i-1)+p_i+1 mod 29, a repeat occurs exactly when p_i=28 (EA); the chosen solved sample has 20 such positions. The chain's +1 offset is closest of 29 in a declared post-observation check, without implying that LP2 uses it.
leo-cipher-model-fingerprints.limitations: One fixed solved plaintext and one instance of each random-key generator; summary statistics do not recover plaintext or identify a cipher. The 29-offset comparison was motivated by the observed source result. The source scales the target chi-square for display in a way that does not preserve its null reference.

scope.representation: Nine relikd unsolved sections with 12,956 rune indices, 2,979 solved plaintext rune indices, and the first 60,000 GP rune indices of a pinned War and Peace baseline.
scope.procedure: Reconstruct all 23 source-specified synthetic generators and compare their adjacent-pair rate, normalized IoC, chi-square and lag-two pair rate with the archived source table. Separately count all 29 additive-chain offsets and verify the equality identity.
scope.parameters: GP29, source random.Random(3301), 23 named source models, 29 post-observation additive offsets b=0..28.
scope.exclusions: Other plaintext samples, key grids, cipher boundaries, complete plaintext recovery, source model selection probabilities and broad cipher-family exclusion.

leo-shared-key-differences.title: Do LP2 sections share a running key?
leo-shared-key-differences.question: Do two LP2 sections appear to share a running key?
leo-shared-key-differences.finding: The top distinct-section score is 6.0117 (pages 3–7 versus 33–39, shift 25, overlap 1120); 53 of 99 shuffled whole searches match or exceed it. The all-pair maximum 11.319 is a self-pair at lag one, not cross-section evidence. The source printout gives z=3.3 for another tested alignment, while pinned current code gives z=5.68; an older SD approximation is numerically consistent with 3.3, but the historical formula used is unverified.
leo-shared-key-differences.limitations: The 36-pair shuffle comparison was specified after the self-pair maximum appeared and is exploratory. Shuffling section order does not model every plausible cipher. No plaintext or key is recovered.

scope.representation: Nine pinned relikd LP2 unsolved section rune streams; 12,956 runes total.
scope.procedure: Replay the source synthetic shared-key power example; scan all 45 unordered section pairs over shifts with at least 300 rune overlap, then 99 seeded full-search section-order shuffles. A clearly post-observation follow-up restricts to 36 distinct-section pairs and 99 separate full-search controls.
scope.parameters: GP29, 1,200-rune synthetic overlap, 300 source-style null draws, 99 all-pair shuffles and 99 distinct-pair follow-up shuffles.
scope.exclusions: Other transcriptions, key models, alternate boundaries or shifts, reverse transforms and full decryption.

leo-transform-periodic-profile.title: Do transformed LP2 runes show a reliable period?
leo-transform-periodic-profile.question: Is the period 238 signal a useful clue?
leo-transform-periodic-profile.finding: The pinned pages 27–32 two-step difference stream has normalized periodic coincidence 1.412285 at period 238, with source within-profile z 5.950736. One of 499 selected-maximum rune shuffles reaches the observed peak. A planted 13-cycle has very high period-13 coincidence (23.464); the ranking selects period 143 = 11 × 13, passing the literal frozen positive criterion. However, its selected standardized score falls below 452 shuffle maxima, so this score alone poorly distinguishes a known periodic source. The observed peak does not identify an encryption cycle.
leo-transform-periodic-profile.limitations: The shuffle tail is conditional on the five-transform, eligible-period scan on pages 27–32. A nine-section selection bound does not cover the separate concatenated stream, other statistics, segmentation choices or prior source analyses. The planted control satisfies the period-multiple gate, but within-profile z is not a calibrated universal periodicity detector. This record does not test decryption.

scope.representation: Nine pinned unsolved relikd rune sections (12,956 runes); pages 27–32 are the selected conditional-control section.
scope.procedure: Replay five source rune transformations, normalized periodic coincidence through 300 in each section and through 600 in the concatenation; independently measure fourgram spacings and word boundaries. Shuffle pages 27–32 rune order 499 times, taking the maximum within-profile z across all five transforms and periods, then test a planted 13-cycle.
scope.parameters: GP29; at least six symbols per residue column; random.Random seeds 330103 and 1330; 499 shuffles.
scope.exclusions: Other text sources, other selection families, alternate word boundaries, full-page plaintext tests and all decryption claims.

leo-word-pattern-dictionary.title: Can LP2 words be shifted dictionary words?
leo-word-pattern-dictionary.question: Could each LP2 word simply be a shifted dictionary word?
leo-word-pattern-dictionary.finding: For lengths four through eight, Caesar-pattern matches are 165/511, 12/317, 0/256, 0/216 and 0/156. The original 2,000-word-per-length random control gives 627, 45, 4, 0 and 0. Affine match rates resemble that control. The published 'reversed' operator reverses a difference tuple, which is not literal word reversal.
leo-word-pattern-dictionary.limitations: Results depend on the pinned external dictionary, relikd word segmentation and source random baseline. A lack of dictionary-pattern hits does not rule out other vocabularies, hidden word boundaries, longer transforms or plaintext recovery. The source dictionary and page files have not been redistributed.

scope.representation: Nine pinned unsolved relikd sections, 12,956 rune symbols, full source-visible words of rune lengths 4–8. The 18 source page files and source rune dictionary are SHA-256 pinned but must be obtained separately.
scope.procedure: Build sets of mod-29 neighboring-rune difference tuples from the dictionary, then count exact Caesar, source-reversed-difference, literal reversed-word Caesar and affine-normalized membership. Compare source's 2,000 uniform-random words per length and solved LP1 plaintext.
scope.parameters: GP29; word lengths 4–8; random.Random(1) continuously across lengths; 2,000 random words per length.
scope.exclusions: Other dictionaries, alternative segmentation, per-word key inference beyond tuple membership, whole-page readability and all other cipher families.

line-initial-layout-control.title: Do positional runes in LP2 hide a message?
line-initial-layout-control.question: Do the first runes of lines, or other fixed positions, hide a message?
line-initial-layout-control.finding: Independent parsing confirms 12,956 runes on 594 physical lines. The line-initial chi-square is 78.656 against a flat-null mean near 27, but a layout-aware reflow gives p=0.177 in the pinned source and p=0.195 in an independently seeded replay. The other nine position tests and five rejection tests do not clear their gate. Six English-reading families remain below their own best-of-family null maxima; planted controls are recovered. The layout-aware detector has 200/200 power in the two source-planted mechanisms when at least 60% of line initials are forced.
line-initial-layout-control.limitations: The width model is approximate and the original typesetter is unknown; the external BabelStone font-width correlation reported by the source cannot be verified because the font file is absent from the pinned checkout. The six message families score English under a bounded keyless transform set. Boundary-rejection tests have little power with only four line-crossing doublets. Planted power applies only to the two specified synthetic mechanisms and fixed phrase; weaker or different forcing remains open. Source message-family nulls were repeated with independent per-family seed states, so sampled extrema differ from the archived serial receipt.

scope.representation: First 55 nonempty percentage-delimited segments of pinned krisyotam_runes.txt; 12,956 rune indices on 594 nonempty slash-delimited physical lines. Hyphen, period, slash and page delimiters retain the source geometry.
scope.procedure: Replay source C-02 Arm A (10 positional histograms), Arm B (six English-scored keyless reading families with within-family best-of-search nulls), Arm C (five position-conditioned repeat/difference checks), the post-hoc width-fit/reflow confound and planted forcing power curve. Independently parse physical lines, verify position and doublet tables, fit widths and reflow with a separate seeded simulation.
scope.parameters: 55 pages; 594 physical lines; 29 runes; source 200,000 Arm A and C null draws per applicable test; source 5,000 layout reflows plus 2,000 independent reflows; six Arm B families and 56,376 source candidate variants; family-specific null replicate counts recorded in replay-armB.json; 200 planted streams per mechanism/fraction and 2,000 synthetic null streams; per-test gate 0.001/21.
scope.exclusions: Other transcripts and page ranges, ornament- or column-defined position sets, language models other than English quadgrams, transforms outside the 232 per-read identity/Atbash/shift/direction/F variants, external font validation, original typesetting software, and any complete LP2 decryption.

linear-ciphertext-feedback.title: Additive, Beaufort and subtractive ciphertext feedback
linear-ciphertext-feedback.question: Which literal feedback recurrences tie a ciphertext doublet to a zero plaintext value?
linear-ciphertext-feedback.finding: Additive and Beaufort feedback make identical zero/doublet predictions on the archived ciphertext. Subtractive feedback does not: its literal inverse has 437 zero outputs versus 86 for the other two.
linear-ciphertext-feedback.limitations: This invariant cannot establish any of the three as the encryption rule. Literal inverse output frequencies are not evidence of readable plaintext or a key-layer exclusion.

scope.representation: Archived 29-rune LP2-00–55 streams, non-runes removed within each page.
scope.procedure: Invert each adjacent pair under three literal recurrences; tabulate outputs 0–28; independently verify zero conditions and the additive/Beaufort sign identity.
scope.parameters: 12,901 within-page adjacent rune pairs; all 29 output values; no adjustable key or scoring threshold.
scope.exclusions: Unknown keys, changed alphabets, zero skipping, interruption, resets, language scoring, and plaintext identification.

literal-prime-affine.title: Literal prime alphabet: affine permutations for every modulus above 109
literal-prime-affine.question: Can a fixed affine map modulo any integer greater than 109 nontrivially permute the full 29-prime alphabet?
literal-prime-affine.finding: No nonidentity permutation exists within scope: 812 anchor pairs reduce to the identity branch and 13,212 candidate maps with no survivors.
literal-prime-affine.limitations: Full literal-prime alphabet only; not rune indices, partial page support, noninjective maps or position-dependent rules. Human review pending. No proof-assistant rerun.

scope.representation: The 29 stored Gematria Primus prime values, from 2 through 109; literal values, not rune indices.
scope.procedure: Enumerate distinct anchor outputs of 2 and 3; reduce each nonidentity branch to divisors of nonzero witness differences; verify full palette equality.
scope.parameters: All integer m>109; all coefficient residues a,b modulo m; 812 distinct anchor pairs; no language score.
scope.exclusions: Partial palettes, ordinal/rune-index transforms, noninjective maps, nonlinear maps, and position-dependent keys.

literal-prime-affine-pages.title: LP2 page supports: literal-prime affine maps and the two page-55 exceptions
literal-prime-affine-pages.question: Which fixed affine maps into the prime palette remain injective on each archived LP2-00–55 page support?
literal-prime-affine-pages.finding: 54 of 55 nonempty rune pages admit only identity. LP2-55 additionally permits (58p+57) mod 114 and (102p+101) mod 202. LP2-50 has no rune support and is not tested.
literal-prime-affine-pages.limitations: Archived rune support only; not a plaintext recovery. Nonlinear, noninjective, position-dependent and rune-index maps are excluded. Human review pending.

scope.representation: Literal prime values of the rune types present on each archived LP2-00–55 page; LP2-50 has no rune support. Outputs may be any GP prime.
scope.procedure: Group identical supports, enumerate all anchor pairs and divisibility candidates, and retain every allowed-output map injective on the observed support.
scope.parameters: All integer m>109 and coefficient residues a,b; 812 anchors per nonempty support; three distinct supports; empty support untested.
scope.exclusions: Noninjective, nonlinear and position-dependent rules; rune-index transforms; altered transcriptions; plaintext scoring or recovery.

literal-prime-quadratic.title: Literal prime alphabet: quadratic permutations for every modulus above 109
literal-prime-quadratic.question: Can a fixed quadratic map nontrivially permute the full literal-prime alphabet for any modulus above 109?
literal-prime-quadratic.finding: No nonidentity permutation within scope. Independent reconstruction verifies 8,254,630 finite-branch coefficient checks and the bounded identity branch.
literal-prime-quadratic.limitations: Full literal-prime alphabet and degree at most two only. Not partial supports, rune indices, higher degrees or position-dependent keys. Human review pending; no proof-assistant rerun.

scope.representation: The 29 stored Gematria Primus prime values, from 2 through 109; literal values, not rune indices.
scope.procedure: Enumerate distinct images of 2, 3 and 5; reduce nonexact branches to finite divisors; solve all coefficient congruences and verify full palette equality; bound the identity-anchor branch.
scope.parameters: All integer m>109; all quadratic coefficient residues a,b,c; 21,924 ordered distinct anchor triples; no language score.
scope.exclusions: Partial palettes, ordinal/rune-index transforms, noninjective maps, degree above two, and position-dependent keys.

lp1-payload-outer-ring.title: LP1 embedded messages: remove the changing outer digit
lp1-payload-outer-ring.question: Does a fixed one-character perimeter removal make the four LP1-10–13 signed-message diagrams identical inside, and does the same reading apply to the two visible LP1 five-by-five squares?
lp1-payload-outer-ring.finding: All four signed-message bodies yield the same original-orientation interior [[10,12,10],[12,14,12],[10,12,10]] under the fixed crop. Their border digits read 3301 in page order. The inner row sums are 32, 38 and 32, so the interior is not magic. The visible LP1-05 and LP1-16 three-by-three cores are unequal and share no value.
lp1-payload-outer-ring.limitations: The supplied discussion has image placeholders and does not name the four diagrams precisely; the identification here follows the thread's four repeated diagrams and the archived signed bodies. GPG validity is taken from preexisting page metadata, not newly reverified. This is an audit of a reported observation, not evidence of a decryption method or intended connection to the solved wording. Human review pending.

scope.representation: The exact ASCII bodies of four extracted PGP-verified OutGuess messages, with verification status read from page metadata; separately the printed LP1-05 mixed square converted by GP values and LP1-16 decimal square.
scope.procedure: Hash-check all inputs, locate each unique seven-line 16-column ASCII diagram, remove only its top/bottom rows and first/last character of other rows, and compare the resulting interior bytes and parsed decimal values in page order. Separately remove one-cell perimeters from both visible five-by-five squares to exclude that reading.
scope.parameters: Exactly LP1-10–13 in page order; one-character ASCII perimeter; no rotation, reflection, recoding or searched crop. The alternate LP1-05/16 check uses the canonical GP table from data/index.json.
scope.exclusions: No new GPG verification, no interpretation of the 3301 border sequence as a cipher, no LP2 text transformation, no claim that the common three-by-three is a magic square.

lp1-section-balance.title: LP1 column balance with section-preserving shuffles
lp1-section-balance.question: Does the fixed 464-word arrangement retain unusually low column-mean variance when each section keeps its own word lengths and occupied slots?
lp1-section-balance.finding: The observed score stays 128256. With section distributions and slots preserved, 88 of 49,999 shuffled scores are at or below it (plus-one lower-tail estimate 0.00178). The observed variance is 25.21% of this model’s exact expectation; the unrestricted baseline was 25.15%.
lp1-section-balance.limitations: Previously selected arrangement and known baseline. This is a model-sensitivity comparison, not independent or exploration-adjusted evidence. Both nulls destroy sentence syntax. No intent, grille or decryption claim; human review pending.

scope.representation: Archived ciphertext runes, headings and interrupting F retained. Join slash and newline wraps and consecutive pages within a section. Rune runs with internal apostrophes form one word; apostrophes count zero runes. Other non-runes delimit words. Never merge sections.
scope.procedure: Retain the baseline word vector and continuous 29-by-16 layout. Independently shuffle fresh copies within each of the four sections, preserving section slots. Compare integer scores proportional to column-mean variance and derive the constrained expectation exactly.
scope.parameters: 16 columns; 29 words per column; section sizes 45,124,208,87; 49,999 trials; Python random.Random seed 330146; lower tail including ties; (tail_count+1)/50000; threshold 0.05. Baseline arrangement and result were known before this frozen variant.
scope.exclusions: Other widths, section orders, sentence-preserving shuffles, coherent-prose comparisons, sentence removal, grille extraction, carrier matching, original-search multiplicity, independent confirmation, authorial intent and decryption.

lp1-section-order.title: LP1 column balance after searching section orders
lp1-section-order.question: How unusual is the flattest arrangement after searching all 24 orders of the four intact LP1 sections?
lp1-section-order.finding: The observed minimum is 128256. Of 49,999 within-section shuffle controls, 440 have a minimum no greater after searching the same 24 orders; plus-one estimate 0.00882.
lp1-section-order.limitations: Accounts only for the declared section-order search, not the earlier choice of word object, width or statistic. Cyclic classes and paired comparisons are not independent evidence. No intent or decryption claim; human review pending.

scope.representation: Archived ciphertext runes, headings and interrupting F retained. Join slash and newline wraps and consecutive pages within a section. Rune runs with internal apostrophes form one word; apostrophes count zero runes. Other non-runes delimit words. Never merge sections.
scope.procedure: Retain all 464 word lengths and continuous 29-by-16 layout. Search all 24 orders of the four intact sections and retain minimum Q. In each control shuffle lengths within sections, search the same 24 orders, and retain its minimum.
scope.parameters: 16 columns; section sizes 45,124,208,87; all 24 orders represented by six cyclic classes; 49,999 trials; Python random.Random seed 330146; lower tail including ties; (tail_count+1)/50000; threshold 0.05. Earlier fixed-order results known before this protocol.
scope.exclusions: Other widths, reversals, sentence removal, sentence-preserving shuffles, prose comparisons, original exploratory multiplicity, independent confirmation, authorial intent and decryption.

lp1-seven-word-825-census.title: LP1 seven-word GP-825 window census
lp1-seven-word-825-census.question: How many seven-word windows in solved LP1 have exactly 21 runes and a Gematria Primus sum of 825?
lp1-seven-word-825-census.finding: The declared LP1 corpus has 694 rune words and 652 section-internal seven-word windows. Exactly one meets both fixed conditions: warning word 9 (zero-based), YOU CNOW TO BE TRUE TEST THE, with 21 runes, GP sum 825 and index sum 232. The reported denominator 716 does not follow from these inputs.
lp1-seven-word-825-census.limitations: The numeric target and comparison phrase were selected during exploration. The one match is an exact census under this text layer, not an adjusted significance test or evidence that the proposed LP2 phrase is correct. The LP1-05 square cells are included as rune words.

scope.representation: Seven solved LP1 sections, decoded runes from published reading traces and word separators from archived rune text. No seven-word window crosses a section boundary.
scope.procedure: Enumerate all section-internal seven-word windows; count decoded runes and sum their GP prime values; retain windows with exactly 21 runes and sum 825.
scope.parameters: Seven consecutive words, 21 decoded runes, GP sum 825; no spelling expansion or alternative boundaries.
scope.exclusions: The proposed LP2 phrase and its rune spelling, cross-section windows, alternative LP1 layers, the original selection process, probability of intent and decryption.

lp1-width-selection.title: LP1 column balance after searching six widths
lp1-width-selection.question: Is the minimum normalized column imbalance unusually low after searching widths 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 and 64?
lp1-width-selection.finding: The observed minimum R is 4167/245948 at width 2. Of 49,999 controls, 6,035 have a minimum no greater; plus-one estimate 0.12072.
lp1-width-selection.limitations: Calibrates minimum R over six declared widths, not selection of the smallest fixed-width p-value or all historical exploration. Unrestricted shuffles do not preserve sentences or section distributions. No intent or decryption claim; human review pending.

scope.representation: Archived ciphertext runes, headings and interrupting F retained. Join slash and newline wraps and consecutive pages within a section. Rune runs with internal apostrophes form one word; apostrophes count zero runes. Other non-runes delimit words. Never merge sections.
scope.procedure: Keep the original four-section word order. For each width 2,4,8,16,32,64, assign word i to column i modulo width without padding. Calculate weighted column imbalance divided by its exact unrestricted-permutation expectation; select the minimum R. Repeat all six widths in every shuffled control.
scope.parameters: 49,999 unrestricted fresh-copy shuffles; Python Random seed 330146; exact rational comparisons; lower tail with ties; plus-one correction; threshold 0.05. Partial final rows retained. Original width-16 result and qualitative width observations known before this protocol.
scope.exclusions: Other widths; section reordering; start rotations; padding; within-section or sentence-preserving nulls; choosing the smallest fixed-width p-value; original exploratory multiplicity; authorial intent; decryption.

lp1-word-length-balance.title: LP1: the 464-word table and column balance
lp1-word-length-balance.question: Does the stated ordered 464-word object have unusually low variance among 16 column means under unrestricted permutations of its fixed word lengths?
lp1-word-length-balance.finding: All 464 word lengths reproduce from the archived runes. The sixteen column averages are unusually even under the stated shuffle model: their variance is 25.15% of its expectation. Only 54 of 49,999 shuffles were at least as even (corrected lower-tail p=0.0011). A full rerun and independent checks agree.
lp1-word-length-balance.limitations: This is an explored, selected arrangement. The p-value does not adjust for the original search and is not the probability of coincidence or intent. Unrestricted shuffling destroys sentence and section structure; it is not a coherent-prose comparison. Reported corpus and carrier findings remain unverified. Human review pending.

scope.representation: Archived ciphertext runes, headings and interrupting F retained. Join slash and newline wraps and consecutive pages within a section. Rune runs with internal apostrophes form one word; apostrophes count zero runes. Other non-runes delimit words. Never merge sections.
scope.procedure: Concatenate Warning, Welcome, first koan and second koan in that order; count native runes per word. Compare all 464 values with the supplied vector. Fill 29 rows of 16 columns across rows without resetting at sections. Measure population variance of the 16 column means and divide by its exact finite-population shuffle expectation. Each trial freshly copies and uniformly shuffles the fixed 464 lengths; compare integer scores proportional to variance.
scope.parameters: 16 columns; 29 words per column; 49,999 shuffles; Python random.Random seed 330146; lower tail including ties; (tail_count+1)/50000; threshold 0.05. Arrangement and approximate ratio were known before the frozen simulation plan.
scope.exclusions: Other widths, section orders, constrained shuffles, prose corpus comparisons, sentence removal, section cancellation, grille extraction, carrier matching, original-search multiplicity, authorial intent and decryption.

lp2-00-02-lag35-selection.title: The LP2 opening section’s lag-35 peak
lp2-00-02-lag35-selection.question: Is the 35-rune repetition gap on the opening pages a real periodic clue?
lp2-00-02-lag35-selection.finding: The highest score is at lag 35: 42/694 equal pairs, z=3.759. Eighty-two of 999 complete-scan control maxima meet or exceed it (plus-one proportion 83/1000); lags 70, 105 and 140 show no comparable recurrence.
lp2-00-02-lag35-selection.limitations: Lag 35 was noticed in the source after scanning many lags; a fixed-lag tail would be misleading. Step-shuffling preserves the exact adjacent-difference inventory but is not an encryption model. This conditional scan correction does not cover other data choices or weak periodic signals.

scope.representation: The 729 GP rune indices in printed LP2-00–02 order; punctuation and separators are omitted.
scope.procedure: Count equal symbols at each lag 1–242 and standardize against 1/29. Shuffle the observed modular adjacent-difference inventory 999 times; reconstruct each sequence from the first original rune, rerun the complete lag scan, and compare its selected maximum with the manuscript selected maximum. Also record the predetermined-lag-35 tail and a planted period-35 positive check.
scope.parameters: 729 runes; 242 tested lags; 999 random.Random(3301) step permutations; ties count as meeting the observed statistic; planted period 35 with 55% independent replacements.
scope.exclusions: Other sections, lags 243+, different transcription, language scores, alternate coincidence definitions, pre/post-transform layers, and broad selection outside this one section.

lp2-15-mobius-panel.title: Arithmetic Möbius values of the LP2-15 panel
lp2-15-mobius-panel.question: What does the arithmetic Möbius function return for all sixteen printed LP2-15 panel numbers?
lp2-15-mobius-panel.finding: The exact operation produces rows 0000, −1−1−1+1, 0000 and 0000. Twelve values have a squared prime factor; the four nonzero values are squarefree.
lp2-15-mobius-panel.limitations: This is a deterministic transform audit of a reported idea, not a solving experiment. The supplied transcript does not preserve the referenced image, and no continuation into a cipher operation is stated.

scope.representation: All 16 printed decimal cells in the original 4×4 page order, taken from the hashed archived page record.
scope.procedure: Factor each positive integer and evaluate arithmetic μ(n) by the prime-square and parity rules; independently check by square-divisor enumeration.
scope.parameters: One fixed arithmetic function; every cell; original rows and columns; no traversal-dependent output.
scope.exclusions: The missing source output image, 3301-derived values, a conjectured key or rune-shift rule, plaintext, and statistical significance.

lp2-15-prime-gap-cycle.title: LP2-15 prime gaps: does the modulo-28 tail repeat?
lp2-15-prime-gap-cycle.question: Do the supplied LP2-15 Fibonacci-indexed prime gaps repeat the final modulo-28 tail 8,20,10,6 under the same fixed generator?
lp2-15-prime-gap-cycle.finding: The shown 8,20,10,6 tail occurs exactly once at gap positions 12–15. The first continuation is 5660 mod 28 = 4, not 8; none of eight new residues matches the fixed period-four prediction at its position.
lp2-15-prime-gap-cycle.limitations: This rejects only the period-four continuation of the supplied arithmetic tail under the established Fibonacci prime-index generator. Modulus 28 is unexplained and no decoding rule was supplied; other panel-derived operations are outside this test.

scope.representation: The user-supplied derived 4×4 prime matrix in source.json, checked against the established LP2-15 panel construction; not the printed panel values themselves.
scope.procedure: Verify the 16 Fibonacci-indexed primes and 15 shown gaps, count exact four-number tail occurrences, then extend the same generator by eight distinct Fibonacci prime indices and compare a fixed period-four prediction.

scope.representation: The printed 4×4 decimal panel and all three 4×4 source arrays preserved in plan.json, including one question mark.
scope.procedure: Apply phi to printed prime cells, enumerate 3301 ± each result, independently compute prime ordinals and compare the posted predecessor-Fibonacci gaps without repairing them.
scope.parameters: All sixteen image-order cells; base 3301; both signs logged; zero-based prime indices; source-stated cells compared individually. No rune operation.

scope.representation: Archived Unicode prefix before the first period, retaining 16 runes and including enlarged initial; standard GP first 29 primes; explicit K-to-C and TH spellings for the phrase.
scope.procedure: Recount each heading rune and word sum; encode the named phrase under one-TH and split-TH conventions; compute an explicitly hypothetical A-to-F sensitivity without correcting any source.
scope.parameters: One 16-rune heading; phrase encodings 15 and 16 runes; one 95-point glyph substitution sensitivity; no search or statistical significance test.

lp2-31-periodic-ioc.title: LP2-31: periodic IoC for periods 2-20
lp2-31-periodic-ioc.question: Does the maximum pooled column IoC over periods 2-20 exceed the fixed-multiset shuffle reference?
lp2-31-periodic-ioc.finding: 269 archived runes; unique maximum at period 13, 216/5300. Across 999 shuffles, 213 maxima meet or exceed it; p=0.214, not below the declared 0.05 threshold.
lp2-31-periodic-ioc.limitations: Only LP2-31, complete archived stream, periods 2-20. Null preserves counts but not local structure. No adjustment for page selection or prior work. No cipher classification or key recovered.

scope.representation: 269 archived runes; headings included; non-alphabet characters removed; no corrections.

lp2-31-row-shuffle-ioc.title: LP2-31: periodic IoC with within-row shuffles

scope.representation: 269 archived runes; headings included; non-alphabet characters removed; no corrections.

lp2-32-message-grid.title: LP2-32: grid sums and the 2016 message file

scope.representation: All 121 alphabet runes in archived LP2-32 order, stripped of separators and filled left-to-right into 11 rows of 11; Gematria Primus prime values.

lp2-39-header-cribs.title: LP2-39: twenty proposed red-header cribs

scope.representation: One inferred complete 14-rune word [37,51), zero-based page-rune indices including headings. lp2-53-red-equality-invariants.title: Equality structure of the LP2-53 red passage
lp2-53-red-equality-invariants.question: Is the red passage statistically different from the rest of its page?
lp2-53-red-equality-invariants.finding: Red IoC is 0.0298 with 26 distinct runes; 2,492 archived solved-reading windows have minimum IoC 0.0400 and at most 23 unique runes. Red IoC lies within 78 black-text window values on LP2-53. Its zero adjacent repeats also occur in 21.55% of 10,000 red-rune shuffles.

scope.representation: Original LP2-53 image and pinned transcription; red rune ordinals 128–178 inclusive (last rune of line 6 plus all of lines 7–9), excluding punctuation/artwork. Eight archived decoded GP output-index sections, omitting LP2-56 hash target.
scope.procedure: Compute 51-rune red IoC, adjacent equal pairs and unique count; compare with all length-51 windows in eight solved GP sections and 78 same-page black-prefix windows; shuffle the red indices 10,000 times for the adjacent-repeat order control.
scope.parameters: 51 red runes, 2,492 overlapping solved-section windows, 78 overlapping black-page windows, 10,000 seeded red shuffles.
scope.exclusions: Key or crib searches, alternative span boundaries, literal English-letter controls, LP2-56 hash target, external corpora and any inference of a solved message.

lp2-53-red-known-keys.question: Has the long red passage on LP2-53 been attacked separately?
lp2-53-red-known-keys.finding: Neither known LP1 key made the red passage resemble the English reading controls. Its best score was ordinary: 460 of 999 shuffled passages scored at least as well after the same 42-setting search.
lp2-53-red-known-keys.limitations: This checks only the Welcome and second-koan keys on the 51 red runes, at every starting phase and in both arithmetic directions. Other keys, interruptions and non-English readings were not tested.

scope.representation: Original LP2-53 JPEG color boundary; archived GP29 rune transcription. Red rune ordinals 128–178 zero-based, 51 runes. Word separators and line wraps do not advance a repeating key.
scope.procedure: For each of the documented Welcome and second-koan key vectors, decode the red rune indices under every phase and both signs. Score canonical GP transliteration with the pinned English quadgram model. Compare the best of all 42 against best-of-42 scores for 999 seeded rune-order shuffles. Gate first on nine solved 51-rune readings, their 200 shuffles each, and nine planted two-key encipherments.
scope.parameters: Two key lengths 8 and 13, 42 phase/sign settings; score threshold −5.5; 999 family-wise shuffled red controls; nine known-reading and nine planted controls.
scope.exclusions: No key from unsolved text, no keyskip/interrupter rules, no cross-page state, no non-English scoring, no inference from the artwork, and no general exclusion of Vigenère or other cipher families.

lp2-54-55-autokey-reset.title: LP2-54–55: reset ciphertext state at selected F runes
lp2-54-55-autokey-reset.question: Does the reset interruption rule produce an unusually high maximum periodic IoC across the declared 64 masks and periods 2–30?
lp2-54-55-autokey-reset.finding: Period 13 is the largest observed score, but the winning configuration selects no interruptions. Its pooled IoC is about 0.04748. The complete mask-and-period search reaches at least this value in 543 of 999 shuffled inputs (corrected p=0.544); the peak is not unusual under this comparison.
lp2-54-55-autokey-reset.limitations: New explicit implementation, not a rerun of unavailable source scripts. The null fixes F locations and rune counts while destroying other order. This tests one chosen statistic and scope; it does not rule out autokey, interruptions or period 13 in general. Both modes have the same observed winner and are not independent confirmations. Human review pending.

scope.representation: Archived rune indices, headings retained, punctuation removed; concatenate LP2-54 then LP2-55 without resetting state.
scope.procedure: P_i=(C_i-previous_ciphertext) mod 29; update previous_ciphertext=C_i. Unselected F behaves normally. Score the compact output after selected Fs are removed. Selected F is emitted unchanged, excluded from scored output, and sets previous ciphertext to zero. Sum ordered equal-symbol pairs within residue columns divided by sum ordered pairs within those columns. Maximize across all masks and periods; exact ratio comparisons. Keep all six F positions fixed. Independently permute the remaining non-F ciphertext multiset, freshly copied each trial. Repeat the complete mask-and-period search for each trial. This conditions on F positions, rune counts and length; it is not an English-text model.
scope.parameters: Initial ciphertext state 0; modulus 29; all 64 subsets of six F positions; all periods 2–30 inclusive; 1,856 configurations per input. 999 shuffles; random.Random seed 330154; upper tail with ties and (count+1)/1000. Threshold 0.05. Bonferroni correction for the two planned reset/skip variants.
scope.exclusions: Plaintext autokey; Other interruption symbols; Arbitrary primers or keys; Heading removal; Page-local state resets; Other period ranges; Language-score or plaintext claims; Significance of original exploratory search.

lp2-54-55-word-square.title: LP2-54–55: the 8×8 word arrangement
lp2-54-55-word-square.question: Do the final two pages contain 64 non-heading words, and does that count specify a labyrinth route?
lp2-54-55-word-square.finding: The 64-word arrangement reproduces after removing the two opening tokens. Its 48/16 page split gives a six-row/two-row boundary. The count leaves multiple routes and no output operation.

scope.representation: Archived word-token export, independently reconstructed from both page transcriptions; first two opening tokens excluded.
scope.procedure: Count remaining words by page of start, arrange in manuscript order as eight columns, and enumerate eight simple inward-spiral variants.
scope.parameters: One 66-word source span; two opening tokens excluded; 64 remaining cells; eight fixed routes without scoring.

lp2-54-header-dictionary.title: LP2-54: dictionary check for simple autokey cribs
lp2-54-header-dictionary.question: Does a simple autokey turn the LP2-54 red header into an English word?
lp2-54-header-dictionary.finding: Zero of six A/I/O by feedback outputs has an eight-rune corpus match. The same six checks on each of 13 printed 1+8-rune pairs across LP2-00–55 yield zero matches; both planted A MOUNTAIN controls recover. This excludes only the specified literal rules and corpus.

This is a new bounded test, not the full reported C/K/D-function search. Other alphabets, spellings, word boundaries, feedback lags, interruption rules and cipher layers remain untested.

scope.representation: Original LP2-00–55 rune texts; printed adjacent one-rune and eight-rune word pairs within a page. Primary target is the nine red runes at the beginning of LP2-54.
scope.procedure: For A, I and O first-rune cribs, decode all eight later runes under ciphertext feedback P[i]=C[i]-C[i-1] or plaintext feedback P[i]=C[i]-P[i-1], modulo 29. Look up the exact resulting eight-rune GP string in the pinned corpus, aliasing its alternate J rune to manuscript J. Apply the same six checks to all same-length visible pairs. Plant A MOUNTAIN with primer seven under both rules as a positive control.
scope.parameters: Canonical zero-based 29-rune GP order; three first-rune cribs; two one-step feedback modes; no reset at the word break. Pinned 138,466-row corpus at revision 9c10cafce02e512840cc9e173127930594a56281.
scope.exclusions: Other reported C/K/D functions, phonetic aliases, extra substitutions, changed word boundaries, other feedback lags, F interruptions, other dictionaries, statistical significance and full-page plaintext claims.

lp2-54-header-feedback.title: LP2-54: fixed ciphertext and plaintext feedback on the red header
lp2-54-header-feedback.question: What do the two explicit one-step feedback rules produce for the nine red runes when the first plaintext rune is A, I or O?
lp2-54-header-feedback.finding: The exact red cipher indices are 24,19,21,23,27,2,14,10,19. For A/I/O first-rune cribs, ciphertext feedback always makes the following eight labels A TH TH R R EO AE N. Plaintext feedback gives three different eight-rune outputs. The source's two named clocks therefore cannot be substituted for each other, and the simple cases do not establish a header reading.
lp2-54-header-feedback.limitations: The source proposes many unspecified functions and possible words; this bounded run implements only the two explicit one-step recurrences. It has no language score or calibrated null, and does not test whether another layer turns the output into text. Human review pending.

scope.representation: Archived 232-rune LP2-54 stream in canonical zero-based GP order, with the first nine red runes checked against the literal source prefix; punctuation has no cipher position.
scope.procedure: For each primer 0–28, decrypt the entire stream by P0=C0-k modulo 29 and then either P_i=C_i-C_(i-1) or P_i=C_i-P_(i-1) modulo 29. Re-encrypt every output and independently verify every saved equation. Compare the six outputs whose first rune is A, I or O.
scope.parameters: 29 primers × 2 recurrences = 58 complete outputs of 232 runes; one continuous stream, no word or row reset; one-rune ciphertext or plaintext feedback; no adaptive key or candidate selection.
scope.exclusions: Eight-rune dictionary census; other C/K/D functions; alphabet permutation; lag greater than one; interruption choices; a second encryption layer; language scoring; a claim that all autokey variants fail.

lp2-56-aligned-digest-blocks.title: Aligned digest blocks in the 256-byte grid payload
lp2-56-aligned-digest-blocks.question: Could the 256-byte grid contain hashes of known puzzle files or text?
lp2-56-aligned-digest-blocks.finding: No digest of the 324 distinct candidate byte strings equals any complete aligned block of the 256-byte payload from LP2-49–51. The seven algorithms made 16,848 exact comparisons. All seven first-and-last-block planted controls passed.
lp2-56-aligned-digest-blocks.limitations: Only the specified candidate bytes, seven algorithms and non-overlapping blocks beginning at byte zero were tested. Sliding offsets, bit shifts, hash truncation, padding, changed encodings and other payload readings remain outside scope. The result does not identify the grid's meaning or evaluate the printed LP2-56 target as a block.

scope.representation: The resolved 256-byte payload from the LP2-49–51 grid, divided at byte zero into non-overlapping complete blocks of 16, 32 or 64 bytes. Inputs are 412 named preserved-artifact variants representing 324 distinct byte strings.
scope.procedure: Verify all original candidate-file and payload hashes; hash each unique candidate once under each algorithm; compare exact output bytes with every aligned block of equal size. Independently rebuild inputs and search block-to-digest in the checker. Plant each known control digest at the first and last aligned block.
scope.parameters: MD5 on sixteen 16-byte blocks; SHA-256, SHA3-256 and BLAKE2s-256 on eight 32-byte blocks; SHA-512, SHA3-512 and BLAKE2b-512 on four 64-byte blocks. 324 unique inputs × 52 algorithm/block comparisons = 16,848 comparisons; 2,268 digest computations.
scope.exclusions: No overlapping windows, offsets other than zero, bit shifts, truncated or reversed digests, padding, additional byte transforms, other input corpora, other algorithms or alternate payload extraction.

lp2-56-four-md5-target-blocks.title: Four MD5 blocks in the printed LP2-56 target
lp2-56-four-md5-target-blocks.question: Could the LP2-56 number be four MD5 hashes?
lp2-56-four-md5-target-blocks.finding: None of the four printed 16-byte blocks matches MD5 of any of 324 distinct candidate byte strings. One digest per unique input, compared with four blocks, gives 1,296 exact comparisons; 412 names include aliases of identical bytes. First- and last-block planted controls passed, as did the independent recount.
lp2-56-four-md5-target-blocks.limitations: Only this exact byte-zero block partition, MD5 and the frozen preserved-artifact corpus were tested. It does not evaluate the unknown web page, arbitrary new inputs, modified bytes, other digests, offsets or encodings. No historical MD5-block claim is attributed or replayed.

scope.representation: The archived LP2-56 reading's 128 hexadecimal characters decoded as 64 bytes, divided into four consecutive complete 16-byte blocks; the same 412 named artifact variants and 324 unique byte strings as the frozen earlier corpus.
scope.procedure: Verify printed target and source-file hashes; compute MD5 once for each unique candidate byte string; compare all 16 bytes at each of four fixed block positions; independently reconstruct inputs and check planted controls.
scope.parameters: Four byte-zero-aligned 16-byte target blocks; MD5 only; 324 × 4 = 1,296 exact comparisons. Known MD5('abc') vector and first/last synthetic block controls.
scope.exclusions: Unknown web pages or other corpus inputs, byte permutations, encodings beyond the frozen variants, truncated or reversed digests, offsets, alternative hash algorithms and hypotheses about the four-part message.

lp2-56-internal-artifact-hashes.title: LP2-56: hashes of preserved manuscript artifacts
lp2-56-internal-artifact-hashes.question: Have we tried hashing the original manuscript files against page 56?
lp2-56-internal-artifact-hashes.finding: The five printed rows total 128 hex digits (64 bytes). None of the 75 original JPEGs, 75 raw rune transcriptions under four newline rules, nine stored literal sections under those rules, or one resolved grid payload matches that value under the three run hash algorithms. One of the nine literal sections is LP2-56's own printed hash, not a decoded reading.
lp2-56-internal-artifact-hashes.limitations: The 412 listed variants contain 324 distinct byte strings. The source JPEG bytes used in an older reported SHA-512/BLAKE2 check were not preserved in that source; this replay uses Liberpedia's pinned originals. Whirlpool and Streebog were unavailable and were not run. Other artifacts, encodings, and transformations are outside this test.

scope.representation: The target is LP2-56's five printed hexadecimal rows. Inputs are all 75 preserved manuscript JPEGs, all 75 raw page strings, nine joined stored literal sections (including the LP2-56 hash itself) and the 256-byte resolved grid payload. Exact source paths and hashes are in plan.json.
scope.procedure: Freeze exact input-file hashes and text-byte rules. Hash each resulting byte stream with three independently vector-checked 512-bit algorithms. Compare the complete 64-byte digest with the printed target.
scope.parameters: 412 candidate variants, including four LF/CRLF terminal-newline forms for text; 3 algorithms; 1,236 comparisons and 324 distinct byte strings.
scope.exclusions: No Whirlpool or Streebog implementation available; no remote URL bytes, historical source JPEG-byte identity, HTML, arbitrary padding, case changes, other encodings, or partial hash searches.

lp2-56-whirlpool-stribog.title: LP2-56: Whirlpool and Streebog-512 artifact hashes
lp2-56-whirlpool-stribog.question: Have Whirlpool and Streebog been checked against page 56?
lp2-56-whirlpool-stribog.finding: The 412 named variants contain 324 unique byte strings. Libgcrypt computed 648 unique Whirlpool/Streebog digests, then 1,236 full-value comparisons including the normal and RFC 6986 byte displays of Streebog. Zero matched the 64-byte target.
lp2-56-whirlpool-stribog.limitations: Inputs and four text-newline rules are exactly those of the prior internal-artifact hash matrix. RFC-display reversal changes only the presentation of Streebog's digest, not the input bytes or algorithm. Other inputs, keyed or salted hashes, arbitrary byte transforms and older Whirlpool revisions remain outside scope. The tested DLL is not bundled; another libgcrypt installation must pass the same controls.

scope.representation: Target: all five printed LP2-56 hexadecimal rows, totaling 64 bytes. Inputs: exactly the earlier pinned 75 manuscript JPEGs, 75 raw page strings × four byte forms, nine stored literal sections × four forms, and 256-byte resolved grid payload. Source plan SHA-256 is pinned in the new plan.
scope.procedure: Validate installed libgcrypt with a Whirlpool reference vector and two RFC 6986 Streebog-512 vectors. Hash 324 distinct byte strings once under each algorithm. Fan out to 412 named inputs; compare complete digest bytes, and for Streebog also their RFC-style byte-reversed display, with the complete target.
