scope.parameters: 324 distinct bytestrings, 412 named variants, two algorithms, 648 actual digest operations and 1,236 complete-value displayed comparisons.
scope.exclusions: No new artifact or encoding choices, digest prefixes, keyed/salted variants, input byte reversal, older Whirlpool-0/T revisions, or hash-to-address conversions.

lp2-alphabet-warning-prefix.title: LP2-00–55: fixed alphabet transforms against the warning opening
lp2-alphabet-warning-prefix.question: Do shifts, alphabet reversal, or whole-stream reversal recover the first 12 decoded warning runes at the start of an archived LP2-00–55 page?
lp2-alphabet-warning-prefix.finding: Alphabet shifts, Atbash-style reversals and backward text did not reproduce the warning’s 12-rune opening in any of 6,496 cases.
lp2-alphabet-warning-prefix.limitations: Only that one page-start opening was checked, with headings included. Other beginnings, later positions, row-wise reversals or broader substitution alphabets remain untested.

scope.representation: Complete archived rune streams, headings included; non-alphabet characters removed; no corrections.
scope.procedure: Choose original or reversed stream; compute output = (a × index + b) modulo 29. Compare only the first 12 output indices with the first 12 Atbash-decoded LP1-01 runes.
scope.parameters: a in {1, -1}; b in 0–28; 2 stream orders; 56 pages; 116 cases per page, 6496 total. Exact prefix equality at position zero; no early stopping.
scope.exclusions: Other openings or positions, heading removal, regional or line-wise reversal, arbitrary substitution alphabets, other affine multipliers, Vigenère, corrections and language scoring.

lp2-fibonacci-openings.title: LP2-00–55: Fibonacci shifts and repeated phases
lp2-fibonacci-openings.question: Does uninterrupted Fibonacci arithmetic recover any of nine fixed 12-rune openings at the start of an LP2-00–55 page?
lp2-fibonacci-openings.finding: Fibonacci shifts produced 1,540 distinct page outputs; none began with any of nine known 12-rune openings. Starting later repeats the same 14-term cycle under these rules.
lp2-fibonacci-openings.limitations: This test uses the standard Fibonacci seeds 0 and 1, with uninterrupted shifts restarting on each page. Other seeds, skips or plaintext beginnings remain untested.

scope.representation: All recognized runes in archived order, including headings. Ignore other characters. Empty pages contribute no candidates.
scope.procedure: Apply Fibonacci shifts F_0=0, F_1=1, F_(n+2)=F_(n+1)+F_n modulo 29, with both subtraction and addition. Compare the first 12 output indices with nine fixed known openings; retain full candidates.
scope.parameters: Offsets 0–28 inclusive; two directions; independent page reset; one term per rune; no interruptions. 55 rune-bearing pages, 3190 candidates, 28710 comparisons.
scope.exclusions: Other beginnings, offsets above 28, interruptions, heading removal, reversed input, word or row resets, cross-page carry, other numerical schedules and language scoring.

lp2-filter-fingerprint-models.title: Does the missing-doublet pattern resemble a lag-one filter?
lp2-filter-fingerprint-models.question: Was the repeat-avoidance rule applied to the whole rune stream?
lp2-filter-fingerprint-models.finding: Independent input measurements reproduce the 86/12,955 lag-one repeat rate, 3.488% lag-2–8 equality, 0.936 window-58 chi-square per degree of freedom, and 4/86 line-crossing repeats. In the source's 200-replicate matched-control ladder, models with extra recent-symbol avoidance or window rebalancing are distinguishable and rejected; the line-reset model is also distinguishable and rejected. The no-extra-effect hand rung has combined discrimination power 0.110 and remains unresolved.
lp2-filter-fingerprint-models.limitations: This is a bounded comparison among specified generators, not proof of a literal machine implementation or entropy source. Controls are calibrated to the observed adjacent-repeat rate. The model ladder does not cover every human strategy; a continuous hand-applied lag-one rule on machine-like symbols is observationally equivalent here. The source counts 648 occupied slash/page line ordinals, whereas the text contains 594 nonempty physical lines.

scope.representation: First 55 nonempty percentage-delimited LP2 segments of pinned UTF-8 rune transcription, concatenated in page order; slash and page markers retained for line-scope comparisons. 12,956 runes, 55 pages, 594 nonempty physical lines, 648 occupied source line ordinals.
scope.procedure: Independently parse raw runes and reproduce lag equalities, repeat gaps, window chi-square, line-crossing doublets and page dispersion. Freshly run the pinned source fingerprint/controls script with 200 replicates, all controls calibrated to the manuscript lag-one repeat rate, and verify its gate, powered model ladder and scope test.
scope.parameters: 29-rune alphabet; lags 1–8; windows 29/58/116/290; 200 source replicates per modeled family; six hand-model rungs plus uniform, continuous filter and line-reset controls; acceptance interval central 95%; minimum discriminator power 0.80.
scope.exclusions: Other transcription layers, alternative human or machine generators not in the source ladder, an exact cipher/key, the physical identity of the author or pad entropy source.

lp2-known-vigenere-keys.title: LP2-00–55: two known Vigenère keys and nine openings
lp2-known-vigenere-keys.question: Do either of the two known Vigenere keys recover a 12-rune known-reading opening at the start of an LP2-00–55 page under uninterrupted repeating-key decoding?
lp2-known-vigenere-keys.finding: The Welcome and second-koan keys did not recover any of nine known 12-rune openings. Every starting position in each key and both addition and subtraction were tested.
lp2-known-vigenere-keys.limitations: The keys ran continuously and restarted on each page. Other keys, pauses or skips in the key, and different beginnings remain untested.

scope.representation: Complete archived rune stream including headings; remove non-alphabet characters; no corrections or reversal.
scope.procedure: Apply each known key with every phase, both addition and subtraction modulo 29. Compare the first 12 output indices against each of nine known-opening vectors. Retain complete candidates.
scope.parameters: Two vectors of lengths 8 and 13; all 21 phases; two signs; 56 pages; 2352 candidates and 21168 exact comparisons. Reset per page. No interruptions.
scope.exclusions: Other keys, interruption placement, noninitial positions, heading removal, cross-page carry, alternative alphabets, transposition and language scoring.

lp2-pad-payload-target.title: Using LP2 as a key for the 256-byte payload
lp2-pad-payload-target.question: Can the manuscript itself unlock the payload from pages 49–51?
lp2-pad-payload-target.finding: None of the eight settings reached the English-score threshold. In a separate check, the search preferred three wrong runes over the known answer. This result does not rule out using LP2 as a key.
lp2-pad-payload-target.limitations: Only the stated payload and key-skipping rules were tested. Its bytes come from a preserved canonical file; the missing historical input was not recovered.

scope.representation: The same 12,956 source LP2 rune indices supply the key. The committed canon_256 bytes, explicitly supplied at payload.bin, are reduced modulo 29 to form a 256-rune ciphertext; unavailable historical payload bytes are not recovered.
scope.procedure: Preserve source beam400/max_skip3 at offset zero for the eight payload labels. Reproduce original controls and 40 primary rows, then merge 48 labels in source order and apply the unchanged selected-top-five null policy. Proceed only as diagnostic completion under the pre-target amendment because the stronger exact-recovery gate failed.
scope.parameters: Four LP2 variants times two signs: eight labels, six effective signed keys; 256 payload runes; one new 200-shuffle panel shared by two selected aliases, three selected old null receipts reused. Eight 256-rune plants plus the original source plant; source 80% character gate and strict exact-rune gate reported separately.
scope.exclusions: No historical payload.bin identification, other payloads, offsets, encodings, key/skip models, repaired AN END bytes, full-search significance, plaintext confirmation or power-validated model exclusion. Only the best new source case receives a separate post-target normalized terminal-beam audit.

lp2-page-join-lag-six-sensitivity.title: Do page-break word joins change the six-rune pattern?
lp2-page-join-lag-six-sensitivity.question: How much do the 32 rune-to-rune LP2 page edges change word-internal lag-six affine counts if they are joined instead of split?
lp2-page-join-lag-six-sensitivity.finding: Splitting gives 2,928 tokens, 1,267 lag-six opportunities, 77 matches and 63 within-word adjacent doublets. Joining gives 2,896 tokens, 1,290 opportunities, 80 matches and 63 doublets. The rune count remains 12,956.
lp2-page-join-lag-six-sensitivity.limitations: A rune on both sides of a page edge is not evidence of an intended word join. Both variants are bounds under one archived transcription and one punctuation rule. The published shuffle reference was not recalculated for the joined variant.

scope.representation: Archived raw page text and stored 29-rune order; 55 adjacent page edges. No new image adjudication of word joins.
scope.procedure: Use the same hyphen/period word delimiters as the published lag-six experiment, first forcing page breaks and then concatenating pages; count word tokens, six-rune affine matches and adjacent doublets. List each edge's contribution and independently reparse structured page records.
scope.parameters: LP2-00–55, 29 runes, lag 6, formula c′=24−2c modulo 29; slash and newline are layout only; page breaks either always split or join when both ends are runes.
scope.exclusions: Alternative punctuation rules, page image adjudication, revised transcription layers, a new null-model test, cipher identification.

lp2-page-pair-alignment.title: One LP2 page as another page’s key
lp2-page-pair-alignment.question: Can one ciphertext page act as another page’s key?
lp2-page-pair-alignment.finding: The observed maximum IoC is 0.0446 (LP2-29 minus LP2-55 across 76 runes). In 256 shared conditional-shuffle controls, 235 global maxima were at least that high; empirical global p=0.9183.
lp2-page-pair-alignment.limitations: IoC measures symbol concentration, not readable plaintext. The result only assesses zero-offset, common-prefix, nonrepeating direct addition/subtraction; other alignments or cipher layers remain untested.

scope.representation: Full GP29 rune streams including headings from 55 rune-bearing LP2-00–55 pages; for each pair use the first min(page lengths) runes.
scope.procedure: For every unordered page pair compute aligned sum and difference modulo29, measure output IoC, and compare the global maximum to 256 seeded shared page shuffles within page-length-delimited bands that preserve every compared-prefix histogram.
scope.parameters: 1,485 distinct pairs × 2 arithmetic operations = 2,970 outputs; 256 global-max null trials; seed 330129.
scope.exclusions: Known-opening cribs, other offsets, page reversals and reorders, repeating or interrupted page keys, later positions beyond the common prefix, alternative arithmetic and language scoring.

lp2-page-pair-english.title: Can one LP2 page decode another?
lp2-page-pair-english.question: Have we tried using another LP2 page as the key?
lp2-page-pair-english.finding: The best eligible stream is LP2-18 minus LP2-02 (201 runes; score −6.802). In 193 of 256 conditional page-shuffle full searches, the best pair and operation scored at least as high (global add-one 194/257≈0.755).
lp2-page-pair-english.limitations: Only direct zero-offset, nonrepeating A+B, A−B and B−A modulo 29 with English scoring were tested. Shifts, repeats, other layers, other languages and clue-selected pairings remain untested. The catalog is an idea list, not proof of a historical attempt.

scope.representation: Canonical GP29 rune indices, including headings, from all 55 rune-bearing LP2-00–55 text transcriptions; independent check re-parses structured page JSON.
scope.procedure: Align every unordered page pair at rune zero to the shorter length. Compute A+B, A−B, and B−A modulo 29; score GP Latin labels with a fixed English quadgram model. Compare best eligible stream to 256 maxima of complete shared conditional-band page-shuffle searches.
scope.parameters: 1,485 pairs × three operations = 4,455 streams, of which 4,136 have ≥100 Latin quadgrams. Each of 256 controls uses Random(33017127+t). Three synthetic planted English outputs check exact arithmetic recovery and the scorer.
scope.exclusions: Offsets, reverse streams, repeated page keys, other operations, changed page order or transcription, later decryption layers, non-English output and historical-negative claims.

lp2-panel-prime-openings.title: LP2-00–55: LP2-15 spiral-prime shifts
lp2-panel-prime-openings.question: Does the sixteen-prime LP2-15 spiral, repeated as modulo-29 shifts, recover any of nine fixed 12-rune openings on LP2-00–55?
lp2-panel-prime-openings.finding: Zero fixed-opening matches among 1760 distinct complete page outputs. The independent checker reconstructs all sixteen primes from the panel ledger and inverts every transformed rune.
lp2-panel-prime-openings.limitations: The shift operation and cyclic repetition are added assumptions, not instructions printed on LP2-15. Only nine fixed 12-rune beginnings are tested; this does not rule out other uses of the panel or other cipher classes. Computational review only; human review pending.

scope.representation: All recognized runes in archived order, including headings. Ignore other characters. Empty pages contribute no candidates.
scope.procedure: Repeat the sixteen panel-derived primes in spiral order as modulo-29 shifts, with addition and subtraction, and compare first twelve output indices to nine fixed openings.
scope.parameters: Offsets 0–15; two directions; independent page reset; one term per rune; no interruptions. 55 rune-bearing pages, 1760 cases and 15840 comparisons.
scope.exclusions: Other page starts, noncyclic use, reversed or reordered spiral, prime-index values, interruptions, heading removal, word or row resets, cross-page carry and language scoring.

lp2-prime-minus-one-openings.title: LP2-00–55: prime-minus-one shifts and known openings
lp2-prime-minus-one-openings.question: Does uninterrupted prime-minus-one arithmetic recover any of nine fixed 12-rune openings at the start of an LP2-00–55 page?
lp2-prime-minus-one-openings.finding: Zero exact opening matches. Full rerun reproduced every saved candidate; an independent trial-division and inverse-arithmetic check audited all 3190 candidates and the 56-rune LP2-56 control.
lp2-prime-minus-one-openings.limitations: This tests nine specific initial openings, not general readability. Offsets 0–28 do not exhaust a nonrepeating prime sequence. The known LP2-56 interruption is not searched or transferred. Computational review only; human review pending.

scope.representation: All recognized runes in archived order, including headings. Ignore other characters. Empty pages contribute no candidates.
scope.procedure: Apply prime-minus-one shifts modulo 29, with both subtraction and addition. Compare the first 12 output indices with nine fixed known openings; retain full candidates.
scope.parameters: Offsets 0–28 inclusive; two directions; independent page reset; one term per rune; no interruptions. 55 rune-bearing pages, 3190 candidates, 28710 comparisons.
scope.exclusions: Other beginnings, offsets above 28, interruptions, heading removal, reversed input, word or row resets, cross-page carry, other numerical schedules and language scoring.

lp2-prime-openings.title: LP2-00–55: ordinary primes instead of primes minus one
lp2-prime-openings.question: Does uninterrupted prime arithmetic recover any of nine fixed 12-rune openings at the start of an LP2-00–55 page?
lp2-prime-openings.finding: None of the 3,190 outputs from adding or subtracting successive primes began with any of nine known 12-rune openings.
lp2-prime-openings.limitations: Only the first 29 starting points were checked, without skips. Ordinary-prime and prime-minus-one shifts differ by a constant alphabet shift, so these are closely related tests.

scope.representation: All recognized runes in archived order, including headings. Ignore other characters. Empty pages contribute no candidates.
scope.procedure: Apply prime shifts modulo 29, with both subtraction and addition. Compare the first 12 output indices with nine fixed known openings; retain full candidates.
scope.parameters: Offsets 0–28 inclusive; two directions; independent page reset; one term per rune; no interruptions. 55 rune-bearing pages, 3190 candidates, 28710 comparisons.
scope.exclusions: Other beginnings, offsets above 28, interruptions, heading removal, reversed input, word or row resets, cross-page carry, other numerical schedules and language scoring.

lp2-row-column-english.title: Do simple row or column routes reveal text?
lp2-row-column-english.question: Have we tried reading the full pages by rows and columns?
lp2-row-column-english.finding: The whole-output English-score comparison was inconclusive. LP2-22 supplied the highest score; 16 of 256 shuffled full searches scored at least as high.
lp2-row-column-english.limitations: This score comparison does not establish a decipherment or judge every route's readability. Other layouts, added cipher layers and other languages remain outside scope.

scope.representation: All 55 rune-bearing LP2-00–55 text pages as ragged, left-aligned source rows. The pinned 16-route trace is reused by the producer and rebuilt from structured page JSON by the checker.
scope.procedure: Score the full output of 16 pure row/column routes per page with canonical GP Latin quadgrams. This includes reversing the rune order within every archived row while keeping the rows in their original order, on LP2-15 and every other rune-bearing target page (row-first, forward outer direction, reversed inner direction, no alternation). Compare the best eligible route with 256 maxima of complete 880-route searches on shared within-page rune shuffles.
scope.parameters: 880 parameter routes, 848 with ≥100 English quadgrams; 256 shared full-route controls seeded 33017128–33017383; all 16 routes have exact inverse-permutation planted Welcome-reading controls.
scope.exclusions: Physical image alignment, diagonals, rectangle padding, spirals, arbitrary permutations, across-page transposition, added substitutions, non-English output and claims about all historical attempts.

lp2-row-column-routes.title: LP2-00–55: simple row and column reading routes
lp2-row-column-routes.question: Can reading the LP2-00–55 runes by rows or columns recover one of nine known passage openings without changing the runes?
lp2-row-column-routes.finding: None of the 880 routes matched any of nine fixed 12-rune openings. The routes include reversing rune order within each row while keeping row order unchanged.
lp2-row-column-routes.limitations: This opening test does not decide whether any output is English. Other beginnings, physical column alignments and added substitutions remain outside scope.

scope.representation: Keep every recognized rune including headings, grouped by archived source line. Ignore non-rune characters and lines with no runes. Retain original line and within-line rune positions. LP2-50 is retained as a zero-rune page, with no candidate routes. Left-align rune rows by within-row ordinal. Unequal row lengths remain unequal. Missing cells are skipped, not padded. Ordinal columns are not asserted to be physical image columns.
scope.procedure: Enumerate 16 row-first and column-first routes, both outer directions, both initial inner directions, and constant/alternating inner direction. This includes reversing the rune order within every archived row while keeping the rows in their original order, on LP2-15 and every other rune-bearing target page (row-first, forward outer direction, reversed inner direction, no alternation). Preserve every source position and compare the first 12 output indices with nine fixed known openings.
scope.parameters: 16 route configurations per nonempty page; 55 nonempty pages; 880 cases; 7920 exact opening comparisons. No substitution or later-position search.
scope.exclusions: Arbitrary column permutations, spiral paths, rectangular reflow, physical x-coordinate alignment, heading removal, substitution, alternative openings and other text regions.

lp2-row-emirp-sums.title: LP2-00–55: emirp row sums with the same page shuffles
lp2-row-emirp-sums.question: Do archived LP2-00–55 row sums contain more emirps than the same page shuffles used in the prime-sum baseline?
lp2-row-emirp-sums.finding: 41 emirp-valued rows; 539/999 shuffled totals meet or exceed 41, giving corrected upper-tail p=0.540. All baseline prime-count vectors reproduce.
lp2-row-emirp-sums.limitations: Global row-boundary count only. No evidence of excess under this model does not exclude deliberate individual sums or establish randomness. Uses the same shuffles as the prime baseline, not independent evidence. Human review pending.

scope.representation: Each nonempty archived text line with at least one recognized rune defines one row. Include headings. Remove non-alphabet characters; ignore rows with no recognized runes. No corrections or decryption. LP2-50 contributes zero eligible rows.
scope.procedure: Total number of rows whose prime-value sum is prime, has a prime base-ten decimal reversal, and differs from its reversal. One global statistic; per-page counts are descriptive only. Independently permute the full rune multiset within each page, then partition it using that page’s original row lengths. Preserve page counts and every row length, not words or per-row counts.
scope.parameters: 594 eligible rows; 56 declared pages, 55 with runic rows; 999 full-dataset trials; seed 330133; greater-than-or-equal upper tail; plus-one Monte Carlo correction; alpha 0.05.
scope.exclusions: Prime palindromes, prime ordinals, decoded text, arbitrary regions, changed spellings, other bases or boundaries and page-specific significance claims.

lp2-row-prime-sums.title: LP2-00–55: prime row sums against shuffled pages
lp2-row-prime-sums.question: Do the archived row boundaries on LP2-00–55 produce more prime-valued Gematria Primus row sums than within-page rune shuffles?
lp2-row-prime-sums.finding: Observed prime-row count 76; shuffled mean 83.786, range 60–115; 843/999 null totals at least observed. Corrected p=0.844, not below 0.05.
lp2-row-prime-sums.limitations: Pages, statistic and null are analyst choices motivated by existing prime-sum discussion, not a blind discovery. No correction for earlier or future alternative analyses. Archived boundaries were not visually reverified. This tests only a global excess, not a deficit or individual-row intent. Human review pending.

scope.representation: Each nonempty archived text line with at least one recognized rune defines one row. Include headings. Remove non-alphabet characters; ignore rows with no recognized runes. No corrections or decryption. LP2-50 contributes zero eligible rows.
scope.procedure: Total number of rows with a prime sum across all selected pages. One global statistic; per-page counts are descriptive only. Independently permute the full rune multiset within each page, then partition it using that page’s original row lengths. Preserve page counts and every row length, not words or per-row counts.
scope.parameters: 594 eligible rows; 56 declared pages, 55 with runic rows; 999 full-dataset trials; seed 330133; greater-than-or-equal upper tail; plus-one Monte Carlo correction; alpha 0.05.
scope.exclusions: Emirps, prime ordinals, decoded text, arbitrary regions, changed spellings, other boundaries and page-specific significance claims.

lp2-seven-page-square-fits.title: LP2-16–22’s 59×59 digit count
lp2-seven-page-square-fits.question: Is the reported 59×59 prime-digit total an exact and locally distinctive seven-page fit?
lp2-seven-page-square-fits.finding: The exact 59² arithmetic reproduces, and LP2-16–22 is the only exact square in the 50-window prime-digit sweep. Under one-based index digits LP2-41–47 gives 57².
lp2-seven-page-square-fits.limitations: Page range, width, representation and square criterion were considered after inspection. One square among these windows is not a chance probability or evidence for a unique route.

scope.representation: Every archived GP rune on LP2-00–55, converted to the decimal digit length of its prime value, with parallel rune/index-count alternatives.
scope.procedure: Count per page; sweep all contiguous seven-page windows; flag exact squares and compare three alternate representations.
scope.parameters: Seven-page width fixed; 50 windows ending no later than LP2-55; printed red runes included.
scope.exclusions: Other window widths, insertions, number encodings, matrix routes, keys and plaintext.

lp2-shifted-page-pair-differences.title: One page as another's key, at every long overlap
lp2-shifted-page-pair-differences.question: Do any two pages become unusually patterned when one is shifted and subtracted from the other?
lp2-shifted-page-pair-differences.finding: The strongest alignment, LP2-14 against LP2-35, is no stronger than results commonly found in shuffled pages: 77 of 128 shuffled searches matched or exceeded it.
lp2-shifted-page-pair-differences.limitations: Forward differences with overlap at least 120 runes and an IoC statistic only; this does not exclude general shared-key encryption.

scope.representation: Forward GP29 indices including headings from 55 nonempty LP2-00–55 pages; 52 have at least 120 runes.
scope.procedure: Exhaust all unordered page pairs and integer relative lags with>=120 overlap; direct difference modulo29; compare global maximum IoC to128 shared whole-page permutations.
scope.parameters: 1,326 pairs; 331,908 alignments (330,582 nonzero lags); minimum overlap 120; 128 nulls; seed 330120261024; no wrapping or reversal.
scope.exclusions: Shorter overlaps, page reversal, repeated/skipped key, plaintext-family exclusion, general key reuse, whole source S1/S2/S3 roadmap.

lp2-shifted-page-pair-english.title: Do shifted pages produce English?
lp2-shifted-page-pair-english.question: Do shifted sums or differences of two pages score like English?
lp2-shifted-page-pair-english.finding: None passed the fixed English-recognition test. The strongest output, from LP2-13 minus LP2-32, scored like results commonly found in shuffled pages. The known-reading tests recovered the intended text.
lp2-shifted-page-pair-english.limitations: Forward sum and both subtraction directions with at least 120-rune overlap, using one fixed English model. Other cipher layers and general shared-key encryption remain open.

scope.representation: Forward GP29 streams including headings from 55 nonempty LP2-00–55 pages; shifted overlaps of at least 120 runes; output scored as canonical GP Latin labels.
scope.procedure: Exhaust every eligible unordered pair and relative offset; score A+B, A-B and B-A modulo 29 with unchanged prior English scorer. Compare observed global best with 128 shared whole-page permutation search maxima.
scope.parameters: 1,326 pairs; 331,908 alignments; 995,724 streams, including 991,746 nonzero-offset streams and 3,978 baseline overlaps; at least 100 Latin quadgrams; fixed recognition gate -5.5; 128 null trials; seed 330120261025.
scope.exclusions: Overlap shorter than 120 runes, page reversal, wrapping, repeated or skipped key symbols, other arithmetic, altered transcription, word resets, additional cipher layers, other languages and general shared-key exclusion.

lp2-spacing-gap-audit.title: LP2-15 number-row spacing: a source-bound line-gap audit
lp2-spacing-gap-audit.question: Is the reported extra vertical gap before the fourth LP2-15 number row measurable on the original JPEG, and how does it compare with neighboring text rows?
lp2-spacing-gap-audit.finding: At threshold 160 the LP2-15 number-row gaps are 62, 61, 79 pixels. The final anomaly persists with the same 17-pixel separation at thresholds 100 and 200. Lower LP2-15 rune text has six 74-pixel gaps; selected LP2-14/16 text gaps are 73–75 pixels.
lp2-spacing-gap-audit.limitations: This verifies one reported line-gap observation, not the word-gap hypothesis or a binary channel. The numeric panel and runic controls use different content and layout, so their difference cannot identify typesetting cause. The source screenshots are not preserved in the supplied transcript.

scope.representation: Fixed source-image rectangles on the three hashed 2400×3600 JPEGs; vertical ink-row bands and blank interline rows, not text transcription.
scope.procedure: Threshold grayscale pixels, group ink rows into printed lines, list every line box and intervening blank-row count; independently rederive at the main threshold and repeat at two alternative thresholds.
scope.parameters: Rectangles, cutoff 160, five ink pixels per row, maximum 14 blank rows within a printed line, threshold sensitivity 100 and 200; all fixed in plan.json.
scope.exclusions: The absent forum screenshots and specific word-gap examples, bit interpretation, fallback-font mechanism, and any claim about LP2 plaintext.

lp2-totient-openings.title: LP2-00–55: totients of consecutive integers
lp2-totient-openings.question: Does uninterrupted consecutive-integer totient arithmetic recover any of nine fixed 12-rune openings at the start of an LP2-00–55 page?
lp2-totient-openings.finding: Adding or subtracting totients of consecutive integers produced 3,190 outputs; none began with any of nine known 12-rune openings.
lp2-totient-openings.limitations: Only the first 29 starting points were checked, with the sequence restarting on each page. Totients of rune values or sums, or different plaintext beginnings, require a different test.

scope.representation: All recognized runes in archived order, including headings. Ignore other characters. Empty pages contribute no candidates.
scope.procedure: Apply consecutive-integer totient shifts phi(j+s+1) modulo 29, with phi(1)=1 and both subtraction and addition. Compare the first 12 output indices with nine fixed known openings; retain full candidates.
scope.parameters: Offsets 0–28 inclusive; two directions; independent page reset; one term per rune; no interruptions. 55 rune-bearing pages, 3190 candidates, 28710 comparisons.
scope.exclusions: Other beginnings, offsets above 28, interruptions, heading removal, reversed input, word or row resets, cross-page carry, other numerical schedules and language scoring.

lp2-trigram-repeats.title: LP2-00–55: repeated trigrams against page shuffles
lp2-trigram-repeats.question: Does LP2-00–55 have an excess of within-page matching trigram pairs compared with independent whole-page fixed-count shuffles?
lp2-trigram-repeats.finding: 55 matching trigram pairs across 12,846 windows. 798/999 simulated totals are at least 55; corrected upper-tail p=0.799. Full rerun reproduces all outputs.
lp2-trigram-repeats.limitations: No evidence of excess under this fixed-count shuffle model does not establish randomness. Aggregate test only; no per-page significance, between-page comparison, alternative length or deficit test. Prior LP2-31 descriptive result was known. Human review pending.

scope.representation: Archived rune indices including headings; remove all non-runes. Overlapping length-three windows cross archived word and line boundaries but never pages. LP2-50 has no runes and contributes zero.
scope.procedure: For each page, sum count*(count-1)/2 over distinct trigram tuples; add page totals. Count unordered pairs of matching window starts, including overlapping occurrences. Do not compare windows from different pages. Independently shuffle the full rune multiset of every page, preserving its rune count and all single-rune frequencies. Score the full set of pages once per trial. Re-copy original streams before each shuffle. Page order follows pages; one Python random.Random generator for the full run.
scope.parameters: Window length 3 only; 999 complete-dataset shuffles; Python random.Random seed 330134; upper tail with ties; (exceedances+1)/1000; threshold 0.05.
scope.exclusions: Other window lengths, between-page matches, per-page significance, selected subsections, decoded readings, approximate matches, key-length inference and a deficit test.

lp2-turtle-spatial-replay.title: LP2 number streams as turtle paths
lp2-turtle-spatial-replay.question: Do the fixed 72 turtle drawing rules from a published LP2 number-channel test reproduce, and do any produce a geometric shape beyond shuffled controls?
lp2-turtle-spatial-replay.finding: All 72 geometric constructions and their 14,400 initial shuffles completed. The independent replay finds the same six initial p<0.01 path/measure screens as the source and reproduces both planted-shape controls. The source's later figure-flag rule accepts none of the six. This is no evidence of a glyph under the specified detector, and no decryption rule follows from the paths.
lp2-turtle-spatial-replay.limitations: The 200-shuffle screen does not resolve a familywise extreme-tail probability. The source's later normal-tail refinement is model-dependent, especially for discrete raster measures; closure and caging duplicate the same ratio. Sampled crossings and floating-point ties cause small source-versus-replay numerical differences. The source's empirical two-sided formula can exceed 1 for tied values. These caveats do not change which six cases entered the initial screen.

scope.representation: The 55 nonempty source transcription segments equal Liberpedia LP2-00–49 plus LP2-51–55, including F (index zero); source stream SHA-256 79b14e630946b64cdca838f328e73904f506df576d15e21fcb46271d4b4c8040.
scope.procedure: For each rune take its GP prime, one-based prime index, or prime totient. Turn modulo 4, 6, 8, 12, 29 or 360, using absolute or relative heading, then step by one unit or proportional to the value. Measure six declared path statistics and compare with 200 seeded histogram-preserving shuffles for every case. Run planted square and block-comb controls.
scope.parameters: 3 streams × 6 moduli × 2 turn interpretations × 2 step rules = 72 fixed constructions; 200 shuffles per construction = 14,400 null paths.
scope.exclusions: Per-page resets, pen-up markers, 3D or L-system routes, other angles or step rules, and any plaintext extraction along a path. G3 base32 and coordinate pointer framings from the broader source lane are not reimplemented in this geometric record.

lp2-word-order-reversal.title: LP2-00–55: reverse the order of word-like segments
lp2-word-order-reversal.question: Does reversing the order of declared word-like segments, while preserving runes inside each segment, recover any of nine known 12-rune openings on LP2-00–55?
lp2-word-order-reversal.finding: All 110 cases completed: 110 distinct page outputs, 990 fixed-opening comparisons and zero matches. Every output also equals the whole-stream reversal of its within-segment sibling.
lp2-word-order-reversal.limitations: Only nine exact beginnings are tested, not general readability. Segments are transcription-defined, not established plaintext words. Prior sibling results were known. Algebraic consistency is not independent evidence. Human review pending.

scope.representation: All recognized runes, including headings. Rune order inside each segment stays unchanged. Split-lines: every non-rune terminates a segment. Join-lines: ignore slash, CR and LF before segmentation; every other non-rune terminates a segment. These are transcription-defined segments, not independently established plaintext words. LP2-50 has no runes and contributes no candidates.
scope.procedure: Reverse the order of all segments across the complete page, then concatenate their runes without changing within-segment order. No within-segment reversal, alphabet substitution, heading removal or later-position search. Compare the first 12 output indices with nine fixed known beginnings.
scope.parameters: Two declared boundary conventions per nonempty page: split-lines and join-lines. 55 nonempty pages, 110 candidates, 990 exact opening comparisons.
scope.exclusions: Within-segment reversal, reversal limited to each row, arbitrary regrouping, heading removal, additional substitution, later-position search, alternative openings and general language ranking.

lp2-word-reversal.title: LP2-00–55: reverse runes within word-like segments
lp2-word-reversal.question: Does reversing runes within declared word-like segments recover any of nine known 12-rune openings on LP2-00–55?
lp2-word-reversal.finding: All 110 cases completed with zero exact opening matches in 990 comparisons. Independent regex/reflection checks and a full rerun agree on every output.
lp2-word-reversal.limitations: Transcription-defined segments are not established plaintext words. Only nine fixed beginnings are tested; other beginnings and combined ciphers remain untested. Human review pending.

scope.representation: All recognized runes, including headings. Segment order stays unchanged. Split-lines: every non-rune terminates a segment. Join-lines: ignore slash, CR and LF before segmentation; every other non-rune terminates a segment. These are transcription-defined segments, not independently established plaintext words. LP2-50 has no runes and contributes no candidates.
scope.procedure: Reverse rune positions within each segment; concatenate segments in their original order. No alphabet substitution, word-order reversal, heading removal or later-position search. Compare the first 12 output indices with nine fixed known beginnings.
scope.parameters: Two declared boundary conventions per nonempty page: split-lines and join-lines. 55 nonempty pages, 110 candidates, 990 exact opening comparisons.
scope.exclusions: Word-order reversal, arbitrary regrouping, heading removal, additional substitution, later-position search, alternative openings and general language ranking.

magic-square-freedom.title: Magic squares: does one fixed entry determine the rest?
magic-square-freedom.question: Does one fixed number determine either LP1 magic square?
magic-square-freedom.finding: Each five-by-five LP1 square has positive-integer alternatives that keep any one chosen cell and all line sums unchanged, while opposite cells remain equal. These conditions do not fix the rest of the square.
magic-square-freedom.limitations: Other requirements, such as prime-only entries, were not imposed. This does not reconstruct the original puzzle server’s acceptance rules.

scope.representation: LP1-05 rune words converted by additive Gematria Primus prime values; LP1-16 decimal grid. Row-major rational variables for comparison models.
scope.procedure: Exact rational RREF of fixed-line-sum difference constraints; separate none, half-turn, transpose and combined models. Add a fixed-cell constraint at every position for half-turn models. Construct and check positive-integer changes to the two archived 5x5 grids.
scope.parameters: Orders 3, 5, 7; four symmetry models each (12 cases). All cells fixed individually for half-turn dimensions. 25 positions per actual page (50 witness cases); first primitive null direction, plus then minus one step only.
scope.exclusions: No other primality, distinctness, normal-square or server-validation requirements; no enumeration of all positive grids; no historical 7x7 transcription or cipher search.

mixed-alphabet-key-openings.title: Keyword-mixed GP alphabets
mixed-alphabet-key-openings.question: Does moving keyword runes to the start of the alphabet change the result?
mixed-alphabet-key-openings.finding: Rearranging the alphabet with 43 keywords recovered none of the nine known 12-rune openings. The closest prefix matched four runes.
mixed-alphabet-key-openings.limitations: All phases of those keys were tested at page starts using one alphabet-building rule and subtraction. Other keywords, constructions, positions or plaintext beginnings remain untested.

scope.representation: First 12 recognized GP29 runes per LP2-00–55 page, including headings; LP2-50 has no runes. Non-runes do not advance the key.
scope.procedure: Deduplicate each key, append unused GP runes, remap ciphertext and key into the mixed order, subtract modulo 29, map back; test every key phase.
scope.parameters: 43 keys/alphabet permutations; 309 phases; 55 pages; nine openings; 152,955 comparisons.
scope.exclusions: Other keys, later positions, unknown openings, alternate signs, resets, interruptions, layers and language scoring.

mixed-square-word-sums.title: LP1-05: candidate word sums and rune segmentation
mixed-square-word-sums.question: Do the sixteen supplied Latin word candidates admit the claimed GP sums, and are those sums forced by their spellings?
mixed-square-word-sums.finding: All sixteen supplied totals are achievable. THAN also admits 208; AETHEREAL admits eight totals, only one equal to 366. Matching sums do not recover a unique word or demonstrate a cipher.
mixed-square-word-sums.limitations: Selected candidate list; no unbiased match-rate estimate, dictionary search or manuscript decryption. Computational review; human review pending.

scope.representation: Sixteen supplied Latin words, uppercase with V replaced by U; exact GP Latin-label segmentations.
scope.procedure: Enumerate all segmentations, sum prime values, and compare each with its supplied target.
scope.parameters: Fixed 16 candidates; 24 complete segmentations; no dictionary expansion.
scope.exclusions: Other words, synonyms, alternate spellings, altered rune values, key searches, manuscript decryption and statistical significance.

mobius-zero-mask-known-page.title: Möbius zero-mask rule against a solved LP2 page
mobius-zero-mask-known-page.question: Does the reported Möbius-of-totient zero-preservation rule hold under the published LP2-56 decoding?
mobius-zero-mask-known-page.finding: The published LP2-56 shift has 28 zero-to-nonzero violations, 22 reverse changes and 50 total mask mismatches among 85 runes.
mobius-zero-mask-known-page.limitations: A counterexample to a universal decoding invariant is not a refutation of a separately specified LP2-00-only mechanism. The report’s LP2-00 word-selection step remains unreplayed.

scope.representation: All 85 GP runes in the archived page, with φ(p)=p−1 and μ(φ(p)) evaluated on each GP prime; plaintext index is cipher index minus one modulo 29.
scope.procedure: Count one-way and reverse zero-mask violations under the published shift; enumerate all 29 constant shifts as a calculation comparison and independently check zero by square divisors.
scope.parameters: 29 GP symbols; 85 page runes; shifts 0–28; reported necessary direction is ciphertext μ=0 implies plaintext μ=0.
scope.exclusions: The proposed LP2-00 candidate sentence, its semantic ranking and word list, other cipher families, proof against a page-specific rule, and significance of a post-selected phrase.

monoalphabetic-crib-capacity.title: Simple substitution and page-opening cribs
monoalphabetic-crib-capacity.question: Does a phrase that fits a simple substitution tell us what comes next?
monoalphabetic-crib-capacity.finding: The LP2-12 start fits the archived second-koan twelve-rune opening under a bijective GP29 substitution. It assigns ten symbols, leaves 19! complete keys and fixes five of the next twelve positions. The other 494 pairs are incompatible with this exact rule.
monoalphabetic-crib-capacity.limitations: The one fit is conditional on a proposed plaintext, not a verified reading. The next twelve unknown plaintext runes cannot validate the five forced outputs. Other openings, positions and cipher layers remain untested.

scope.representation: First 24 recognized GP29 runes including headings on each of 55 rune-bearing LP2-00–55 pages.
scope.procedure: Compare each first-twelve-rune ciphertext against nine fixed known-reading openings for consistency under a bijection f(C)=P; count complete keys as (29-m)! for m assigned symbols; count which of the next twelve positions are forced.
scope.parameters: 55 page starts ×9 fixed 12-rune cribs =495 comparisons; one 29-symbol substitution permutation per comparison.
scope.exclusions: Other openings, later alignments, ciphertext-transposition, homophonic or polyalphabetic substitutions, multiple substitution layers, non-English plaintext, page-specific crib selection after output, and full-page language scoring.

multiplicative-ciphertext-autokey.title: Literal multiplicative ciphertext autokey: zero-state check
multiplicative-ciphertext-autokey.question: Can c[i] = p[i] × c[i−1] (mod 29) produce the LP2 ciphertext without a special zero rule?
multiplicative-ciphertext-autokey.finding: The literal uninterrupted multiplicative ciphertext-autokey recurrence is contradicted by 450 zero-to-nonzero ciphertext edges on all 55 nonempty LP2 pages.
multiplicative-ciphertext-autokey.limitations: This exact algebraic exclusion does not extend to zero-skipping, resets, offsets, alternate alphabets or other modified recurrences.

scope.representation: Archived 29-rune LP2-00–55 streams, non-runes removed within pages; F has index zero.
scope.procedure: Apply the exact absorbing-zero invariant of c[i]=p[i]×c[i−1] mod 29; enumerate zero-to-nonzero within-page edges; verify a synthetic positive control.
scope.parameters: Every within-page transition on LP2-00–55; arbitrary plaintext values and page-start seeds; no statistical threshold required.
scope.exclusions: Zero skipping, resetting, inserted markers, changed alphabets, additional key terms, or other modified feedback functions.

mutated-dictionary-key-openings.title: One-rune changes to public dictionary keys
mutated-dictionary-key-openings.question: What happens if a likely key has one wrong rune?
mutated-dictionary-key-openings.finding: No exact 12-rune opening match occurred in 82,494,720 named comparisons, represented by 83,328 altered-key/phase settings and 77,048 distinct 12-rune clocks. Planted positive controls and independent reconstruction passed.
mutated-dictionary-key-openings.limitations: Only first 12 GP runes at page starts and nine fixed known openings were assessed. A meaningful page with a different beginning, internal start, key rule or English score remains outside scope.

scope.representation: Canonical GP29 rune indices from first twelve recognized runes of each page transcription; LP2-50 has no runes.
scope.procedure: For each of 43 source rune keys replace one rune position or every instance of one rune type with each of the other 28 GP runes; deduplicate altered strings; test every phase in subtractive and additive repeating-key GP29 against nine fixed openings.
scope.parameters: 7,056 named rune-type changes + 8,652 named position changes = 9,856 distinct altered keys; 83,328 phases; 55 page starts; nine openings; two directions.
scope.exclusions: Other positions or plaintext openings, unknown languages, whole-page English scoring, Atbash, word resets, other keys or alphabet mappings.

n-rune-gaps.title: LP2-00–02: N-rune distances and prime-value labels
n-rune-gaps.question: Which prime-value labels result from successive N-rune gaps under two distance definitions and two page-boundary rules?
n-rune-gaps.finding: LP2-00 position distances begin 2,11,7,4,71, giving F R O . M. Joined pages add cross-page distances 40 and 53; only 53 maps to S. Intervening-rune counts give different labels.
n-rune-gaps.limitations: Exploratory reconstruction after the proposal and initial output were seen. No null model or independent plaintext criterion. A fragment is not evidence of a complete cipher. Computational review; human review pending.

scope.representation: All recognized runes in archived order including headings; punctuation and whitespace excluded. Target N only.
scope.procedure: Measure successive N distances, map exact GP prime values to labels, and retain every unmatched distance as a dot token.
scope.parameters: Two distance conventions (position difference; intervening runes) by two boundaries (page reset; join 00,01,02). Four configurations, eight output streams. No filtering of unmatched gaps.
scope.exclusions: Other runes, punctuation-based gaps, heading removal, anagrams, significance testing and interpretation of signpost artwork.

night-thoughts-729-line-audit.title: Night Thoughts: six proposed line-729 pointers in a pinned edition
night-thoughts-729-line-audit.question: Do the six quoted Night Thoughts passages fall on verse line 729 in one identifiable, reproducible edition?
night-thoughts-729-line-audit.finding: LP2-00–02 contain 262, 266 and 201 runes, totaling 729. In the pinned 1853 text, five of the six source-quoted passages are verse line 729. Night IX's quoted 'And deep reception' passage is line 731, two lines after the numbered 728 marker, so a six-of-six line-729 claim does not reproduce in this edition.
night-thoughts-729-line-audit.limitations: The source links a different Google Books volume whose exact scan/edition was not pinned in this test. Variant wording and line numbering may change there. The six lines were chosen after looking at the book, and no target-page cipher operation is supplied; this audit cannot establish a key or calculate a discovery probability.

scope.representation: Original three page transcriptions plus a pinned UTF-8 plaintext of Project Gutenberg ebook 33156, a transcription of an 1853 Gilfillan-edited Night Thoughts, with only CRLF normalized to LF. The upstream and normalized SHA-256 hashes and the supplied discussion's six quotations and Google Books link are identified separately in the plan.
scope.procedure: Count alphabet runes across the three pages. Search each quoted phrase within its named Night after only case and punctuation normalization. Infer the printed verse line from adjacent right-margin number markers, requiring neighboring anchors to agree; retain exact line, file position and marker evidence.
scope.parameters: One public-domain 1853 comparison edition; Nights IV–IX; six posted quotations; target verse line 729; no alternate line or book selected after output.
scope.exclusions: The linked Google Books scan's unverified edition and page labels; Blake's 1797 illustrated object; any GP-key construction, six-line concatenation cipher, RSA step, or LP2 decryption.

numeric-stream-skip-grid.title: Numeric keys with conditional skips
numeric-stream-skip-grid.question: Can these numeric keys decode pages when key positions may be skipped?
numeric-stream-skip-grid.finding: None of the 322 complete-page outputs selected by this numeric-key search cleared its English-score bar. The strongest complete output was on LP2-49.
numeric-stream-skip-grid.limitations: Only the listed 33 streams, five key phases, conditional-skip rule and English screen. Rejected short screens were not decoded as complete pages; a high score alone does not establish a reading.

scope.representation: 55 exact source GP29 page arrays, LP2-00–49 and LP2-51–55; canonical GP Latin labels scored with the pinned source English quadgrams.
scope.procedure: Unchanged source numeric sweep_keystream; source beam records all 50-rune screens and confirms only strict screen survivors on complete pages. Independent scalar reconstruction of every full survivor and maximum screen; independent rescore of all outputs.
scope.parameters: 33 labelled numeric streams at exact length1176 × 55 pages × signs −1/+1 × Atbash off/on × offsets0–4 =36,300 screens. Screen50/beam60/strict>−6.5; survivor full beam200/strict>−5.5; max3 conditional key skips.
scope.exclusions: 841 Fibonacci seed pairs; other numeric catalogs, offsets, clocks, languages and joined pages; no full decoding of rejected screens, full-search null calibration, general key-family exclusion or proof of plaintext.

oae-uniform-remapping.title: What if O, A and AE were treated as one rune?
oae-uniform-remapping.question: Could confusing O, A and AE explain the repeat counts?
oae-uniform-remapping.finding: Merging all three rune types increases equal neighbors from 89 to 192. Merely swapping their names changes neither statistic. The source’s comparison also changes scale: keeping the same IoC multiplier gives 1.22 after merging, rather than 1.14.
oae-uniform-remapping.limitations: These are uniform label changes in a text sample that includes the solved closing pages. They do not decide any glyph reading or show how an unknown cipher would respond to errors.

scope.representation: Every GP29 rune in the exact 13,136-rune source text, joined across punctuation and page boundaries; includes both solved closing pages.
scope.procedure: Enumerate all 27 uniform O/A/AE-to-O/A/AE mappings. Count equal neighbors and raw collision probability; report a fixed 29-symbol IoC multiplier separately from the source program’s observed-alphabet multiplier. Independently materialize every remapped stream.
scope.parameters: 3^3=27 deterministic maps; six bijections; three complete collapses; 13,135 adjacent pairs. No random control or language-score cutoff.
scope.exclusions: Individual glyph adjudication, context-dependent assignments, other rune families, word-boundary revisions, original image-clustering replay, decoder recovery and language identification.

obscura-sum-collision-control.title: OBSCURA word-sum matches in LP2
obscura-sum-collision-control.question: If an LP2 word has the same rune sum as an OBSCURA candidate, does that narrow the choice much?
obscura-sum-collision-control.finding: There are 104 observed matches. The page-preserving shuffle mean is 95.1645, with a central 95% range of 77–114; 375 of 2,000 controls reach at least 104. Sum equality by itself does not distinguish candidate keys or establish a cipher.
obscura-sum-collision-control.limitations: The candidate totals and manuscript text were examined before this control was specified. The shuffle is a reference for match abundance, not a ciphertext generator or a test of a defined decryptor. The original proposal did not supply one exact transform.

scope.representation: Thirteen distinct GP totals from sixteen fixed OBSCURA candidate words; all visible rune words on LP2-00–55, with hyphens and periods separating words and line breaks continuing them.
scope.procedure: Count exact word-sum matches, then shuffle GP prime values within each page while retaining page rune inventory and every visible word length.
scope.parameters: 2,928 words; 13 target totals; 2,000 shuffles with seed 330105.
scope.exclusions: No word-specific decryptor, candidate-selection tie-break, alternate transcription, semantic scoring or held-out prediction.

outguess-default-key.title: Original JPEGs: default-key OutGuess sweep
outguess-default-key.question: What does default-key OutGuess retrieval return from all 75 manuscript JPEGs and the two historical cover/opening images?
outguess-default-key.finding: All ten known payload hashes match. Other outcomes: 21 unverified nonempty outputs with exit 0; five exit-1 rejections; 41 abnormal exits with code 3221225620. Every status, diagnostic and output byte reproduced on rerun.
outguess-default-key.limitations: A successful process exit does not authenticate bytes. Failed retrieval does not prove no hidden data. The 41 abnormal exits are unresolved build/tool failures. Only one key and build were tested. Computational review only; human review pending.

scope.representation: Original archived JPEG bytes with fixed SHA-256 hashes: 75 manuscript images plus opening-2014 and 1033. No recompression or image transformations.
scope.procedure: One OutGuess retrieval per image with literal key Default key. Retain all output bytes and stderr/return codes; compare ten expected payload hashes. Repeat complete run for reproducibility.
scope.parameters: 77 images; one key; 20 seconds per invocation; pinned upstream commit 24810e14327c2bbeedeaadd3e24491f2a4425c02, Windows port binary SHA-256 b342b8b85d678d3b2ed26efab70fba2b3956725670be7149b89646868f0ebade.
scope.exclusions: Other keys, other builds/platforms, other steganographic methods, recompressed files, signature verification, and interpretation of candidate bytes.

outguess-guard-sweep.title: Original JPEGs: guarded OutGuess build comparison
outguess-guard-sweep.question: Does a clean build with explicit iterator guards change the baseline retrieval results on the same 77 images?
outguess-guard-sweep.finding: All 77 payload byte streams match the baseline exactly. Thirty-one successful exits and five existing rejections retain their diagnostics. All 41 formerly abnormal cases now exit 1 with an explicit iterator skipmod-zero diagnostic. Ten known controls pass.
outguess-guard-sweep.limitations: This compares two Windows builds from the same upstream source, not independent implementations or platforms. The patched diagnostic is not a stack trace from the original build. Successful extraction does not authenticate candidate bytes; a guard rejection does not establish absence of hidden data. Human review remains pending.

scope.representation: Original archived JPEG bytes with fixed SHA-256 hashes: 75 manuscript images plus opening-2014 and 1033. No recompression or image transformations.
scope.procedure: Use the recorded clean guarded build on the same 77 original JPEGs with the same key and timeout. Run ten controls first and stop on a control failure. Compare saved payload bytes, return codes and normalized diagnostics against the original baseline. Pinned upstream commit: 24810e14327c2bbeedeaadd3e24491f2a4425c02; clean guarded Windows executable SHA-256: bdc1810e59cb1152e7c3da88b38eaedfe49eba1656b4a4ab6f8c2b3f40126273.
scope.parameters: 77 original JPEGs; literal Default key; one clean guarded Windows build; 20 seconds per invocation.
scope.exclusions: Other keys, other platforms, independent OutGuess implementations, other steganographic methods, transformed images, payload authentication, and a stack trace of the original executable.

outguess-keyed-lp2.title: Six keyed OutGuess probes on LP2 images
outguess-keyed-lp2.question: Do six fixed manuscript-derived passphrases retrieve an identifiable hidden message from any original LP2 JPEG?
outguess-keyed-lp2.finding: 232 of 348 calls returned nonempty bytes. For each key, all nonempty outputs have one repeated length across the images; the byte streams differ and show no inspected readable message or common file header. Six planted carriers each recover only under their own key.
outguess-keyed-lp2.limitations: A successful retrieval or repeated length is not payload authentication. The six-key list is narrow, file-header inspection is not exhaustive, and this guarded Windows build is not an independent OutGuess implementation. Initial synthetic covers failed one correct-key roundtrip; replacement control bytes were pinned before the original-image run. Exact executable is a Windows PE build; other operating systems can inspect the saved bytes and source/build specification but cannot run that binary natively.

scope.representation: Original archived JPEG bytes for all 58 LP2 pages; the six synthetic planted carriers are separate controls, not target images.
scope.procedure: Retrieve each original image once with each of six frozen literal keys using the clean guarded OutGuess build. First recover the known 43-byte payload from six pinned key-specific carriers under all six keys. Retain every status, diagnostic, length, hash and output byte stream.
scope.parameters: Six exact ASCII keys, 58 original images, 348 retrievals, six planted carriers x six retrieval keys, 10-second per-call timeout, four worker processes, guarded OutGuess SHA-256 bdc1810e59cb1152e7c3da88b38eaedfe49eba1656b4a4ab6f8c2b3f40126273.
scope.exclusions: Unlisted passphrases and case variants; other tools and steganographic channels; recompressed or edited JPEGs; source-level absence proof; treating successful extraction as authenticated message.

page-join-sensitivity.title: LP2 page joins: sensitivity of word-length counts
page-join-sensitivity.question: How much do word-based LP2 statistics change when each unresolved rune-to-rune page edge is treated as a separator?
page-join-sensitivity.finding: Under the specified tokenizer, each of the 32 candidate edge splits adds one token. Splitting all edges increases the count from 2,896 to 2,928, increases one-rune tokens from 83 to 99, and reduces tokens of length ten or more from 109 to 104. The 11–11–10 length window count remains one.
page-join-sensitivity.limitations: The candidate edges are based on archived characters, not verified manuscript word boundaries. The all-split case is an endpoint sensitivity comparison, not a corrected transcription. This result measures segmentation sensitivity rather than evidence for a particular cipher.

scope.representation: Archived LP2-00–55 UTF-8 transcription text and the 29-rune site alphabet; all 32 rune-to-rune page edges are candidate separators, not verified word splits.
scope.procedure: Remove slash and CR/LF row wraps; preserve other delimiters. Compare fully joined, all 32 candidate edges separated, and every single candidate edge separately split using the same rune-token rule. Report token lengths and selected word-based counts.
scope.parameters: Fixed 56-page corpus, 32 identified candidate edges, no random search, 29-rune alphabet, headings retained, apostrophes internal to tokens but zero rune length.
scope.exclusions: No image review, inferred English words, plaintext scoring, cipher trial, alternate transcription, LP2-56–57, or claim that either endpoint is the intended manuscript segmentation.

page-margin-row-alignment.title: LP2 margin trimming: do neighboring text rows align uniquely?
page-margin-row-alignment.question: After one fixed image crop and zero-shift registration, are consecutive LP2 text-row positions distinctive relative to nonconsecutive same-layout pages?
page-margin-row-alignment.finding: Adjacent mean 0.764289935; nonadjacent mean 0.672274805. Four adjacent pairs and six nonadjacent controls score 1.000. LP2-44–48 share the same measured row mask under the fixed rule, so perfect line alignment is not unique to consecutive pages.
page-margin-row-alignment.limitations: The source proposed a possible image join but fixed no target pages, crop or success rule. This audit uses a chosen coherent page run. Row masks ignore glyph identity and horizontal seam continuity; enlarged initials and gap variation affect scores. Pairs share pages, so no significance test is assigned.

scope.representation: Original 2400×3600 JPEG pixels converted to grayscale; one fixed central text crop and y-row occupancy mask.
scope.procedure: Crop every page to x=650–1749, y=620–2899; sample every third x pixel; mark rows with >12 samples below gray 90; score all 36 unordered page pairs by occupied-row Jaccard without shifting.
scope.parameters: 9 images, 8 adjacent pairs, 28 nonadjacent controls, zero fitted parameters; x step 3, threshold 90, row occupancy >12.
scope.exclusions: No rune recognition, word-boundary judgment, page-order search, best-fit registration, decryption, or claim that this is the original proposer’s exact intended test.

page-number-prime-skip-grid.title: Keys based on page order
page-number-prime-skip-grid.question: Can keys derived from page order decode the text?
page-number-prime-skip-grid.finding: These three page-assigned key rules produced no output that cleared their fixed English-score test. Only seven of the 660 short trials reached complete-page checking.
page-number-prime-skip-grid.limitations: Only these three rules and this skip procedure were tested. Most settings received a 50-rune check; passing the score test would still need plaintext verification.

scope.representation: 55 exact source GP29 page arrays, LP2-00–49 and LP2-51–55; canonical GP Latin labels scored with the pinned source English quadgrams.
scope.procedure: Execute unchanged source numeric2 sweep_page_seeded with return-preserving observations of its beam/helper results. Screen all assigned page rules and fully decode only strict survivors. Independently reconstruct all short/full outputs with the exact nonzero-linear-step skip criterion; separately freeze and audit every retained terminal candidate.
scope.parameters: Three source page-assigned modes x55pages x2signs x2Atbash states =660screens; exact1124-value keys, offset0. Screen50/beam60/strict>-6.5; survivor full beam300/strict>-5.5.165assignments,56base arrays,112signed-array plants representing8step/reading situations.
scope.exclusions: Source numeric2 PartsA/B, unassigned page keys, other phases/clocks/languages and joined pages; no full decoding of rejected screens or intermediate normalized ranking.330Atbash-off rigid paths already overlap progressive Caesar; reflected rigid coverage is not established by that record. No page-number significance, global-null probability, general key-family exclusion or plaintext proof.

page40-for-every-arithmetic.title: LP2-40: replay the FOR EVERY opening arithmetic
page40-for-every-arithmetic.question: Do the fixed shift, Atbash and prime-minus-one steps in the reported FOR EVERY proposal predict its eight-position LP2-40 opening without a fitted residual?
page40-for-every-arithmetic.finding: The posted fixed transformation reproduces its intermediate row exactly. Against the archived ciphertext it matches 1 of 8 positions—the held F—and 0 of 7 non-F positions. The eight residual key values are congruent with the post, but are calculated from the target. FOR sums to 20 (composite), EVERY to 251 (prime), and the full phrase to 271 (prime).
page40-for-every-arithmetic.limitations: The source presents an additional running-key theory, not a claim that the fixed layers alone decrypt the page. Its Möbius argument, starting point, eight-state operation map, sign/zero handling and key clock are not frozen in the supplied discussion; the linked spreadsheet was described as changing. The pasted discussion refers to images that are not present in its text export. The source's 13/31 floral reading is treated as a proposal, not an independently established measurement. Human review pending.

scope.representation: The first three- and five-rune groups of archived LP2-40, the 29-entry stored GP alphabet, and the eight source-reported FOR EVERY indices and transformation rows; source discussion pinned by SHA-256 in plan.json.
scope.procedure: Confirm the archived opening's indices; hold first F as the source's zero placeholder; shift the next seven proposed plaintext indices by 18 modulo 29, then Atbash, then add the posted prime-minus-one stream modulo 29. Count exact matches. Compute the residual from ciphertext only as a diagnostic and separately verify GP sums.
scope.parameters: One fixed eight-rune crib, first two printed groups, zero-based GP indices, shift +18, Atbash x→28−x modulo 29, source totient stream [0,1,2,4,6,10,12,16], no tuned variants or body text.
scope.exclusions: No verified meaning assigned to flower details; no fixed Möbius seed, trigram state table or key schedule; no untouched continuation, language score, full-page decoding or test of later Slidefair/Quagmire/Fibonacci follow-ups.

parallel-language-blocks.title: Language comparison: shorter aligned passage controls
parallel-language-blocks.question: Does the eight-language length comparison remain stable on shorter aligned passages?
parallel-language-blocks.finding: English has the smallest manuscript length-distance in all eight blocks in each representation. Known-language reference matching succeeds in 64/64 decisions per representation. This is stability within FLORES, not proof of plaintext language.
parallel-language-blocks.limitations: Blocks match sentences, not token counts, and may share source articles; the 64 control decisions are not independent. Genre, cipher and transcription differences prevent a plaintext-language conclusion.

scope.representation: Existing rune-only joined LP2-00–55 token ledger, 2896 tokens, headings included; no decimal tokens. Three shared representations plus a Welsh digraph sensitivity; details in plan.
scope.procedure: For each block and representation, compare each language length histogram to the fixed manuscript histogram with the baseline TV metric. Report all scores and ranks, not a posterior. Classify each of 64 language/block profiles by nearest full dev language histogram, separately per representation; publish confusion matrices and individual decisions. Dev is unchanged; no fitting or tuning.
scope.parameters: Eight disjoint blocks from all 1,012 FLORES devtest sentences per language: four of 127 sentences, four of 126. Identical sentence ranges across languages; three fixed representations; no bootstrap.
scope.exclusions: No matched-length random samples, genre-matched corpus, known decoded LP control, cipher recovery or all-language inference. GP grouping remains an unvalidated orthographic sensitivity.

parallel-languages.title: Could the unsolved text be another language? Eight aligned translations
parallel-languages.question: Which of eight languages best matches the unsolved text under word-length and fixed-substitution assumptions?
parallel-languages.finding: English had the closest word-length pattern among the eight tested languages. It remained closest under all three counting methods.
parallel-languages.limitations: This comparison assumes that encryption preserves word boundaries and word lengths. It ranks these reference texts; it does not identify the hidden language.

scope.representation: Existing rune-only joined LP2-00–55 token ledger, 2896 tokens, headings included; no decimal tokens. Three shared representations plus a Welsh digraph sensitivity; details in plan.
scope.procedure: Total variation distance between word-length histograms, bins 1..15 and16+. Lower is closer. Rank eight languages separately for each of first three representations. Never combine metrics into a language probability. IoC and within-word adjacent-identical fraction; separate distances under fixed bijective substitution only. Distinct symbol inventory reported. Dev language profiles classify each whole devtest language by word-length distance (8 held-out documents per representation). No tuning after scoring.
scope.parameters: Eight fixed languages; all 997 dev and 1012 devtest aligned sentences; 281 devtest article clusters; 200 paired bootstrap draws; seed 3301; 16 length bins.
scope.exclusions: No decryption; no claim one global cipher/language; no posterior; no all-language coverage; no genre-matched medieval/philosophical corpus; no unknown phonetic conversion; no unspaced languages or mixed plaintext inference.

payload-ciphertext-skip-replay.title: Number-grid bytes as an encrypted message
payload-ciphertext-skip-replay.question: Could the number-grid bytes be an encrypted message under these keys?
payload-ciphertext-skip-replay.finding: Neither archived grid reading passed the score test under any of the twelve keys. Scores also accepted seven wrong known-message outputs, so this does not rule out a message in the payload.
payload-ciphertext-skip-replay.limitations: Only this byte-to-rune reading, these twelve finite keys and the source decoder were checked. The two inputs are alternative readings of one grid, and the controls reuse two known passages.

scope.representation: Two pinned 256-byte grid readings, each byte reduced modulo 29 to GP indices. Optional ciphertext Atbash maps c to 28-c. These are alternate readings of one grid, not independent messages.
scope.procedure: Source payload_ciphertext.py section 1 only. Construct all twelve finite keys, then execute unchanged skipdecode.beam_decode at offset zero for every input/sign/Atbash case. Preserve stable cumulative winner and its normalized score; separately record every retained terminal normalized score and first maximum. Report all exceptions rather than trusting printed denominator.
scope.parameters: 12 distinct source arrays, exactly 356 symbols each; 2 inputs x 2 signs x 2 Atbash =96 full 256-rune calls. Beam 300, max_skip 3, strict score > -5.5. Source appends 4L+8 zeros when 4L>=key length. Known-message controls: 144 fixed-seed cases plus next-key wrong controls; 24 forced pointer-435 boundaries and 96 allocation checks.
scope.exclusions: Other keys, offsets, key clocks, infinite cycling beyond the source prefix, alternate scoring/ranking, other languages, raw-byte reversible interpretations, source sections 2–4 and later probes. No global-null significance or general payload-message rejection. All seven known-reading ranking failures preserved.

payload-doublet-gaps.title: Do LP2 grid bytes track doublet gaps?
payload-doublet-gaps.question: Do fixed-width or varint readings of the LP2-49–51 payload correlate with distances between adjacent equal-rune events in LP2?
payload-doublet-gaps.finding: Among 14 fixed comparisons, the largest absolute Spearman rank correlation is 0.119, below the published 0.5 effect-size gate. For the primary 85-gap target, 83 of 84 nonzero circular alignments have an equal or larger best-of-seven correlation than the unshifted comparison.
payload-doublet-gaps.limitations: Only fixed byte-zero readings and two event-gap definitions are tested.

scope.representation: Pinned 256-byte source grid and 86 within-page equal-rune-pair starts on archived LP2-00–55, concatenated in page order for gap distances.
scope.procedure: Decode seven fixed integer/varint readings at byte zero. Compare first available values with 85 inter-event distances and with the first one-based event coordinate plus those distances using tie-aware Spearman correlation. Audit all 84 nonzero rotations of the 85-gap target with the best-of-seven statistic.
scope.parameters: Seven byte readings; two targets; 14 comparisons; 85 gap distances; 84 alignment controls; published effect-size gate |rho| >= 0.5.
scope.exclusions: Other payload transcriptions, starting offsets, byte permutations, transforms, noncontiguous selections, distinct event definitions, and inference of a cipher mechanism.

payload-phase-skip-grid.title: Moving the number-grid key's starting position
payload-phase-skip-grid.question: Does moving the number-grid key help decode a page?
payload-phase-skip-grid.finding: None of the 234 complete-page results passed the source’s English-score test. The strongest result was on LP2-49; most settings stopped after the first 50 runes.
payload-phase-skip-grid.limitations: Only four grid-derived keys and the source’s page-specific starting positions were tested. A good score can select an incorrect reading, and rejected short screens were not decoded as complete pages.

scope.representation: 55 exact source GP29 page arrays, LP2-00–49 and LP2-51–55; canonical GP Latin labels scored with the pinned source English quadgrams.
scope.procedure: Run unchanged source numeric2 Part B with four payload interpretations and its page-specific phase bounds. Record every short output and confirm only source short-gate survivors. Independently rescore every output and reconstruct all complete survivors, best short output and best normalized terminal witnesses. Preserve source selection separately from a labelled post-target audit.
scope.parameters: Four source 256-byte streams tiled seven times to 1,792 values. For page length L, offsets range(max(1,268−L)); 1,882 page/offset pairs × four streams × two signs × two Atbash states = 30,112 screens. Screen 50/beam 60/strict >−6.5, survivor full beam 300/strict >−5.5, max three conditional key skips. 880 offset-zero labels overlap earlier payload work; 29,232 nonzero labels.
scope.exclusions: Source numeric2 Parts A/C, phases outside the executable page-length bounds, other payload constructions, clocks, languages, joined pages, full decoding of rejected short screens, general key-family exclusion or global null significance. Earlier offset-zero replay used another width, no short gate and another finite allocation.

periodic-affine-crib-capacity.title: How many periodic affine keys can fit a twelve-rune opening?
periodic-affine-crib-capacity.question: Can I make a periodic affine key fit an opening, and would that fit mean anything?
periodic-affine-crib-capacity.finding: No fixed opening fit periods 1–5. At period 6, 287 of 495 page-opening pairs fit, 276 with one key and 11 with 28. Periods 7 and 8 have 262 and 293 fits respectively, all with many keys: at least 784 and 614,656. Compatible fits at those periods force only 6–9 and 3–6 of the next twelve positions. These are algebraic fits, not readings.
periodic-affine-crib-capacity.limitations: Only nine proposed twelve-rune openings at page position zero, periods 1–8, invertible GP29 affine maps and archived page text are examined. A contradiction excludes that exact combination only; compatible openings do not establish an encryption method.

scope.representation: First 24 runes including headings on each rune-bearing LP2-00–55 page; first twelve paired with nine fixed reading openings and next twelve inspected only for forced-position count.
scope.procedure: For each period 1–8, enumerate the 812 invertible GP29 affine maps independently at each residue and retain those satisfying its crib observations; multiply residue counts. Count the following positions whose output is identical under every compatible map for its residue. Verify with a planted period-3 known reading and exhaustive F3 small-field key enumeration.
scope.parameters: 55 pages × 9 fixed openings × 8 periods = 3,960 cases. Each residue has 0, 1 or 28 compatible affine maps after the twelve-rune crib; no whole-key brute force and no language score.
scope.exclusions: No other opening, later alignment, period above 8, key clock reset, mixed alphabet, nonlinear transition, feedback model or historical Alberti branch mechanism.

pgp-packet-keys.title: PGP packet bytes as repeating LP2 keys
pgp-packet-keys.question: Have the Cicada public-key bytes been tried as a rune key?
pgp-packet-keys.finding: All 119,900 complete-page settings scored below the predeclared −5.5 English gate. The best score was −6.456; 174 of 199 page-shuffled full-search controls reached at least that value. Nine known-reading and planted-key controls passed.
pgp-packet-keys.limitations: This is a newly constructed baseline, not a historical replay. It tests byte modulo 29, repeating page-local addition/subtraction and all cyclic phases of exactly four archived public-key streams. Other packet parsing, conversions and cipher relations remain open.

scope.representation: Every GP rune including headings on all 55 nonempty LP2-00–55 pages; non-rune marks omitted, page-local clock.
scope.procedure: Extract the two v4 RSA public packet bodies and their binary fingerprints from the pinned Cicada key, map every byte modulo 29, try every cyclic phase and both additive signs, score complete pages using the fixed English quadgram model and 199 full-search page-shuffled nulls.
scope.parameters: Four streams of 525,20,525,20 bytes; 2,180 phase/sign combinations per page ×55 pages =119,900 complete-page settings.
scope.exclusions: Other PGP packet fields or signatures, raw key text/armor, different byte-to-rune conversion, nonrepeating offsets, additional transforms, crib selection, non-English plaintext, and hidden key construction.

position-divisor-labels.title: LP2-00–55: fixed divisor labels of rune positions
