position-divisor-labels.question: Can fixed divisors greater than one label consecutive rune positions, with any starting integer?
position-divisor-labels.finding: All 55 nonempty rune pages exclude the defined unit-stride model. For any gcd-one rune and general stride s, its divisor must divide s; noncoprime strides remain outside the exclusion.
position-divisor-labels.limitations: Fixed labels and the specified rune clock only. Does not exclude all prime-based constructions or all strides. Necessary divisibility is not a deterministic encoder or decryption. Transcription dependent; human review pending.

scope.representation: Archived alphabet runes only, headings retained, nonrunes removed, zero-based positions reset at each page.
scope.procedure: Compute same-rune occurrence-gap gcds; use gcd-one witnesses to exclude unit strides for any origin; independently check all pairwise gaps and a noncoprime-stride counterexample.
scope.parameters: 56 page files; 55 nonempty rune streams; any integer origin; fixed integer divisor q>1 per rune, not necessarily prime or distinct; unit strides +1 and -1; general necessary condition q divides stride for gcd-one labels.
scope.exclusions: Irregular clocks, within-page resets, time-varying labels, transformed outputs, plaintext mixing, general rejection of noncoprime strides, and LP2-56–57.

prepared-opening-evidence-gates.title: Four Warning-opening tests already settled by saved evidence
prepared-opening-evidence-gates.question: Do saved prefixes already exclude four prepared 24-rune Warning-opening proposals under their exact reversal or cumulative-reset rules?
prepared-opening-evidence-gates.finding: Saved evidence rules out all four fixed Warning-opening proposals on all 55 rune pages. The mismatch appears at rune one, two or three, before any changed reset could repair it. No complete new manuscript decode is needed.
prepared-opening-evidence-gates.limitations: This excludes one specified page-start opening under four exact rules, not the cipher families or other plaintexts. It is a retrospective evidence audit, not an independent statistical discovery. LP2-50 has no runes and is excluded from the denominator.

scope.representation: Canonical GP29 indices from pinned raw LP2-00–49 and LP2-51–55 text, headings retained; 55 nonempty rune pages. LP2-50 is outside the opening denominator because it has no runes.
scope.procedure: Reuse saved row-reversal and word-reversal prefix arrays, applying the inverse-Atbash condition to the fixed Warning vector. For cumulative resets, reuse saved first-difference census prefix bounds only before the first differing reset. Verify every witness against source positions and pinned recipe identities. No complete new target decode.
scope.parameters: Four fixed prepared recipes; one fixed 24-rune page-start Warning vector; canonical alphabet indices 0–28; Atbash a=28,b=28; cumulative initial sum zero; every-non-rune word resets or CR/LF line resets. All four recipes excluded on each of 55 nonempty pages.
scope.exclusions: Other plaintexts/openings, later start positions, general readability, corrected text, heading removal, extra keys, other reset or reversal conventions, null distributions and a full LP2 decryption claim.

prime-distance-reverse-add.title: LP2-15 reported reverse-add palindrome: arithmetic and control
prime-distance-reverse-add.question: Does the reported 53-digit reverse-add example hold, and how often do its own digits give palindromes after shuffling?
prime-distance-reverse-add.finding: The quoted sum is correct and palindromic. All 53 mirrored digit-pair sums are at most seven, so no carrying occurs and symmetry is guaranteed. Of 100,000 fixed-digit shuffles, 50,442 produce palindromes under the same integer operation; all 50,442 also satisfy the no-carry condition with a nonzero outer pair.
prime-distance-reverse-add.limitations: The original decimal string and zero grouping were selected before this audit. The source-to-digits derivation has not been replayed, and the conditional shuffle is not a p-value over all available pages, segmentations and arithmetic choices. Computational review only; human review pending.

scope.representation: The exact 53-character decimal string reported for an LP2-15 word-sum-distance construction, including its leading zero; no rune or word transcription is used in this arithmetic-only replay.
scope.procedure: Add the string to its full character reversal as integers, verify all 53 paired decimal columns and carries, then shuffle the fixed digit multiset 100,000 times with seed 3301 and apply the same operation to each.
scope.parameters: One selected 53-character example; 100,000 conditional random permutations; Python random.Random seed 3301; leading zero allowed in shuffled strings.
scope.exclusions: Derivation of GP word sums and nearest-prime distances, alternative zero groupings, a complete search-adjusted p-value, plaintext recovery, and evidence of authorial intent.

prime-distance-word-derivation.title: LP2-15–16: derive the reported prime-distance digits
prime-distance-word-derivation.question: Does the reported 53-digit nearest-prime sequence follow word by word from the archived first-section rune transcription?
prime-distance-word-derivation.finding: The 53 reported digits do not match the 57 distances under the declared archived segmentation. A minimum of seven digit edits separates them. The 57-digit reverse-add result is nevertheless a palindrome because every mirrored digit pair sums to at most eight. In 100,000 matched digit-multiset shuffles, 53,845 results are palindromes.
prime-distance-word-derivation.limitations: The pasted source does not preserve the author's full transcription, exact separator choices or computation script. The figure gives one of multiple possible minimum alignments; it cannot identify which words the author omitted or changed. The archived text, though source-hashed, has not been reverified rune by rune against the image for this audit. The shuffle is conditional on a selected section and digit multiset. Human review pending.

scope.representation: Archived 29-rune LP2-15 heading and first LP2-15–16 section through the word preceding the next section's ᛈᚹᚷᚷ. Slash-newline and the page break join rune words; hyphens and periods separate words. Each word is mapped to its Gematria Primus prime sum and closest-prime absolute distance.
scope.procedure: Compute all 57 word distances from the hashed archived text and compare their string to the reported 53-digit source string. Audit reverse-add arithmetic on the complete archive-derived string, then shuffle its fixed digit multiset 100,000 times with the same operation.
scope.parameters: First section only; 29 GP values; nearest-prime distance without directional preference; leading zero retained for reversal; 100,000 random.Random shuffles, seed 33011516; report sequence alignment is descriptive and may be non-unique.
scope.exclusions: Image-level certification of each rune and separator; other page or section selections; altered word segmentation; other prime mappings; full discovery-search correction; a decryption of LP2-15–22.

prime-fibonacci-position-extraction.title: Runes at prime and Fibonacci positions
prime-fibonacci-position-extraction.question: What happens if we read only the prime- or Fibonacci-numbered runes?
prime-fibonacci-position-extraction.finding: Page-local prime extraction scored −7.472, the best of three eligible arms. In 201 of 256 page-shuffled trials, the strongest eligible arm scored at least that high (global add-one estimate 202/257≈0.786). The joined Fibonacci arm selected only 20 runes and was not scored.
prime-fibonacci-position-extraction.limitations: Direct English quadgram scoring cannot exclude further encryption, another language or alternate position origins/directions. The book-wide Fibonacci stream is too short for the declared scorer. The catalog is an idea list, not a verified historical test record.

scope.representation: 12,956 recorded GP runes on the 55 rune-bearing LP2-00–55 pages, with non-rune punctuation and artwork excluded.
scope.procedure: Select one-based prime or unique Fibonacci positions, either restarting per page and pooling within-page English quadgrams or indexing the joined page stream once. Require at least 100 Latin quadgrams to score. Compare the best eligible arm to 256 shared within-page-shuffle global maxima and verify planted known-reading extraction.
scope.parameters: Two selectors × two boundary rules; prime-page-local 2,797 selected runes, prime-joined 1,542, Fibonacci-page-local 634, Fibonacci-joined 20 (unscored). 256 null trials with seed 33017119+trial.
scope.exclusions: Every-n/phase variants, backwards indexing, alternate page ordering, another cipher layer, alternate languages, using selected positions as a key rather than direct text and claims about unscored short outputs.

prime-lag-autokey-openings.title: Prime-lag autokey against fixed opening cribs
prime-lag-autokey-openings.question: Do any prime-delayed autokey settings produce one of the nine proposed openings?
prime-lag-autokey-openings.finding: None of the tested settings produces any of the nine proposed openings on these page starts. Longer known-text controls do recover correctly.
prime-lag-autokey-openings.limitations: Only the fixed one-rune primers, delays and nine opening guesses were tested. Longer primers or different plaintexts could behave differently.

scope.representation: Original GP29 rune order; all non-runes removed; first 12 runes on each nonempty page; page-local reset.
scope.procedure: One rune repeated for consumed j<lag; afterwards subtract prior cipher at lag or recovered plaintext at lag. No interruptions; reset each page.
scope.parameters: 11 prime lags 2..31; 2 feedback modes; 29 repeated single-rune primers; 638 settings; 55 nonempty pages; 9 frozen 12-rune cribs; 638 full 64-rune plants.
scope.exclusions: Original C++ compilation; variable-length arbitrary primers; interruptions; other lags/openings; general language/solve or significance claims.

public-circumference-substitutions.title: Public 2πR rune substitutions
public-circumference-substitutions.question: What happens when each rune is transformed using the circumference formula?
public-circumference-substitutions.finding: The index- and prime-radius truncation maps reproduce 57/57 full source-page streams each; nearest rounding differs. The source provides no language score.
public-circumference-substitutions.limitations: The source gives no prespecified language score. These are fixed symbol substitutions; reproducing their output or counting collisions is not a full decryption test.

scope.representation: LP2-00–55 in canonical 29-rune GP order; non-rune marks retained.
scope.procedure: Map each rune by 2π times its zero-based index or GP prime value, modulo 29; compare nearest rounding with truncation and separately verify all 57 complete archived source-page streams per variant.
scope.parameters: Four 29-symbol maps; 56 LP2-unsolved pages in the original test and 57 complete source pages per archived truncation variant.
scope.exclusions: Other geometric formulas, secondary keys, reverse maps and full language scoring. Archived page 56 is checked only for complete-output agreement.

public-deepweb-jpeg-hashes.title: Do the manuscript JPEGs hash to the deep-web target?
public-deepweb-jpeg-hashes.question: Have we tried hashing the manuscript images against LP2-56?
public-deepweb-jpeg-hashes.finding: All 75 source JPEGs match both digest columns in the pinned source checksum table; none of 150 full-file digests equals the LP2-56 target. In a distinct follow-up, none of 116 digests from 58 preserved seventh-onion JPEGs matches either. Separate planted image-00 targets are recovered for both sets and algorithms.
public-deepweb-jpeg-hashes.limitations: These are two specified file sets, not one historical source run: the 75-file set replays Failed-Attempts, while the 58-file seventh-onion check is a new bounded follow-up. Neither preserved set is independently authenticated as creator-original bytes. Other files, transforms, combinations and hash interpretations remain untested.

scope.representation: Two explicitly separate exact-byte sets: 75 hosted LP1+LP2 JPEGs identified by the Failed-Attempts checksum table, and 58 preserved seventh-onion LP2 JPEGs identified by a pinned archive manifest.
scope.procedure: Freeze both candidate sets separately before target comparison; hash full files with SHA-512 and BLAKE2b-512; join LP2-56's five printed hex lines; compare 150 source-replay digests and 116 follow-up digests without combining their results. Independently rehash and plant a known image-00 target in both sets.
scope.parameters: 75 source images plus 58 distinct archived images, each under two fixed 512-bit algorithms, one exact 128-hex LP2-56 target; no adjustable key, transform or substring search.
scope.exclusions: Re-exports or crops beyond the two pinned sets, concatenated or embedded file data, other web pages, other hash algorithms and claims about LP2's runic cipher.

public-kdf-seed-stretch.title: Password-derived key streams against the LP2 opening
public-kdf-seed-stretch.question: Could a short password be stretched into Liber Primus's key?
public-kdf-seed-stretch.finding: The planted PBKDF2 control ranked first at −4.186, but no LP2 candidate cleared the −5.500 advancement bar. The best LP2 score was −6.259 across 692,064 completed decodes.
public-kdf-seed-stretch.limitations: Only the first 120 unsolved runes and offset zero were tested. The source's 200 shuffled controls were scored with one fixed key, rather than repeating the whole search; they do not calibrate the winning score's selection probability. Other secrets, salts, recipes, languages and page-dependent keys remain untested.

scope.representation: The first 120 rune indices of the pinned unsolved LP2 stream. Source-defined seed dictionary entries are bytes; KDF output is expanded with SHA-256 counter mode and reduced modulo 29 or by the source rejection rule.
scope.procedure: Run the pinned K1 expander control and the K2 planted-PBKDF2 control, then sweep the complete Stage A grid against LP2 with skip-aware beam width 400 and at most three key skips per rune.
scope.parameters: 534 ordered secrets × 27 KDFs × 3 salts × 2 reductions × 2 signs × 2 Atbash choices × 2 key directions = 692,064 LP2 decodes. Offset zero, first 120 runes. The K2 control independently traverses the same configuration grid on a planted message.
scope.exclusions: Secrets outside the fixed dictionary, other KDF configurations or salts, nonzero offsets, longer page spans, different languages, page-varying construction and Stage B salt expansion.

public-keyed-columnar-word-counts.title: Source keyword columns at the printed word alignment
public-keyed-columnar-word-counts.question: Do keyword-selected column orders reveal words at the printed alignment?
public-keyed-columnar-word-counts.finding: The best keyword gives 126 dictionary matches, but shuffled pages commonly score as highly. Known-text tests recover the intended reading. These word matches do not confirm plaintext.
public-keyed-columnar-word-counts.limitations: The shuffled comparison was designed after seeing the result, so it is exploratory. Only these 45 keyword labels, this dictionary and the original visible word lengths were tested.

scope.representation: Remove slash and line breaks; hyphens delimit visible word slots; ignore all nonalphabet characters inside each slot.
scope.procedure: Exact source keyword list; strip duplicate characters preserving first occurrence; alphabetic column order with original-position tie break; decrypt ragged columns with original leftmost columns longest; no wraps; one transform per page. Separate POST-TARGET calibration: 128 shared-page rune-order shuffles, rerun all 45 aggregate per-key scores and retain trial key maximum. 45 full 184-rune known-Warning planted score/rank controls use its existing decoded boundaries.
scope.parameters: 45 source labels, 43 distinct column orders; 56 pages/55 nonempty; 2,776 visible slots; 369,652 fixed dictionary entries; 1,125 permutation controls. Exploratory calibration: 128 shared-page nulls, Random seed 330145; 45 known-reading score/rank controls, separate from 1125 inverse tests.
scope.exclusions: Original absolute-path transcription/dictionary and blocks[:55] are not silently reconstructed. This is a precisely declared local-input followup, not exact archived target/result replay. Source percent26 one-long-word random control is not used.

public-lp2-as-pad.title: LP2 as a running key for shorter Cicada texts
public-lp2-as-pad.question: Could Liber Primus itself be the key to a shorter message?
public-lp2-as-pad.finding: No tested pairing passed the source's English score bar. The best of 40 decodes scored −7.032 against −5.500; the five highest scorers did not exceed their own shuffled-target maxima. A planted message was recovered exactly.
public-lp2-as-pad.limitations: This is a cross-artifact key test, not a direct LP2 decrypt. The pp49–51 payload was unavailable, and all keys began at offset zero. The null was calculated only for the selected top five configurations; the hard-coded 63-byte AN END sequence is not independently authenticated here.

scope.representation: The pinned source's 12,956 unsolved rune indices are key material; English targets are converted to GP rune indices and the hard-coded byte target is reduced modulo 29.
scope.procedure: Use the source beam decoder with up to three key skips and its English quadgram score. Sweep five targets, four LP2 key variants and two signs at offset zero; compare the selected top five with 200 target-order shuffles each.
scope.parameters: 40 source decodes (some arithmetically equivalent); 500-rune cap on the three English-text targets, 63-byte numeric target, 200-rune LP2 prefix target; beam width 400; 100 shuffles for the planted control.
scope.exclusions: Absent pp49–51 payload, other key offsets, other targets and encodings, alternative boundary rules or skip models, and the reverse use of other objects as keys.

public-multihistory-feedback.title: Two-to-six-rune feedback and autokey screen
public-multihistory-feedback.question: Could each rune be decoded using a key derived from the preceding runes?
public-multihistory-feedback.finding: None of 23,520 settings reached the English-score threshold. But the search also missed all 14 planted plaintext-history and mixed-history examples when limited to its actual starting values, so that negative result cannot rule out those methods.
public-multihistory-feedback.limitations: The search uses seven fixed rules, two to six earlier runes, and only starting sequences whose values are all equal. Other starting sequences and feedback rules were not searched.

scope.representation: Zero-based GP rune indices from the pinned source transcription: 12,956 unsolved runes in 55 nonempty source segments, plus their concatenation.
scope.procedure: For each stream, sweep seven fixed feedback functions, k=2..6, three history sources, both signs and both directions; score decoded transliteration using the pinned English quadgram table and 29 all-equal seeds for plaintext/mixed history.
scope.parameters: 56 streams x 7 functions x 5 history lengths x 3 sources x 2 signs x 2 directions = 23,520 scored configurations. Ciphertext history ignores the seed after k; plaintext/mixed source probe eq0 through eq28. Twenty-one k=3 planted controls.
scope.exclusions: Non-equal initial seeds, k outside 2..6, formulas outside the seven-source basis, state crossing other page boundaries, skip-aware decoding, different transliterations or language scorers.

public-nskips-crossover.title: Skip-count signal across planted message lengths
public-nskips-crossover.question: How much text is needed before a skip-count clue becomes useful?
public-nskips-crossover.finding: For the exact decoder, the first separating ladder point is 6,000 runes, bracketed by a non-separating 3,600-rune point; separation persists at 9,000 and 12,956. This is a property of the planted test and its chosen null, not an LP2 decryption.
public-nskips-crossover.limitations: Only one English-source plant per length was made. The random ciphertext/key null is not a model of all wrong puzzle keys, the planned shuffle surrogate was not run, and no LP2 keys were screened. The permissive drift channel has a distinct left-tail artifact; the skip-by-two mechanism fails recovery. The labels on the 6,000-rune panel are English windows, not language corpora.

scope.representation: Source-planted GP-index ciphertexts of ten lengths from 400 through 12,956 runes, paired with their correct keystream; uniform random GP-index ciphertext and key pairs form each 300-trial null. No unsolved LP2 ciphertext is decoded.
scope.procedure: First reproduce the L400 and L12956 source gates; then run its ten-length ladder for exact keyskip1 and permissive drift decoders, the separate skip-by-two plant curve, and four additional 6,000-rune English-window labels. Compare correct-key skip counts with exact empirical null tails and require at least 90% planted recovery.
scope.parameters: Seed 3301; support 0.83; lengths 400, 600, 900, 1,200, 1,600, 2,400, 3,600, 6,000, 9,000, 12,956; 300 null decodes for each of 20 unique length/mode groups; 34 reported cells; empirical two-sided bar 0.01.
scope.exclusions: Other plaintext windows or distributions, other skip mechanisms or decoder transition rules, a complete key search, LP2 test pages, alternative nulls and the order-preserving shuffle surrogate mentioned in the plan.

public-p20-static-boundary.title: A bounded test of the P20 boundary model
public-p20-static-boundary.question: Has the proposed P20 static boundary rule been checked?
public-p20-static-boundary.finding: Across 34,020 allowed state-pair assignments at eight contexts, six lower-complexity classes have zero complete fits and the saturated (6,6) class has five. An independent exact calculation gives 4.94 expected and P(at least five)=0.552. Two planted low-complexity laws are recovered exactly.
public-p20-static-boundary.limitations: The original raw workspace is absent. We did not independently derive the eight numeric menus or feature vectors from LP2, and this conditional replay does not decode a page or exclude dynamic boundary rules. The pinned source's manifest also names two absent files, so its quick verifier does not pass.

scope.representation: Eight source-supplied numeric boundary contexts for an 812-rune section named P20 by the external repository; no asserted mapping to one Liberpedia page.
scope.procedure: Verify pinned Git blobs, execute source scripts 33, 35 and 38 in isolation, compare regenerated JSON objects, and independently calculate the menu product and exact conditioned tail.
scope.parameters: 34,020 assignments; seven joint feature-count classes over GF(83), including saturated (6,6); conditioned c18 menu of nine state pairs; two planted affine laws plus one-value mutations.
scope.exclusions: Original raw-data derivation, all other static or dynamic state models, independent manuscript decryption, and other sections of LP2.

public-prng-seed-sweep.title: Seven seeded generator streams against LP2
public-prng-seed-sweep.question: Could the LP2 key stream come from a seeded random-number generator?
public-prng-seed-sweep.finding: The strongest manuscript candidate scored −6.347 against a required −5.500. The planted control scored −4.155 with full recovery. The replay's winner and score match the original run.
public-prng-seed-sweep.limitations: The executed source tested daily-spaced seeds rather than the hourly seeds in its plan, mod-29 reduction only, offset zero and the source's own implementations. PHP, .NET and ISAAC reference vectors in this script are self-generated, not independent runtime checks. No other generators, reductions, seeds, offsets, languages or key-skip rules are excluded.

scope.representation: The source's 12,956-byte zero-based GP rune stream; first 120 runes scored under its English quadgram model.
scope.procedure: Run the source's seven generators for each of its 1,877 fixed seeds; decode both signs and both directions with its beam width 400 and maximum three rejected symbols; compare scores to the fixed −5.5 bar and 200 shuffled-prefix nulls.
scope.parameters: Seven implementations × 1,877 seeds × 2 signs × 2 directions = 52,556 decodes; modulo-29 reduction, key offset zero, 120-rune screen.
scope.exclusions: Hourly seed grid in the plan, rejection reduction, other generators or seeding conventions, nonzero offsets, longer first-stage screens, other scoring languages, and other key-skip transition rules.

public-rsa-payload-e01.title: Whole grid payload under public RSA moduli
public-rsa-payload-e01.question: Could the number-grid bytes be an RSA block?
public-rsa-payload-e01.finding: Zero strict or loose structural matches in 162 valid RSA public-power checks; 12 source encodings excluded because s≥n. Original planted signature controls and 10,000 random-block controls passed.
public-rsa-payload-e01.limitations: Only three pinned payload readings, two valid PGP moduli, source encodings, three exponents and three structural predicates. Public exponentiation cannot decrypt an RSA ciphertext. The 432-bit 2013 modulus admits no whole-payload input.

scope.representation: Three pinned 256-byte readings of the printed base-60 grid as one complete value; two 4096-bit published PGP moduli, with the 432-bit 2013 modulus checked for fit.
scope.procedure: Replay pinned E-01 public exponentiation and PKCS#1 v1.5 signature/encryption plus PSS padding checks on valid endian/alignment representations, exponents 65537, 3 and 17.
scope.parameters: 3 payloads; 2 usable PGP moduli; 3 valid encodings per PGP modulus; 3 exponents; 3 structural predicates = 162 evaluated matcher rows. Twelve source encodings excluded for s≥n, including every 2013-modulus case.
scope.exclusions: Private-key RSA decryption, 54-byte windows within the payload, other key pairs, other padding or payload readings.

public-wordlist-vigenere.title: Public 43-key Vigenère sweep
public-wordlist-vigenere.question: Did the public wordlist Vigenère sweep turn any unsolved page start into a known reading?
public-wordlist-vigenere.finding: Full archived output matches in 2,494/2,494 cases across 58 pages and 43 keys. The original fixed-opening test remains 0/21,285 exact comparisons.
public-wordlist-vigenere.limitations: The 12-rune negative result covers only phase-zero page starts, this source key list, our transcription and nine exact openings. Complete source-output reproduction confirms the archived transform but not the source informal no-good-result judgment, which has no declared language-score threshold.

scope.representation: LP2-00–55 rune stream in canonical 29-rune GP order; LP2-50 is number-only.
scope.procedure: Subtract each source key modulo 29 at page phase zero; compare nine fixed 12-rune openings on LP2-00–55; separately verify complete Latin rune-label streams for all 58 archived pages.
scope.parameters: 43 archived keys, 58 complete source pages (56 unsolved-page opening-test pages), nine 12-rune openings, 21,285 exact opening comparisons.
scope.exclusions: Other keys, phases, directions, word resets, page segments, languages, and semantic assessment of the complete plaintext strings.

py27-prior-front-opening-cribs.title: Python 2.7 priority seeds against fixed LP2 openings
py27-prior-front-opening-cribs.question: Could the Python 2.7 priority seeds produce a familiar LP2 opening?
py27-prior-front-opening-cribs.finding: All 45,975 source priority words were reconstructed and crossed with the four source reducer and ABI settings. The exact keyskip1 path test found zero complete openings, with maximum feasible prefix five; 183,356 of the 183,900 cases have different first-45-symbol key streams. This new fixed-crib result does not replay the source's English-panel screen.
py27-prior-front-opening-cribs.limitations: Only nine predeclared openings at 55 page starts in LP2-00–55 were tested. It assumes source sign -1, no Atbash, zero starting offset and the exact keyskip1 collision rule. Other plaintexts, offsets, transitions, seeds beyond the priority front and later positions remain untested. The source's original 884,000-case language-panel claim is separate and not reproduced here.

scope.representation: Canonical GP29 transcription; first 12 runes of every nonempty LP2-00–55 page (LP2-50 is blank); nine fixed 12-rune known-reading openings.
scope.procedure: Rebuild the source's exact 45,975-word ordered priority front. For each word, generate all four source Python 2.7 reducer and ABI key prefixes. Test exact existential keyskip1 paths against fixed page-start openings, with no beam pruning or English score.
scope.parameters: 45,975 priority words × grb5_mod_i386, grb5_rej_i386, shuffle29_i386, random29_amd64 = 183,900 generated cases; source sign -1, no Atbash, zero offset, up to three collision-rejected key draws per rune; nine openings and 55 page starts.
scope.exclusions: Later dense seed words, other reducers, another Python runtime or ABI map, different starting offsets, keyskip2, other plaintexts, alternate rune transcriptions, non-page-start matches and the unavailable source language-panel verdict.

py27-reducer-sweep-source-audit.title: Python 2.7 reducer sweep: source and control audit
py27-reducer-sweep-source-audit.question: Were the Python 2.7 random reducers tried on LP2?
py27-reducer-sweep-source-audit.finding: All 95 pinned Stage-B rows reconcile with the source aggregate; none reaches the 7.6342 final score bar. The 45,975-word proposed-seed front reconstructs. The source-reported 884,000 Stage-A tests cannot be replayed from public bytes, and the 4/4 saved positive controls do not exercise Stage A. The source prose also counts 71 perfect-recovery rows where its receipt contains 67.
py27-reducer-sweep-source-audit.limitations: This audits saved receipts and control wiring, not the absent 884,000 first-stage scores or the original panel calibration. It makes no claim about unscreened words, other keystreams, other decoders, or other plaintext registers.

scope.representation: The source's canonical LP2 numeric stream; first 120 runes of LP2-00 screened and first 240 assessed after promotion. This audit inspects pinned source outputs and code, not a fresh cipher decode.
scope.procedure: Hash the pinned source files; independently reconcile all saved survivor rows and aggregate counts; reconstruct the proposed-seed front; inspect source call paths for the two-stage gate; inventory unavailable model inputs.
scope.parameters: Four pinned reducer/map configurations; source-reported 884,000 screened words; 95 saved promoted rows; screening score bar 5.0 and final score bar 7.6342.
scope.exclusions: No replacement panel trained on different corpora; no unverified source rerun; no inference about unsaved Stage-A scores or the other 99.99% of each nominal word space.

quagmirror-six-rune-replay.title: QuagMirror draft: replay of its first six runes
quagmirror-six-rune-replay.question: What does the pinned QuagMirror script actually produce before its debug stop?
quagmirror-six-rune-replay.finding: Independent replay agrees with the script: autokey indices 15,28,2,10,3,14 and output indices 23,5,17,7,11,3 transliterate to DCBWJO. The source has an explicit break after six positions.
quagmirror-six-rune-replay.limitations: The public repository contains multiple changing variants. This record covers only the pinned file and its six-position debug prefix. DCBWJO is not a coherent plaintext and no complete output is present.

scope.representation: Archived LP2-00 first six runes as zero-based GP indices; nine 29-entry substitution tables from the pinned draft script.
scope.procedure: Recalculate the source autokey and Möbius-driven table selection for its six executed positions, including the two explicit startup overrides; compare intermediate and final streams with the source stdout.
scope.parameters: Pinned source commit 88ef1e60; first six cipher indices 15,8,18,3,6,19; first-position and second-position overrides retained.
scope.exclusions: All positions beyond six, alternative repository drafts, thematic key search, full-page plaintext or English-score controls.

quagmirror-variant-continuations.title: Three QuagMirror drafts and their actual stopping points
quagmirror-variant-continuations.question: Do the other QuagMirror drafts continue into a complete reading?
quagmirror-variant-continuations.finding: The original, version-4 and WIP drafts process 153, 49 and 500 of 729 source runes. They print some wordlike fragments but none reaches the end of its input, and no planted recovery control or held-out reading is supplied.
quagmirror-variant-continuations.limitations: The scripts are separate drafts with handwritten tables and different recurrences. Exact output agreement does not establish a decipherment. Source version 4's skip at index 17 does not advance its loop counter, so its 48-index stop occurs after 49 input positions. This record does not choose new mirror rules or extend any script past its own stop.

scope.representation: The source's 729 zero-based rune indices, equal to the concatenated LP2-00–02 transcription after normalizing the J-rune glyph alias; source-specific 29-entry mirrors and Latin fragment mapping.
scope.procedure: Execute each pinned script without editing its stop, skip list or tables; extract its ciphertext, autokey and plaintext-index rows and complete formatted output; independently compare source input with manuscript pages, nine mirror permutations and transliteration.
scope.parameters: Pinned commit 88ef1e60b0738b8b28db96bc9dc44dc4da8dd307; original stops at 153 positions, version 4 at 49 because of its counter behavior, and WIP at 500; no searched wordlist or retuned alphabet.
scope.exclusions: Positions beyond each source stop, other QuagMirror revisions, alternative initial states, regenerated mirror tables, a new complete decryption rule, planted-recovery power and held-out manuscript validation.

r18-drift-ladder-replay.title: Can skipped key draws shift a page start?
r18-drift-ladder-replay.question: Could we miss a correct key by starting too early?
r18-drift-ladder-replay.finding: The true key ranks first on all three planted pages at corrected offsets, where its scores are -3.95 to -4.19; uncorrected starts score -6.94 to -7.33. Among 230 candidates across 55 nonempty page starts, the best new corrected score is -6.012 and the best overall -5.885 at a prior restart control; none reaches the source -5.5 reading bar. All 230 source candidate rows replay after a documented staged-input amendment.
r18-drift-ladder-replay.limitations: This tests 100-rune page starts under one continuous key-skip law, a score-selected 230-key list, a four-standard-deviation offset band, and a historical English-score gate. It does not exclude other keys, global starting positions, longer segments, or different skip rules.

scope.representation: Gematria Primus indices from the source transcription; 55 nonempty LP2-00–55 pages, with source ordinal 52 mapped to LP2-53.
scope.procedure: Run F0 parity gate, replay the three-page planted offset control, and search 230 source-mined key candidates at 5,961 offsets each over first 100 runes of every nonempty page; compare all candidate rows with pinned source output.
scope.parameters: Suppression 0.8129; beam width 400; maximum three skipped draws; predicted key offset start+rho*start with +/-4 standard deviations, plus uncorrected and restart controls; English-score gate -5.5.
scope.exclusions: Keys outside earlier top lists, other global key origins, text after each page first 100 runes, alternate boundaries or filter laws, source B5 skip-count channel.

r18-entropy-budget-replay.title: What can an entropy budget tell us?
r18-entropy-budget-replay.question: Do the missing repeats give enough information to solve LP2?
r18-entropy-budget-replay.finding: The source measures 2.568 bits/rune as the best of six KJV held-out Markov test scores and 62,617 ciphertext bits under its fitted uniform-pad Markov law. In its 256-bit-seed row, the source input proxy is only 33,525 bits while it reuses that 62,617-bit output law: a 29,091-bit conditional mismatch unless the model adds uncounted randomness or a different output distribution. The five source budget rows and all source fields reproduce exactly.
r18-entropy-budget-replay.limitations: The English cross-entropy is one KJV segment and the best order is chosen on the same test set; it is not measured LP2 plaintext entropy. The source’s exact uniform-key conditional-channel theorem is already covered separately. This audit does not show LP2 has any particular key, language, filter, or decryption.

scope.representation: Source’s joined 12,956 LP2 rune events for fitted repeat rate; exact recovered KJV text converted to GP29, 400,000 train and 200,000 test runes.
scope.procedure: Replay full source C calculation in temporary checkout; independently verify Markov output-entropy, corpus-score selection, conditional repeat law, five arithmetic budget rows, sensitivity rows, and the low-seed model-entropy mismatch.
scope.parameters: GP29; fitted suppression 0.8129; KJV Markov orders 0–5; 1,000 Monte Carlo arms per plaintext; hypothetical full-pad and 40/256/64/32-bit seed key budgets.
scope.exclusions: Re-estimating actual LP2 plaintext entropy, other corpora or ciphers, empirical unique decryption, and any proof that no finite-key model can solve LP2.

r18-filter-locus-replay.title: Where could a repeat filter act?
r18-filter-locus-replay.question: Could a filter explain LP2’s scarce repeated runes?
r18-filter-locus-replay.finding: The manuscript has 86 adjacent repeats among 12,955 pairs (0.664%). Simulated key skipping and random output rewriting give 0.633% and 0.668%. The source classifier has only 17.5% in-sample power to separate those two at its 5% false-positive threshold. A fixed +1 nudge matches repeats but produces a much larger modular-difference peak (16.5 versus 2.64 standardized units).
r18-filter-locus-replay.limitations: The source tunes suppression to the observed repeat rate and fits/evaluates its classifier on the same 200 simulations per model. This conditional comparison does not identify the manuscript encryptor or rule out other filters, keys, plaintexts or reset conventions.

scope.representation: Joined canonical 29-rune LP2-00–55 stream (12,956 runes) and the source’s exact KJV-derived GP29 plaintext.
scope.procedure: Replay all seven pinned source models at 200 simulations each; compare every non-timing field with the preserved source JSON. Independently recount manuscript statistics and analytic draw-count formula.
scope.parameters: Source revision f08b20b; 200 seeded simulations/model; source-calibrated suppression; five fixed primary statistics; source 5% false-positive classifier threshold.
scope.exclusions: Other corpora, nonuniform or dependent keys, other filter rules, alternative segment boundaries, held-out classifier evaluation, and actual decryption.

r18-keyskip-drift-power.title: Can a correct key survive skipped draws?
r18-keyskip-drift-power.question: Could key skipping make a correct key look wrong?
r18-keyskip-drift-power.finding: Given the correct key, the skip-aware decoder recovered 99.97% of the plaintext on average in three full-length simulations.
r18-keyskip-drift-power.limitations: These simulations use one English source and one proposed skip rule. This result does not show that LP2 uses that rule or identify its key.

scope.representation: 12,956-rune synthetic GP29 ciphertext built from the pinned KJV source text and SHA-256-counter key; LP2 contributes only the previously measured repeat-rate calibration.
scope.procedure: Replay source F0 reference-versus-fast-beam gate, B1 200 drift samples, B2 six lengths × 200 planted windows, B3 six lengths × three planted keys plus one wrong-key full-length control; compare all non-timing source fields.
scope.parameters: Source revision f08b20b; suppression 0.8129; beam width 400; maximum three skipped draws per step; reading score gate -5.5 and minimum planted rune recovery 90%.
scope.exclusions: Real LP2 key search, other language/key/filter families, independent held-out classifier power, source B.4 ladder and later R18 subattacks.

r18-skip-channel-power.title: Can inferred key skips distinguish a correct key?
r18-skip-channel-power.question: Do the missing repeats reveal which key is right?
r18-skip-channel-power.finding: None of the 20 tested LP2 key candidates produced a supported reading. The largest inferred skip count, 353, was within the wrong-key range of 260–357.
r18-skip-channel-power.limitations: The skip count depends on paths chosen for their English-language score. One known-key simulation is not enough to measure how reliably it identifies correct keys.

scope.representation: Source's 12,956-rune concatenated GP29 LP2 stream and separately generated synthetic English-rune encrypted stream.
scope.procedure: Run the unchanged B5 stage: known true key on plant; forty wrong keys each on plant and full LP2; then the source's twenty selected real candidate keystreams. Compare saved original null arrays and full new ranking.
scope.parameters: Source skip suppression 0.8129, maximum three skips per rune, English-quadgram beam width 400, source KJV corpus and deterministic seeds; 40+40 null decodes and 20 candidate decodes over 12,956 runes.
scope.exclusions: Unselected keys, other skip models, other language scorers, a repeated true-key power study, source B4 offset search and any complete plaintext validation.

r21-fold-tail-scope-controls.title: Which part of a decode does the fold check verify?
r21-fold-tail-scope-controls.question: Can a consistency check leave part of a decoded page unverified?
r21-fold-tail-scope-controls.finding: The helper checks overlapping right tails; it never compares the first fold of reference indices and skips the final fold.
r21-fold-tail-scope-controls.limitations: Known-key diagnostic controls; no manuscript key, complete hit decision or original hallucination catch surface is tested.

scope.representation: One source-derived 240-rune English plaintext window; six newly enciphered GP29 known-key plants.
scope.procedure: Execute unchanged source class/helper definitions selected by AST, real source encoder and beam; trace prefix/tail calls, compare diagnostic reference edits, independently recount encryption and agreements.
scope.parameters: Seeds 3301,3302,3303; suppression 0/.83; k2..6; min/mean/frac_pass; beam400 exact/keyskip1; offset0; sign-1; 2000 key symbols.
scope.exclusions: Original hallucination selection, calibrated nine-register adjudication, full hit gate, wrong-key false-pass rates, manuscript search and other fold/proxy implementations.

r26-derived-generators-opening-cribs.title: Older random generators against fixed LP2 openings
r26-derived-generators-opening-cribs.question: Have the proposed older random generators been checked against familiar openings?
r26-derived-generators-opening-cribs.finding: None of the tested older random-generator keys reproduced a complete known 12-rune opening. Across 24,231 generated key cases and two skip rules, the closest match was four runes.
r26-derived-generators-opening-cribs.limitations: Only nine specified beginnings at the starts of 55 pages were checked, with the saved seeds, subtraction direction and starting offsets. This does not test unknown openings or repeat the source’s broader English-scoring search.

scope.representation: Current canonical GP29 transcription; first 12 runes on each of 55 nonempty LP2 pages. Nine fixed, published 12-rune known-reading openings.
scope.procedure: Regenerate each R26-A source keystream from the exact ordered dictionary and dense baseline. Check existential fixed-plaintext skip paths under exact and pair source presets, sign -1, no Atbash. No English scoring or beam pruning.
scope.parameters: 312 dictionary integer seeds plus 400 dense integers for eight Perl reductions and four TeX generators; 347 dictionary entries plus 400 dense integers for three Python 2.7 reducers at 64-bit wordsize and offsets 0,1,2,3,5,7,13. Each generated case gets exact/keyskip1 and pair/keyskip2 preset. 24,231 generated cases (19,986 distinct first-100-symbol streams); 48,462 rows; 55 nonempty page starts in LP2-00–55; nine cribs.
scope.exclusions: Different plaintext openings, later positions, other source seed classes, full 32- or 64-bit key spaces, reverse stream, other decode signs, Atbash, word reset, altered transcriptions, and the source's original English-panel verdict.

r28-c-generator-port-controls.title: Finite checks of the C generator ports
r28-c-generator-port-controls.question: Does the C port generate the same keys as the reference models?
r28-c-generator-port-controls.finding: The C implementations produced the same output as the reference models in every comparison: 152,192 symbols checked.
r28-c-generator-port-controls.limitations: This verifies these generator implementations on a fixed test set. It does not rerun the seed search or recover manuscript text.

scope.representation: GP29 generator outputs; finite model streams and archived vectors.
scope.procedure: Compile unchanged source generator region; compare every symbol against source models and independently built expectations.
scope.parameters: 9 modes x 8 seeds x 2000 symbols; 64 archived random29 vectors x 128 symbols.
scope.exclusions: Language-panel scores, plant/decoder recovery, native runtime parity, all LP2 searches and fullspace coverage.

rail-fence-visible-words.title: Rail-fence readings of visible LP2 words
rail-fence-visible-words.question: Does writing each page into a rail-fence zigzag reveal English words?
rail-fence-visible-words.finding: The best printed-alignment score is 70 words for rails 2, 4 and 9, compared with a control median of 78. There are 195 of 199 control maxima at least as large as 70; a one-sided plus-one tail is 196/200.
rail-fence-visible-words.limitations: The score uses exact dictionary membership, not sentence coherence. The dictionary includes obscure words and the page-rotation null is an alignment comparison, not a cipher generator. This result cannot exclude a layered or differently segmented rail cipher.

scope.representation: LP2-00–55 GP rune indices; each visible hyphen-delimited segment is a fixed word slot, preserving page boundaries. The English lexicon is a pinned, filtered public word list.
scope.procedure: For each page, apply the standard rail-fence inverse with rail counts 2–10; transliterate the resulting runes in the original word slots and count exact English-list hits. Compare the printed-order best of nine with 199 seeded controls that independently rotate each page by a nonzero offset before repeating the identical nine-way selection. Verify the inverse on LP1-03 and check manuscript counts through a separate permutation implementation.
scope.parameters: 56 LP2 pages; 12,956 runes; 2,776 visible word slots; 369,652 dictionary entries; 2–10 rails; 199 controls, random.Random(3301); ties count against the proposed alignment.
scope.exclusions: Other rail counts, grouping pages, changed word boundaries, keyed or other transpositions, preceding substitution layers, other languages and alternate lexicons. Original source counts are not claimed as reproduced because its dictionary and input paths are unavailable.

red-initial-presence-order.title: LP2 red initials: corrected page-order test
red-initial-presence-order.question: Once pages with ordinary red text are removed, is the pattern of pages with large red initials unusually spaced?
red-initial-presence-order.finding: No declared spacing measure is unusual for a uniform 13-of-58 subset. The internal-gap variance is 12.85 (upper-tail estimate 0.328); the longest run is two (exact upper-tail 0.968); the span is 57 (exact lower-tail 1). The zlib score is 16 bytes, matched by 99977 of 100000 random subsets. These are narrow page-order results, not a proof against hidden information.
red-initial-presence-order.limitations: Two pages in the earlier 15-page list contain only small red text. The page-order test has narrow bounds, and its compression measure has little power on a 58-bit string.

scope.representation: Binary page presence from the archived JPEG image audit: at least one red component of 10000 full-resolution-equivalent pixels, measured with four-connectivity after half-resolution sampling. The original JPEG SHA-256 values are recorded per row in the audit CSV.
scope.procedure: Compare 13 corrected page positions with uniform 13-page subsets of 58; test internal-gap variance in both directions and packed-bit compression with 100000 seeded samples; count span and adjacent-run tails exactly; run evenly spaced and consecutive planted controls.
scope.parameters: Pages 00–57; 13 selected; random.Random(3301) with 100000 subsets; zlib level 9; plus-one Monte Carlo tails; five tail directions with Bonferroni correction.
scope.exclusions: Initial-rune identities, multiple initials on one page, red centroids, nonuniform authorship or section-placement models, alternate image segmentation, arbitrary encodings and any complete decryption rule.

rejection-channel-information.title: What a collision filter reveals under a random key
rejection-channel-information.question: Do the missing doublets point toward plaintext?
rejection-channel-information.finding: Under the stated independent uniform-key model, each filter's visible next-symbol law is plaintext-independent. Skip and rewrite filters can have identical visible laws while differing by about 374 expected extra key draws over 12,955 transitions.
rejection-channel-information.limitations: This proves only a conditional model identity. It does not identify the LP2 generator, test real keys or decrypt a page. Both filters are fitted to the observed repeat count; source English-corpus entropy and Monte Carlo arms are not replayed because their exact corpora are unavailable.

scope.representation: LP2's aggregate 86 equal adjacent pairs among 12,955 pairs; no LP2 rune stream is decoded.
scope.procedure: Fit skip and rewrite parameters to the aggregate repeat rate, derive the conditional output and key-draw laws, compare with the source's preserved closed forms, and verify a nontrivial finite-field control exhaustively.
scope.parameters: 29-symbol alphabet, 12,956 rune events, independent uniform key, memory of previous visible ciphertext symbol, one-step filter law; exact N=3 oracle with skip s=1/2 and rewrite t=3/5.
scope.exclusions: Structured or plaintext-dependent keys, reset variants, actual LP2 plaintext/key recovery, source English-corpus entropy estimates and original stochastic simulations.

relikd-autokey-interrupt-database.title: Saved autokey scores with selectable interruptions
relikd-autokey-interrupt-database.question: Did the saved autokey and interruption scores decode a passage?
relikd-autokey-interrupt-database.finding: All eight saved score files reproduce, but an elevated coincidence score is not a decoded message. The known-text control works only with the inserted interruption positions supplied.
relikd-autokey-interrupt-database.limitations: Thirteen whole and eight partial pages entered any saved score. Seven files lack an active source call in this revision, and the skip/primer selection has no matched null.

scope.representation: Nine pinned section streams verified against all 56 LP2-00..55 site page JSON files. The actual scored-position union covers 13 complete and eight partial pages across eight databases; 35 do not contribute. The called -p file covers 12 complete and eight partial pages. Inverted files select source index28 before mapping c to 28-c.
scope.procedure: Audit eight committed database files, recomputing every row's first-16-interruption cutoff, selected deletion, primer-dependent plaintext feedback and normalized whole-prefix coincidence score. Independently reconstruct eight complete known-text controls and map scored positions to page records.
scope.parameters: GP29 prime/index previous-plaintext feedback × plus/minus sign × original/inverted input; primer field 0..28 with source field0-to-primer1 behavior; 2,412 saved rows, eight 96-rune controls with three declared inserted interruptions.
scope.exclusions: No fresh 2^16 skip-mask search, whole-search null, OEIS corpus, word resets, other signs/functions or LP2 plaintext claim.

relikd-interrupt-db-keyfit.title: Interrupt-key fits needed a stronger known-text check
relikd-interrupt-db-keyfit.question: Did removing selected F runes reveal a readable key or message?
relikd-interrupt-db-keyfit.finding: Thirteen saved LP2 key fits pass the source score limit, but six comparable planted known messages are only partly recovered. No readable message has been established.
relikd-interrupt-db-keyfit.limitations: The original branch was unreachable and these are nine saved candidates, not a full interrupt search. The control failure prevents a negative claim about Vigenère or affine ciphers.

scope.representation: The exact three pinned source section streams p0-2, p27-32 and p40-53 agree with site rune data, including empty LP2-50. Nine saved database rows are fitted on section prefixes; the fitted keys are then applied to the full 22 nonempty pages across those sections.
scope.procedure: Extract the otherwise unreachable source break_cipher saved-row branch. For each row, delete its declared F occurrences before the twenty-first F from the fit prefix, fit both original source key models, and decode the complete section with source skip-clock semantics. Independently recount fits and decoded hashes.
scope.parameters: Nine source database rows selected by interrupt F and score at least 0.55; two source fitters (18 outputs); source mean-similarity limits 0.05 and 0.04; six matched-length known-text controls plus solved-page and short skip-clock controls.
scope.exclusions: No regeneration of interrupt database rows, no other interruption rune, altered language model, arbitrary key length, additional LP2 section, new plaintext scorer or whole-family exclusion.

relikd-interrupt-pattern-database.title: Mirror and alternating-group interrupt scores
relikd-interrupt-pattern-database.question: Did the saved mirror and alternating-group scores uncover a message?
relikd-interrupt-pattern-database.finding: Every saved score can be reproduced, but a high rune-frequency score is not a decrypted message. The known-period control is imperfect, and the original skip-mask selection was not repeated on controls.
relikd-interrupt-pattern-database.limitations: The score archive covers 44 whole pages and parts of seven more. It cannot tell whether the selected high scores reflect a cipher, chance after a large search, or an untested rule.

scope.representation: Nine exact pinned source section rune streams were checked against 56 site page JSON files. Forty-four pages enter at least one saved score completely and seven enter partially; four text pages plus empty LP2-50 are verified-only. F or EA stops are taken from committed db_indices and the source's first-20-interrupt cutoff.
scope.procedure: Parse and independently recount every committed mirror/modulo database row with exact source group and skip-clock rules. Apply each of 24 source scoring arms to a planted known-text period-5 construction, then run a labeled post-target 49-replicate known-control shuffle diagnostic. Compute exact actual page contribution from scored rune positions.
scope.parameters: Mirror a/b × high/norm (4 files), modulo-a and modulo-b for moduli 2/3 and all subgroups × high/norm (10 files each); 7,407 saved rows, 24 known-period controls, candidate periods 2–8, 49 post-target shuffles per control.
scope.exclusions: No fresh search over all interruption masks; no LP2 selection-adjusted p-value, candidate key recovery, plaintext language test, OEIS database search or uncommitted source branch.

relikd-rotated-key-source-gate.title: A rotating-key search stopped at its first screen
relikd-rotated-key-source-gate.question: Did this rotating-key search produce any candidate readings?
relikd-rotated-key-source-gate.finding: This rotating-key search produced no candidate readings. Every LP2 setting stopped at its initial repeat-frequency screen, so no keys were fitted. A deliberately encrypted known text was recovered correctly.
relikd-rotated-key-source-gate.limitations: The search covered 26 complete pages and parts of seven more. Its successful control was longer than every searched section; shorter texts and other rotating-key rules remain open.

scope.representation: Nine exact committed LiberPrayground section files for LP2-00–55; site rune streams match in full. Actual searched prefixes include 26 complete pages and seven partial pages. Source punctuation and line handling determine the first-970-symbol prefix before removing non-runes; 22 other nonempty pages were only verified against source bytes.
scope.procedure: Repair one integer-to-generator call using the source's shift_pattern helper; retain the nine sections, k3–18, step1..k−1, all phases, strict source IoC and similarity gates. Verify a 970-rune known reading and 49 shared whole-grid within-section shuffles.
scope.parameters: 1,936 key schedule settings per section; nine sections and 17,424 target settings; source IoC in (1.6,2.1), similarity <0.1; one complete known-text planted control and 49 complete-search shuffles.
scope.exclusions: No result from unmodified probability.py, no source-unreachable interrupt/affine branch, alternate plaintext distribution, other rotating or mirrored generators, altered key range or source-model repair.

relikd-trigram-shift-control.title: Three-rune shift display: recovery control
relikd-trigram-shift-control.question: If fragments look like English, did the method recover the page?
relikd-trigram-shift-control.finding: The highest-scoring row still had 78 wrong runes out of 207. The tool found some correct fragments, but did not recover the known page well enough for the planned LP2 test.
relikd-trigram-shift-control.limitations: Only known readings were tested; the scorer's training overlap is unknown.

scope.representation: 17 already decoded GP29 rune streams, 15 from LP1 and the two solved LP2 end pages, each shifted by +7 modulo 29.
scope.procedure: Execute pinned NGramShifter on each page at three starting positions, preserving all 29 ranked local shifts per block; score complete printed rows and compare with 49 shared within-page shuffles.
scope.parameters: 51 page/start displays; 29 rank rows each; 100 scored quadgram eligibility; selected recovery >=70% and score above >=47/49 shuffle maxima required before any target screen.
scope.exclusions: No unsolved LP2 target, global key constraint, interrupted cipher, validation of unknown key laws, or held-out language-model claim.

repeated-long-ngrams.title: Are the long LP2 rune repeats unusual?
repeated-long-ngrams.question: Does the repeated DJUBEI sequence point to a repeating key?
repeated-long-ngrams.finding: The source counts reproduce: six distinct five-rune repeats, one six-rune repeat (DJUBEI), no seven-rune repeats. Of 999 sectionwise step-shuffled controls, 300 meet the five-rune threshold, 150 meet the six-rune threshold, and 361 meet either; the combined plus-one proportion is 362/1,000.
repeated-long-ngrams.limitations: The control conditions on observed step inventories and nine section boundaries; it is a comparison distribution, not a cipher simulator. The combined threshold covers selection between lengths five and six only, not all possible methods or motifs.

scope.representation: 12,956 GP rune indices, concatenated in manuscript order from LP2-00 through LP2-55; non-runes removed.
scope.procedure: Count distinct repeated contiguous rune-index tuples at lengths 5, 6 and 7, including overlapping windows and joins. Rebuild 999 sectionwise step-shuffled controls, count each length, and compare fixed-length and either-length selection thresholds.
scope.parameters: Nine declared unsolved sections; 29-symbol modular steps; 999 random.Random(3301) controls; upper-tail ties included; one planted six-rune copy.
scope.exclusions: Other transcriptions, gaps and noncontiguous motifs, alternate segmentation, longer lengths, specific plaintext or key tests, and selection over further search choices.

rotating-folded-key-openings.title: Rotating and folded wordlist keys
rotating-folded-key-openings.question: Could changing the key as it repeats reveal a familiar opening?
rotating-folded-key-openings.finding: Zero of 3,104,640 exact comparisons match; the longest shared prefix is four runes. Planted controls and independent census pass.
rotating-folded-key-openings.limitations: Only four declared schedules, 43 keys, page starts and nine fixed openings. Different plaintexts, keys or key rules remain possible.

scope.representation: First 12 recognized GP29 runes per LP2-00–55 page, including headings; LP2-50 has no runes. Non-runes do not advance the key.
scope.procedure: Expand each key by left/right cycle rotation or forward/backward folding with/without repeated endpoints. Reduce to true period; test every phase; subtract scheduled key index modulo 29.
scope.parameters: 43 keys; four expansions; 6,272 settings; 55 pages; nine 12-rune openings; 3,104,640 comparisons.
scope.exclusions: Other keys, later positions, unknown openings, alternate signs, resets, interruptions, layers and language scoring.

round19-decoder-baseline-control.title: When a pair-skip decoder loses a known key
round19-decoder-baseline-control.question: Could the wrong skip rule make a correct key look wrong?
round19-decoder-baseline-control.finding: At suppression 0.83, median exact rune recovery is 100% with the matching decoder at both 240 and 400 runes, versus 37.9% and 41.2% with the pair-skip decoder. All 336 non-timing replay rows and 48 cell summaries match the pinned source output.
round19-decoder-baseline-control.limitations: Synthetic known-key ciphertext from one English-derived source; no LP2 ciphertext or unknown-key search. A failure under one alignment rule cannot exclude other rules. Source score bar -5.5 is not a calibrated family-wide error rate.

scope.representation: Synthetic English-derived GP29 rune ciphertext, correct source key supplied to each decoder.
scope.procedure: Replay source G-BASE: four suppression settings, two lengths, six decoder modes, seven seeds; compare every non-timing row and independently recount all 48 cells.
scope.parameters: Source revision f08b20b; lengths 240/400; suppression 0/.4/.83/1; beam width 400; source score bar -5.5 and 90% rune-recovery gate.
scope.exclusions: Real LP2 ciphertext, unknown-key search, source G-FIX/G-COST and G-FP grids, other skip models or independent language calibration.

round19-decoder-null-bars.title: When wrong keys cross a language-score line
round19-decoder-null-bars.question: Could a wrong key look convincing just because the decoder has more freedom?
round19-decoder-null-bars.finding: Changing decoder rules changed how often wrong keys cleared the same score cutoff: 500 of 500 in one permissive setting, versus 0 of 2,000 in the repository setting. Crossing that line is not a decipherment.
round19-decoder-null-bars.limitations: Saved wrong-key decoder scores are source outputs; the 34,000 beam decodes were not rerun. The reserved-row check is internal to those arrays at small block sizes. Gumbel bars for one million or one billion trials are model extrapolations, not measured error rates. A high score is not a plaintext or an LP2 cipher identification.

scope.representation: Archived wrong-key English-score rows under real LP2 ciphertext and synthetic source controls; no plaintext candidate output is evaluated here.
scope.procedure: Run the pinned source fit over 34,000 saved rows; compare all 26 fit records, independently recount the fit arithmetic and test an alternating-row diagnostic at observed block sizes.
scope.parameters: Source samples have 240 runes and beam width 400; wrong keys use SHA256-counter seeds WRONGKEY-%08d. 13 decoder modes × real/synthetic source nulls; 500–2,000 scores per mode/null cell; source 40 seeded block partitions, two block sizes, Gumbel 1% family-wise projections to 10^6 and 10^9; diagnostic blocks 10/25/50 with 80 seeded held-out partitions.
scope.exclusions: Re-execution of the 34,000 source beam searches, independent validation of million/billion-trial tails, manuscript key discovery, alternative scorers, other decoders and general LP2 cipher exclusion.

round19-decoder-repair-controls.title: Can a correct key look wrong to the decoder?
round19-decoder-repair-controls.question: Could a decoder mistake the right key for a failed decryption?
round19-decoder-repair-controls.finding: Same known message and key: 45.8% recovery with the original beam versus 100% with permissive drift. Across source-gated groups: 0/20 versus 20/20.
round19-decoder-repair-controls.limitations: This checks the decoder on planted text; the source replay differs in tiny score bits and does not test an unknown LP2 key.

scope.representation: Synthetic English-derived GP29 rune ciphertext from the pinned Self-Reliance text; the construction and correct key are given to each decoder.
scope.procedure: Replay the exact Round 19 G-FIX source grid; check every keyed row, independently recompute 300 group summaries and distinguish exact-byte failure from post-result tiny-roundoff agreement.
scope.parameters: Fifteen constructions, ten decoder modes, lengths 240/400, seven seeds, beam width 400; 2,100 decodes; 200 gated construction-and-length groups using median recovery at least 90% and median score at least −5.5.
scope.exclusions: No LP2 ciphertext, unknown-key search, calibrated wrong-key false positives, full-length power for all ten modes or family-wide cipher exclusion.

round19-full-book-decoder-power.title: Can the decoder follow a known key through a full book?
round19-full-book-decoder-power.question: Can this decoder stay aligned with a correct key over a full book?
round19-full-book-decoder-power.finding: With the correct key, the two decoders recovered a median 99.98% and 99.82% of a 12,956-rune planted message. Wrong-key controls recovered less than 5%.
round19-full-book-decoder-power.limitations: This checks a known key on synthetic text. It does not find an LP2 key or show how often an unknown-key search gives false positives.

scope.representation: Synthetic English-derived GP29 runes using the exact pinned Self-Reliance source text and GP converter.
scope.procedure: Run the pinned Round 19 G-BOOK source stage in an isolated copy; independently compare eight non-timing rows and recount correct-key gates and wrong-key recovery.
scope.parameters: Length 12,956; one-draw keyskip suppression 0.83; modes repo_ms3 and drift_l8; three correct seeds and one wrong-key seed per mode; beam width 400.
scope.exclusions: No unknown-key LP2 scan, other skip relations, other plaintext sources, statistical false-positive calibration or family-wide cipher exclusion.

round19-rsa-key-provenance.title: Round 19 RSA key scan: source replay and provenance
round19-rsa-key-provenance.question: Did the larger RSA scan test more Cicada keys?
round19-rsa-key-provenance.finding: 594 valid public-power settings produced no source-defined PKCS#1 or PSS structure; 144 inputs were invalid. The 22 parsed PGP packets comprise two Cicada packets and 20 keys archived for unrelated reasons.
round19-rsa-key-provenance.limitations: This is a whole-payload public-power replay and key-provenance audit. It does not test RSA private-key decryption, other byte windows, or unknown keys. The 540 evaluated rows under unrelated keys are exploratory, not Cicada-key coverage.

scope.representation: Three pinned 256-byte grid readings as whole RSA values, two byte orders and source zero-extension alignments.
scope.procedure: Recompute every Round 19 C1 E-01 source row under its named moduli and exponents, test source structural predicates, and derive OpenPGP fingerprints and moduli from pinned armored witnesses.
scope.parameters: 23 named moduli (22 PGP packets plus one 2013 puzzle modulus), three payload readings, source endian/alignment options, three exponents: 738 named settings, 594 valid and 144 s>=n exclusions.
scope.exclusions: Private-key RSA operations, extra modulus witnesses, unknown keys, partial payload blocks, and alternate padding.

round20-sieve-register-gate.title: Does the sieve's pass gate require every register?
round20-sieve-register-gate.question: Can a filter pass a test when some required measurements are missing?
round20-sieve-register-gate.finding: The gate can issue a full pass even when some required text groups were never measured.
round20-sieve-register-gate.limitations: This tests the gate function with constructed summaries; the source’s actual infeasibility decision remains unchanged.

scope.representation: Constructed register-survival summaries and archived pilot summaries; no plaintext candidate.
scope.procedure: Run unchanged P1 adjudicate over every nonempty register subset plus three complete comparison summaries; reproduce all four source pilot cells and independently check coverage and threshold logic.
scope.parameters: 9 named registers; 511 nonempty subsets; included survival .95; reduction 100; low-survival comparison CY=.89; low-reduction comparison 99.
scope.exclusions: Original survival measurement replay, missing-corpus substitutions, model training, target searches and cipher-method exclusion.

rsa-window-54-source-replay.title: RSA structure in 54-byte payload windows
rsa-window-54-source-replay.question: Could the grid payload hide a 432-bit RSA block inside one short stretch?
rsa-window-54-source-replay.finding: The independent replay agrees with the source: zero strict frames across 1,218 direct readings and 2,493 modular exponentiations. One loose PSS-shaped row per payload reading, at offset 62 with exponent 17, fails the required zero-padding length. All 15 planted strict frames were recovered.
rsa-window-54-source-replay.limitations: A structural pattern is not a verified signature over a known message. This result is limited to three pinned payload readings, the published 2013 432-bit modulus, 54-byte contiguous windows, two byte orders, exponents 65537/3/17 and the source’s PKCS#1 v1.5/PSS recognizers. Other moduli, formats and noncontiguous arrangements remain outside scope.

scope.representation: Three pinned 256-byte readings of the base-60 grid payload: canon_256, canon_256_decpref and payload_resolved.
scope.procedure: For starts 0–202, take 54 bytes in both directions; inspect each directly, then for exponents 65537, 3 and 17 inspect pow(value,e,2013 modulus) only when value is below the modulus. Apply the source’s strict/loose PKCS#1 v1.5 and PSS structural tiers.
scope.parameters: 3 payload readings × 203 windows × 2 directions = 1,218 direct inspections; 2,493 modular exponentiations after 1,161 s≥n exclusions. Ten planted type-1 and five planted PSS signatures; 200 random-buffer controls.
scope.exclusions: Other moduli or exponents, noncontiguous windows, bit shifts, 54-byte windows built from different grid routes, signatures without these PKCS#1/PSS frame shapes, and verification against a known signed message.

rune-direct-byte-packing.title: LP2 runes packed directly as bytes
rune-direct-byte-packing.question: If we turn the runes into bytes without changing their order, do we get text or the start of a file?
rune-direct-byte-packing.finding: No stream is completely printable or begins with any of the six specified file signatures. Prime-byte streams are syntactically UTF-8 only because all GP prime values are one-byte ASCII codes; control characters make them nonprintable.
rune-direct-byte-packing.limitations: The source suggestion did not fix an encoding, so this is a declared direct baseline, not a replay of a reported output. Absence of six file prefixes or whole-stream printable text does not exclude other representations, transformations, or meaningful fragments.

scope.representation: Each rune becomes a zero-based GP index or its GP prime value; punctuation is omitted. Nonempty pages are screened separately and as one joined LP2-00–55 stream.
scope.procedure: Encode each target as high-bit-first five-bit index tokens, reversed-bit five-bit tokens, or single-byte GP primes. Append zero bits only at the end of each five-bit target. Screen whole-stream printable ASCII and strict UTF-8, and six exact file prefixes at byte offset zero.
scope.parameters: 55 nonempty pages plus one joined stream; three encodings; 168 streams. PNG, gzip, ZIP, PDF, ELF and MZ prefixes; no extra transformation.
scope.exclusions: Word sums, other widths or byte orders, alternate rune ordering, transformed or compressed data, headers beyond offset zero and execution of generated bytes.

rune-direct-compression.title: Complete compression decodes of directly packed LP2 runes
rune-direct-compression.question: Could directly packed LP2 runes be compressed data?
rune-direct-compression.finding: All 840 format/stream attempts were invalid: zero complete decompressions among 168 fixed rune-to-byte streams under five formats. No attempt hit the 1 MiB output cap. Known compressed, truncated, trailing-junk and over-limit controls passed for every format; a synthetic rune-packed zlib stream also decoded correctly.
rune-direct-compression.limitations: Only the three fixed rune-to-byte modes and byte-zero complete streams were tested. Compression after an unknown transform, offsets, reordered pages, altered packing, dictionary-assisted decoding, other formats and disputed transcription choices remain outside scope. Invalid decompression does not identify the manuscript's cipher.

scope.representation: The 168 exact source-record byte streams: 55 nonempty LP2-00–55 pages and one joined stream, each under index-5-msb, index-5-lsb and prime-byte encoding.
scope.procedure: Verify every reconstructed input SHA-256 against the earlier saved record; run complete-stream zlib, gzip, raw DEFLATE, bzip2 and XZ decoders at offset zero; require EOF, no unused input and output no larger than 1 MiB; independently rebuild bytes from page JSON.
scope.parameters: 168 input streams × five formats = 840 attempts; output cap 1,048,576 bytes; no offsets. Synthetic valid, truncated, trailing-junk and over-limit controls for all five formats, plus one rune-packed zlib fixture.
scope.exclusions: No prefixes, shifted starts, alternate bit widths, token ordering, recursive layers, dictionary search, other formats, unlimited expansion or language scoring.

rune-matched-scorer-calibration.title: Does a rune-matched scorer improve candidate screening?
rune-matched-scorer-calibration.question: Would scoring rune output differently help recognize a real LP reading?
rune-matched-scorer-calibration.finding: The source's five solved-page scores, 200 seed-42 random-key decodes, model size and gates reproduce exactly. The weakest known reading rises from -4.9789 to -4.7744, separation from 28.69 to 29.71 sigma; wrong-key SD rises from 0.0880 to 0.0895, failing the predeclared tightening gate. An independent model reconstruction shows the new quadgram table is exactly the original count table after K/Q->C, V->U and Z->S alias collapse.
rune-matched-scorer-calibration.limitations: This is English-scorer calibration, not an unsolved-page cipher test. The 200 wrong keys are one seeded sample on A Koan; the small sampled SD change does not prove a generally noisier model. The source's claimed multi-character rune expansion is not implemented in this particular model construction. A narrative note in the original JSON says +2.9% despite its tabulated values yielding +3.6%.

scope.representation: Five source-decoded LP1 solved sections (A Warning, Some Wisdom, A Koan, Welcome, Circumference), and A Koan's 742-rune ciphertext parsed from the pinned markdown.
scope.procedure: Replay the source's old and transformed quadgram scorers on identical known texts; score 200 modulo-29 random-key A Koan decodes with Python Random(42); compare the -5.5 known-reading gate, wrong-key SD and sigma separation. Independently rebuild the count tables and scores.
scope.parameters: Five solved pages, 200 random-key decodes, 742 ciphertext runes, seed 42, old vs transformed English quadgram models, -5.5 known-reading gate.
scope.exclusions: Unsolved LP2 ciphertext, other languages, independent held-out scorer training, complete key searches, alternative null samples, or a genuinely rune-unit-aware model.

rune-reading-sensitivity-t3.title: How disputed rune readings change the measurements
rune-reading-sensitivity-t3.question: How much could disputed rune readings change what we measure?
rune-reading-sensitivity-t3.finding: Changing all 450 proposed rune readings adds 17 adjacent repeats and shifts the frequency statistic. These are hypothetical alternatives, not 450 confirmed errors. In a separate full-length known-key fixture, 450 random changes reduce median recovery to 86%.
rune-reading-sensitivity-t3.limitations: The reader was trained using canonical labels from the control pages too, so its agreement does not independently establish accuracy. The decoder controls cover one model and simulated errors. The short and full-length fixtures also use different plaintext texts.

scope.representation: Pinned source LP2 pages 0–54 joined as 12,956 GP rune indices. The 450 O/A/AE alternatives are source-reader locations. Separate LP1 planted passages of 120 and 400 runes provide decoder controls. A separate 12,956-rune planted KJV passage is the full-book decoder control.
scope.procedure: Rerun source baseline and 400-trial random, dense and targeted substitution grids; apply all 450 exact alternative readings; rerun source 14-level LP1 decoder grids at 120 and 400 runes; compare numeric source outputs and independently recount repeats and IoC from the pinned stream. Replay the exact source six-level KJV full-book fixture using a recovered hash-matched input; compare every fresh result field with the pinned source output except elapsed seconds.
scope.parameters: 450 unique mapped source alternatives; 400 trials per sampled perturbation level; source fixed seeds/levels; 120×14 L120 and 60×14 L400 LP1 decoder cells; F0 parity gate; source German-corpus comparison floor 0.972% corresponds to 126 repeats. Six KJV full-book error levels [0,50,100,200,450,900] with six replicates each; optional 1–4 level-isolated replay workers.
scope.exclusions: No independent hardcopy image review, strict held-out glyph training, regenerated historical dependency graph, alternative cipher model, or actual LP2 plaintext/key recovery.

search-maximum-controls.title: How does trying more keys change the best score?
search-maximum-controls.question: How do complete-search maxima change under fixed nested key budgets, with the true key absent or included?
search-maximum-controls.finding: Null maxima increase with nested search budgets, but no null or key-absent positive search crosses -5.5 in this grid. Appending the true key yields exact recovery and acceptance in all positive controls.
