search-maximum-controls.limitations: Fixed dependent controls and a chosen null generator; zero exceedances are not a universal false-positive guarantee. Included-key searches have one additional candidate. Human review pending.

scope.representation: First min(240, available) known-reading output rune indices from nine traces; null indices and additive positive ciphertexts; canonical labels for scoring.
scope.procedure: Run complete nested derived-key dictionaries on 32 null/positive pairs per section; retain every candidate score and maximum; separately append the known true key to positive searches.
scope.parameters: Seeds 0..255; budgets 1,4,16,64,256; nine sections and 32 replicates; 147456 wrong-key scores and 288 true-key controls; fixed normalized English quadgram threshold -5.5.
scope.exclusions: No unknown-page test, adaptive search, beam decoder, offsets, alternate signs, language identification or population false-positive estimate.

section-1433-pairing.title: The three 1,433-rune section streams
section-1433-pairing.question: Do three reported 1,433-rune streams produce a distinctive printed-order pairwise arithmetic output?
section-1433-pairing.finding: The printed-order best is reverse-subtraction for Koan 2 + Spirals against Cuneiform, IoC 0.03481289. 465 of 999 selected-shift controls tie or exceed the observed score; their median best score is 0.034799.
section-1433-pairing.limitations: The comparison is conditional on the already-chosen sections, F rules, operations and score.

scope.representation: Koan 2 plus Spirals without F, Cuneiform without F, and Wing and Tree retaining F; explicit & section boundaries.
scope.procedure: Rebuild three 1,433-rune streams; test each pair under add/subtract modulo 29, forward/reverse second stream; choose highest whole-output IoC; repeat full 12-way selection for 999 seeded independent nonzero circular-shift trials.
scope.parameters: Three pairings, four operations each, 1,433 positions, seed 14333301, 999 control trials; ties count as at least observed.
scope.exclusions: Other section combinations, F choices, routes, key offsets, language scores and discovery-wide selection adjustment.

section-1814-pairing.title: The 1,814-rune section pairing
section-1814-pairing.question: Does four-way pairwise arithmetic give an unusual printed alignment for the two reported 1,814-rune streams?
section-1814-pairing.finding: The printed reverse-add output scores 114,642 ordered equal-rune pairs (IoC 0.034859), above the shifted median best-of-four score of 113,934; 107 of 1,813 nonzero shifts tie or exceed it.
section-1814-pairing.limitations: The conditional shift control fixes the published equality and tests only four operations and whole-stream IoC. It does not adjust for the search that noticed the equality or establish readable plaintext.

scope.representation: A is Koan 1, Loss of Divinity and Koan 2 in printed rune order. B is Sign Post and Spirals in printed rune order. Every F is omitted from both complete-page streams.
scope.procedure: Pair the two 1,814-rune streams in printed order. Apply B+A or B-A modulo 29, with B forward or reversed. Score the complete output by whole-stream IoC and select the best. Repeat this choice for all nonzero circular shifts of B.
scope.parameters: Four operations; zero-based GP indices; 1,814 positions; 1,813 exhaustive nonzero circular-shift controls; ties count as meeting the observed best score.
scope.exclusions: Other section combinations, F-removal rules, operations, offsets across unequal streams, n-gram/language scores and discovery-wide selection adjustment.

section-1894-pairing.title: The 1,894-rune section pairing
section-1894-pairing.question: Do four fixed pairwise arithmetic operations yield an unusual alignment for the two reported 1,894-rune streams?
section-1894-pairing.finding: The best printed-order output scores 123,870 ordered equal-rune pairs (IoC 0.034549), below the median best-of-four shifted score of 124,096. 1,410 of 1,893 nonzero shifted controls tie or exceed it.
section-1894-pairing.limitations: This conditional control fixes the reported sections and tests one small operation set and whole-stream IoC; it cannot assess all possible cipher combinations or correct for finding the equality after a broad search.

scope.representation: A is the Koan 1, Loss of Divinity, Koan 2 and Instruction rune sequence with every F removed. B is Mobius after its nine-rune heading, retaining F. Explicit ampersand section boundaries are respected.
scope.procedure: Pair the two 1,894-rune streams in printed order. Apply B+A or B-A modulo 29, with B forward or reversed. Score the complete output by whole-stream IoC and select the best. Repeat this choice for all nonzero circular shifts of B.
scope.parameters: Four operations; zero-based GP indices; 1,894 positions; 1,893 exhaustive nonzero circular-shift controls; ties count as meeting the observed best score.
scope.exclusions: Other section combinations, F-removal rules, operations, offsets across unequal streams, n-gram/language scores and discovery-wide selection adjustment.

sectionwise-rune-profile.title: LP2 sections: rune collisions and adjacent repeats
sectionwise-rune-profile.question: Do the last two pages look statistically different from the preceding section?
sectionwise-rune-profile.finding: LP2-54–55 has IoC 0.033821 and 3/306 doublets. Both lie inside the middle 95% of 2,701 overlapping 308-rune windows in LP2-40–53.
sectionwise-rune-profile.limitations: Only two summary measures and one proposed section split were checked.

scope.representation: All archived LP2-00–55 text, filtered to the 29 GP runes; headings included, page 50 has no runes.
scope.procedure: Profile nine artwork-section groups; compare LP2-54–55 to all same-length rune windows of LP2-40–53.
scope.parameters: Whole-section rune IoC and within-page adjacent equal-rune rate; 308-rune overlapping reference windows.
scope.exclusions: Alternative transcriptions, ciphertext transformations, other statistical features, decryption, and formal cipher-model tests.

seed-crib-controls.title: Does matching the opening text identify a seed?
seed-crib-controls.question: Which seeds survive exact plaintext prefixes, and do they predict withheld text under included-seed, omitted-seed, wrong-generator and incorrect-crib controls?
seed-crib-controls.finding: Matching two opening runes does not identify a seed: every control retains multiple candidates. Only the true generating pairs recover the complete withheld text. At four or more tested crib runes, included-pair searches retain only their true seed; other controls retain none.
seed-crib-controls.limitations: One known passage and dependent deterministic fixtures; exact crib and alignment are supplied. Results apply only to two specified generators and dictionaries. Human review pending.

scope.representation: All 95 known output rune indices from LP2-57, encrypted into six new synthetic additive ciphertexts.
scope.procedure: Search each generator dictionary for exact crib compatibility; retain all survivors and independently compare the full decoded passage and withheld suffix. Never select using withheld text.
scope.parameters: SHA-256/SHA-512; fixed ASCII domain and unsigned four-byte big-endian seed/counter; reject bytes >=232 then reduce mod 29; searched seeds 0..4095; planted seeds 17,4095,4096; cribs 2,4,8,16,32; correct or first-rune-plus-one crib; 120 cells.
scope.exclusions: No unsolved-page decoding, unknown-position search, language score, adaptive dictionary expansion, generator identification or population recovery probability.

selected-phrase-word-sums.title: Selected phrase and MYRMELEONTIDAE: five word-sum candidates
selected-phrase-word-sums.question: Do the selected PROVE WORTHIER FIND TRUTHS and MYRMELEONTIDAE candidates admit their proposed sums under the baseline rules?
selected-phrase-word-sums.finding: Five selected targets match; ten complete segmentations retained. The 809 candidate requires mixed treatment of EO and AE, so its sum is not fixed by the Latin spelling.
selected-phrase-word-sums.limitations: Selected candidate list; no unbiased match-rate estimate, dictionary search or manuscript decryption. Computational review; human review pending.

scope.representation: Five supplied Latin words, uppercase with V replaced by U; exact GP Latin-label segmentations.
scope.procedure: Enumerate all segmentations, sum prime values, and compare each with its supplied target.
scope.parameters: Fixed five candidates; ten complete segmentations; no dictionary expansion.
scope.exclusions: Other words, synonyms, alternate spellings, altered rune values, key searches, manuscript decryption and statistical significance.

semantic-seed-screen-gate-audit.title: Semantic-seed sweep: an unreachable screen gate
semantic-seed-screen-gate-audit.question: Did this seed search actually let promising answers through to its final check?
semantic-seed-screen-gate-audit.finding: A planted key recovered all 120 screening runes and was still discarded at −4.35. The 4,274 source rows and best score −6.5781 reproduce, but zero escalations follow mechanically from the unreachable +5 gate; this is not a negative cipher result.
semantic-seed-screen-gate-audit.limitations: The original nine-register model and three exact training corpora are absent from the pinned source. Its full hitfn20 gate and source-reported planted control were not independently replayed. The bundled control.json is a source artifact, not our validation of the complete pipeline.

scope.representation: Pinned Dukotah/LP2 flattened 12,956-rune transcription, first 120 runes screened, 240-rune full-hit path never reached. Source labels 0–54 skip blank Liberpedia LP2-50 and include LP2-55.
scope.procedure: Regenerate the 323 source seeds; run the exact 4,274 source screens; inspect the promotion condition and score domain; pass a source-generated planted perfect-recovery key through that same screen.
scope.parameters: 292 integer seeds through seven generators and 31 phrase seeds through three generators, each with exact and pair decoders at offset zero; beam width 64; source promotion bar +5.
scope.exclusions: No corrected-threshold sweep, full language-panel adjudication, original model rebuild, other seeds/generators/offsets, or inference that a derived-key family is ruled out.

short-text-prefix-extension.title: Word-length prefixes in previously omitted short texts
short-text-prefix-extension.question: Do shorter archived texts match either word-length prefix?
short-text-prefix-extension.finding: Neither shorter prefix matched completely. The best alignments agreed at 87 of 400 and 37 of 120 word-length positions, below the earlier scan’s maxima.
short-text-prefix-extension.limitations: Matching word lengths does not recover words. Only two fixed prefixes and the previously omitted texts from the same 94-file corpus were tested; this is not the historical 224-text scan.

scope.representation: Same pinned 94-file corpus and source manuscript parser as the baseline: first 55 percent-separated segments, 2,928 words, with greedy rune encoding and directional F-count intervals. Raw files, normalized arrays, ordering and hashes unchanged; corpus inputs external.
scope.procedure: Construct exact original prefix patterns after consuming all four full-length RNG permutations. Run unchanged scanner.scan_corpus separately for the three 400-word patterns on 8 newly eligible texts and the three 120-word patterns on 10, retaining default blocks/FFT and raw strict-maximum/tie selection. Independently integer-count every target alignment.
scope.parameters: Seed 3301 and original RNG order. First 400/120 real interval patterns plus two fixed shuffles each; 5,378 starts per 400-word pattern and 8,037 per 120-word pattern, 40,245 total scores. Newly eligible means prefix width <= words < 2,928. No repeated 84-text scan. 37 synthetic controls; 1,371 checked synthetic alignments.
scope.exclusions: No new corpus texts, historical 224-text replay, full 2,928-pattern rerun, alternative manuscript windows, changed parser/editions, word/content recovery, language exclusion or calibrated global probability. Corpus texts and normalized corpus arrays are not bundled.

short-window-lag13.title: Short-window repeated rune patterns at lag 13
short-window-lag13.question: Are the reported short lag-13 repeats unusual?
short-window-lag13.finding: Seventeen exact lag-13 two-rune windows occur among 12,186 eligible spans. The exact page-shuffle expectation is 14.12 and 111 of 499 shuffles produce at least 17. The best-of-27 lag ratio is also inside the shuffle comparison (30 of 499 at least as high).
short-window-lag13.limitations: This is a narrow new test of one interpretation, not a replay of the reported attempt.

scope.representation: Archived LP2-00–55 rune-bearing page texts; 29 GP runes, headings included, no across-page windows.
scope.procedure: Count exact matching two-rune blocks separated by 13 rune positions in every 15-rune window. Repeat on 499 within-page rune shuffles and scan lags 2–28 for selection sensitivity.
scope.parameters: Fixed lag 13, two exact equalities, window length 15; 499 page-preserving shuffles; max observed/expected ratio across lags 2–28.
scope.exclusions: The source's unspecified original windows and broader pattern rule, other motifs, word boundaries, marker resets, F skips, collision skips and cipher decryption.

single-rune-null-doublets.title: Deleting one fixed rune type: adjacent-pair census
single-rune-null-doublets.question: Does deleting every occurrence of any one of the 29 rune types reduce LP2's within-page adjacent equal-rune count?
single-rune-null-doublets.finding: No complete one-rune-type deletion reduces the 86 original adjacent equal-rune pairs. The resulting counts range from 92 to 109; the exact bridge identity explains each change. Fixed-count shuffle expectations for the retained streams range from 437.08 to 440.80 pairs.
single-rune-null-doublets.limitations: This finite result only addresses raw within-page doublet counts after one globally deleted rune type. The shuffle expectation is descriptive and does not model a plaintext language. Deletion before another transform may change key alignment and is outside scope.

scope.representation: Archived LP2-00–55 UTF-8 text and the site 29-rune alphabet; headings included; non-runes removed before within-page adjacent-pair counts.
scope.procedure: For each rune type separately, delete every occurrence while preserving surviving order and page boundaries; recount equal adjacent rune pairs, destroyed pairs, newly bridged pairs, surviving edges and fixed-count shuffle expectation.
scope.parameters: Exactly 29 fixed global deletion rules. No individual position selection, no threshold optimization, no plaintext scoring, no key or subsequent decoder.
scope.exclusions: Multi-type or position-specific deletion; word-boundary-dependent counting; changed cipher alignment after deletion; alternative transcriptions; LP2-56–57; a claim of general null impossibility.

solved-reading-running-key.title: Solved manuscript readings as a running key
solved-reading-running-key.question: Could the solved pages be a key for the unsolved pages?
solved-reading-running-key.finding: The highest-scoring output was not coherent English. LP2-49’s 66 runes nevertheless scored above all 16 shuffled-key search maxima.
solved-reading-running-key.limitations: The search used one fixed 2,892-rune key order on 55 pages, trying every fitting whole-page offset and both arithmetic directions. It did not test wrapping, skips, partial pages or other languages.

scope.representation: 2,892 canonical GP29 rune indices from eight established readings in manuscript order; 55 nonempty LP2-00–55 ciphertext pages.
scope.procedure: At every fitting contiguous source offset, add or subtract one key index per rune modulo 29 and score the entire page with the pinned English quadgram model. Compare the global best to 16 whole-key shuffled full-grid maxima. A separate post-observation diagnostic searches four disjoint 2,892-GP-rune windows of preserved Emerson English.
scope.parameters: 55 complete pages; 292,318 observed page/offset/sign alignments, 16 complete shuffled-key grids (seeds 33017100–33017115), both arithmetic signs, four post-observation English GP-key windows.
scope.exclusions: Other source orders, substrings of pages, wrapping, key skips, word resets, alternate languages or score models, source text variants and any claim of general running-key exclusion.

solved-text-selection-source-gate.title: Solved-text selections: what the source controls prove
solved-text-selection-source-gate.question: Have people tried finding a message hidden in the already-decoded pages?
solved-text-selection-source-gate.finding: The four planted examples clear their own length thresholds and all miss the final bars. The source therefore established that it can extract and score these planted reads, but not its claimed power to detect them at the threshold used for the manuscript. Its zero-hit result is a bounded report, not a control-validated exclusion.
solved-text-selection-source-gate.limitations: This checks the source's saved rows and the decision rule against the independently replayed output from 2026-10-22; the 1,000-shuffle nulls were not rerun for this packaging step. Its decoded source sections cover ten LP1 images, with line geometry that differs from Liberpedia's current reading exports. No LP2 unsolved text was tested.

scope.representation: Five decoded source sections spanning ten LP1 images. Source section order is 01, 05, 06–09, 03–04, 14–15; the concatenation is not manuscript order.
scope.procedure: Replay and audit the pinned R22-A every-k/diagonal selections and R23-A2 first/last printed-line/word reads. Compare planted-control scores with both the length-specific bars they were tested against and the final family bars actually applied to manuscript reads.
scope.parameters: R22-A: 1,754 selection functions for each of letter and rune streams (3,508); R23-A2: four read types × six scopes × two directions (48). Both use seed 3301 and 1,000 source null shuffles per distinct length.
scope.exclusions: No new LP1 image-checked transcription, no new whole-search null or end-to-end power estimate, no LP2 ciphertext search, and no claim that all acrostic or selection methods have been excluded.

source-independent-key-floor-audit.title: Does the doublet floor rule out every independent key?
source-independent-key-floor-audit.question: Do the missing repeats prove that an independent key cannot work?
source-independent-key-floor-audit.finding: The pinned rune stream has 86 equal pairs in 12,901 within-page adjacencies; no cross-page join creates a pair. D2's planted-English scoring control passes. Its broad independent-key exclusion is not established by that replay: the four corpus inputs are unavailable, the B4 preregistration called for five large corpora, and an exact finite independent-key example produces below-floor outcomes with positive probability.
source-independent-key-floor-audit.limitations: The toy example tests the logic of the claimed hard floor; it does not assign an LP2 probability. Existing exact evidence strongly disagrees with an iid uniform additive key. The reported English corpus values cannot be independently recomputed without their original text bytes or a specified replacement corpus protocol.

scope.representation: Pinned 29-rune source transcription of the 55 nonempty LP2 pages before AN END and PARABLE; 12,956 runes. A separate Unicode-rune parser checks the count without using source gematria code.
scope.procedure: Run the D2 source's planted-English control and recount; compare an independent parser; inspect B4 G3 source prerequisites and saved values; enumerate all independent uniform keys in a three-symbol logical control.
scope.parameters: D2's LP2 stream, per-page adjacency, 54 page joins, the B4 predeclared five-large-corpus rule, the implemented four-corpus loop, and all 3^4 keys of the finite control.
scope.exclusions: No new LP2 key or plaintext search. No re-estimation of the English floor without the absent source corpora. No claim that the finite control makes iid uniform keys likely on LP2.

spiral-branches-paired-subtraction.title: LP2: pair the 2,883-rune sections by subtraction
spiral-branches-paired-subtraction.question: Do five fixed pairwise-subtraction variants of the two 2,883-rune streams produce unusually high whole-stream IoC after selection among the variants?
spiral-branches-paired-subtraction.finding: Reverse-tail produces 287,504 ordered equal-symbol pairs out of 8,308,806, IoC 0.034602. The other four scores are lower. Complete-search control fractions are 922/2,883 ≈ 0.320 for circular shifts and 342/1,000 = 0.342 for within-page shuffles. No unusual IoC peak under either conditional comparison.
spiral-branches-paired-subtraction.limitations: A new bounded computation of suggested variants, not a claimed original source output. The source transcript has no full scored sweep and is identified by hash, not redistributed. The two controls condition on fixed streams and variants; they do not adjust for all prior exploration of equal section lengths or all possible operations. A whole-stream IoC alone cannot identify language or plaintext. Human review pending.

scope.representation: Archived 29-rune indices; A = LP2-03–07 + LP2-08–14 + first nine runes of LP2-15; B = LP2-40–53 with every F removed. Headings retained, punctuation excluded. Posted A streams match archive exactly by SHA-256.
scope.procedure: For each aligned position output (B_i − A_i) mod 29. Search direct, reverse Branches, reverse full 1,738-rune tail, Atbash Branches, and Atbash full tail. Score each complete output by whole-stream ordered equal-symbol pairs / N(N−1), N=2,883. Compare the selected maximum to every nonzero circular shift of B and 999 within-page non-F shuffles of B; repeat all five variants per control.
scope.parameters: Five predeclared variants; 2,883 positions; 2,882 exhaustive shifts; 999 shuffles with random.Random seed 33012883. Include ties. Shift comparison (tail+1)/2883; shuffle estimate (tail+1)/1000. Threshold 0.05, considered separately for both controls.
scope.exclusions: N-gram scoring; periodic IoC; additions, multiplication or XOR; arbitrary offsets; alternative page ranges; page-heading removal; other interruption conventions; full historical discovery-search correction; plaintext claims.

study-here-bidirectional-pointer.title: LP1: the 331 / 133 STUDY HERE pointer
study-here-bidirectional-pointer.question: Does the forward-331/reverse-133 pointer uniquely select STUDY HERE and reproduce both reported prime block sums?
study-here-bidirectional-pointer.finding: The archived text has STUDY HERE at five adjacent pairs; the selected 331/133 pair gives first/last GP sums 72,065/26,893. Only the latter matches the reported 71,963/26,893. Thirteen of 463 cuts yield two prime sums, but this selected cut does not.
study-here-bidirectional-pointer.limitations: The original poster’s exact input list was not supplied. A 102-point discrepancy may reflect different transcription or accounting. Phrase and positions were selected after the solved reading was known; cut counts are descriptive.

scope.representation: Four solved LP1 sections concatenated into the pinned 464-word order; original ciphertext rune values and published literal readings.
scope.procedure: Confirm forward and reverse indices, recalculate GP block sums, enumerate all adjacent STUDY HERE pairs and all 463 possible word cuts.
scope.parameters: One-based word positions; split after forward word 331; GP prime values from the archived alphabet; no resegmentation.
scope.exclusions: The reporter’s unavailable private 464-word list, alternate page sets, changed punctuation rules, probability under a prespecified search or any LP2 decoding rule.

target-sized-languages.title: Language controls with exactly 2,896 tokens per sample
target-sized-languages.question: Do fixed language profiles distinguish samples the same token size as the unsolved manuscript?
target-sized-languages.finding: All 59 complete samples per representation have their own language as unique nearest profile. English is nearest to the manuscript, but all 24 manuscript-to-profile distances exceed the corresponding observed control maxima.
target-sized-languages.limitations: Descriptive sample ranges, not rejection thresholds or language probabilities. Shared benchmark, different genre and uncertain rune-to-letter units; disjoint blocks may share articles. Human review pending.

scope.representation: Existing 2896-token rune target and three inherited common corpus representations: letters, folded letters and GP grouping; documented dotted-I boundary amendment.
scope.procedure: Partition each evaluation token stream into complete disjoint blocks of 2896; compare all blocks and manuscript with eight full development profiles using exact rational length TV; retain ties, margins, endpoints and remainders.
scope.parameters: Eight fixed languages; 59 complete blocks per representation, three representations, bins 1..15 and16+; no resampling, fitting or score-based selection.
scope.exclusions: No genre matching, posterior, all-language coverage, equal translated passage boundaries, independent-trial accuracy or cipher identification.

totient-map-route.title: LP2-00–02: 27 × 27 totient-map route replay
totient-map-route.question: Do the selected three-rune-node readings and transition rules reproduce, and what selections remain unresolved?
totient-map-route.finding: The proposed passage can be reproduced when its chosen map cells and keys are supplied. All 65 supplied rune calculations and 16 transitions match the stated rules.
totient-map-route.limitations: The rules do not yet choose a unique path through the map or predict an unseen continuation. Reproducing the selected words does not confirm the intended plaintext.

scope.representation: 729 archived runes including headings, page-order row-major 27x27, punctuation removed; one-based cells; indices 0–28.
scope.procedure: Replay supplied nodes and ciphertext; independently check arithmetic; recompute three transition rules; compare three documented SOON centers; census mirrors and 99 frequency-preserving shuffled controls.
scope.parameters: Pinned commit d5eed3f10428372c7202ceebc65cc3bdead0819d; 17 primary blocks plus alternative SOON; 16 primary transitions; phase thresholds 7,14; four mirror axes/radii 1..13; seed3301; ordered signature keys indices1..28.
scope.exclusions: Automatic route discovery; original image transcription review; significance of numerical/thematic coincidences; new THE continuation after THEN; complete rule-space enumeration; probability of intended English; all possible totient/geometric methods.

transcription-correction-sensitivity.title: Stored transcription corrections: LP2 word lengths and IoC
transcription-correction-sensitivity.question: Do the seven published LP2 reviewed-text corrections change the joined-page rune-token sequence, word-length distribution, or whole-stream IoC under the site's published counting rule?
transcription-correction-sensitivity.finding: None of the seven current LP2 reviewed-text corrections changes the ordered rune stream, normalized rune-token sequence, 2,896-token length distribution, or whole-stream IoC pair counts. LP1-10's separate adjacent-rune swap changes six ordered-bigram type counts but preserves its rune multiset and word-length sequence.
transcription-correction-sensitivity.limitations: This measures only the eight stored reviewed layers and one declared tokenizer. The correction evidence is taken from page records, not a new independent image reading. Punctuation-sensitive ciphers and unrecorded ambiguities remain open. The exact LP2 null effect does not imply punctuation never matters.

scope.representation: Archived raw and separate reviewed_text fields in the eight current page records; joined LP2-00–55 corpus with the seven LP2 reviewed layers substituted and all other pages archived.
scope.procedure: Check ordered rune equality, rune multiset and whole-stream IoC pair counts. Remove slash/CR/LF wraps; tokenize rune runs with optional internal apostrophes, retaining headings and joining pages. Compare ordered normalized rune tokens, word-length histograms and ordered bigrams. Independently reconstruct edit strings and scan tokens.
scope.parameters: 29-symbol stored alphabet; eight reviewed pages; LP2-00–55 in order; no search, random trial or significance threshold. Each of 57 source files and the plan is SHA-256 pinned.
scope.exclusions: Unrecorded disputed marks; new photographic review; alternative word delimiters; punctuation-driven cipher resets; page-local tokenization; LP2-56–57; any claim that the entire transcription is correct.

turtle-shape-refinement-replay.title: The six refined turtle-shape checks
turtle-shape-refinement-replay.question: Do rune-driven drawings stand out from shuffled text?
turtle-shape-refinement-replay.finding: None of the six refined checks passes the source’s two-part threshold. Some measurements stand out among shuffled paths, but no symbol or reading is established.
turtle-shape-refinement-replay.limitations: These are six previously selected checks. Part of the source threshold relies on a distribution assumption that was not validated. Other drawing rules remain open.

scope.representation: The 55 nonempty source transcription segments equal Liberpedia LP2-00–49 plus LP2-51–55, including F (index zero); source stream SHA-256 79b14e630946b64cdca838f328e73904f506df576d15e21fcb46271d4b4c8040.
scope.procedure: Replay exactly the six source-selected 2,000-shuffle refinements using frozen pure source functions. Share identical surrogate walks across diagnostics of the same rule; independently recount tails and compare coordinates, rasters and selected measures with a separate implementation. Repeat the source square and block-comb controls.
scope.parameters: Six selected diagnostics across four distinct rules: value/M6/absolute/unit symmetry; value/M8/relative/value fill, symmetry and components; value/M12/absolute/unit fill; prime-index/M6/relative/unit fill. Seeds 103301..105300, 2,000 shuffles per rule = 8,000 null walks; two plants with 200 shuffles each.
scope.exclusions: No new 72-rule screening pass, new drawing rule, per-page reset, pen-up marker, 3D route, glyph recognition or plaintext extraction. No independently validated Gaussian-tail or familywise-probability claim. The other rules remain covered only by the earlier 200-shuffle baseline.

two-rune-feedback-family.title: Two-rune feedback with every starting pair
two-rune-feedback-family.question: Can any starting pair make these two-rune feedback rules yield a strong English score?
two-rune-feedback-family.finding: No starting pair passed the fixed score checks. Thirty-five of 49 shuffled searches scored at least as highly; some controls ranked a wrong output above the known text.
two-rune-feedback-family.limitations: One fixed two-rune feedback family and English scorer. The controls reuse only two passages; this is score screening, not a validated rejection of autokey ciphers.

scope.representation: The same pinned 12,956 GP29 rune indices on 55 nonempty LP2-00–55 pages, excluding empty LP2-50. Page-local input; drop first two decoded runes before source GP Latin expansion and normalized English quadgram scoring.
scope.procedure: Enumerate all 841 ordered two-rune key starts for every fixed k2 source function, plaintext/mixed history, both signs and forward/reversed inputs. Compute 48 proved effective branches and retain all 56 source labels by exact signed-function/starting-key permutation. Repeat the same whole-family selection on 49 shared within-page-shuffled corpora. Retain failed known-text identification diagnostics; interpret as fixed score-screening enumeration only.
scope.parameters: 7 functions × 2 histories × 2 signs × 2 directions × 55 pages × 841 starts = 2,590,280 labelled cases, 2,220,240 effective cases. Uniform recomputation; prior union overlaps 133,980 labelled/121,220 effective cases, leaving 2,456,300 labelled/2,099,020 effective additional settings. Whole-family null seeds 3301241024–3301241072, same page shuffle order as the prior corner. Candidate gate >= max(−5.5, largest of 49 whole-family null maxima + 0.5). Original stable label/page/starting-key order; exact scores.
scope.exclusions: Other history lengths/functions, continuous or word-reset streams, skipping, different alphabets or language scorers, plaintext identification, per-branch significance claims and control-validated cipher-family rejection. Identification controls reuse two passages, three starts and dependent branch labels: all 336 true-key outputs recover, but only 264 selected winners recover completely; 88 ties-only and 32 higher wrong alternatives remain material limits. Null full-grid independent checks are sampled; observed scores and reported null maxima are all independently checked.

two-rune-primer-extension.title: All two-rune starts for one feedback rule
two-rune-primer-extension.question: Could two unequal starting values reveal an English-like page under this feedback rule?
two-rune-primer-extension.finding: Unequal starts improved the best score slightly, but no candidate passed the fixed English-score gate. Forty of 49 shuffled searches scored at least as highly.
two-rune-primer-extension.limitations: One two-rune plaintext-feedback rule and one English scorer only. The controls reuse two known passages; this does not exclude other autokey rules or plaintext languages.

scope.representation: Zero-based GP29 indices from the same pinned source transcription: 12,956 runes in 55 nonempty LP2-00–55 pages, excluding empty LP2-50. Page-local streams only; score source Latin transliteration after omitting the first two decoded runes.
scope.procedure: For plaintext-history f_sum, k=2, sign −1, forward and page-local reset, enumerate every two-rune key primer. Decode P0=C0−s0, P1=C1−s1, Pi=Ci−P(i−1)−P(i−2) modulo 29; preserve the source English quadgram scorer. Repeat the complete page/primer search on 49 within-page-shuffled corpora; independently check all target outputs and scores and retained null maxima.
scope.parameters: 55 pages × 841 ordered primer pairs = 46,255 cases: 1,595 overlapping equal-primer cases and 44,660 new unequal-primer cases. 49 matched whole-search shuffles, random.Random seeds 3301241024–3301241072. Hit requires score >= max(−5.5, largest null maximum + 0.5). 40 top outputs, 55 per-page outputs and all 50 × 55 × 841 scores retained. Two known passages × three unequal primers give six full-search plants; exact source parity across 5,046 candidates.
scope.exclusions: Other six source functions, other history sources, k outside 2, sign +1, reversed/continuous/word-reset streams, skips, other alphabets or languages, broader autokey exclusion and plaintext identification. The six plants reuse two texts; 49 null searches do not establish a general probability.

typed-seed-random-opening-cribs.title: Typed seeds and Python Random streams at LP2 page openings
typed-seed-random-opening-cribs.question: Were words, dates and numbers tried as Python random seeds?
typed-seed-random-opening-cribs.finding: Zero of 61,632 source configuration-and-mask paths produces a complete fixed opening; the longest prefix is five runes. This is a new opening-crib check, separate from the source's LP2-00 English-score result.
typed-seed-random-opening-cribs.limitations: This assumes one of nine known-reading openings appears at one of the included page starts. It uses CPython 3.12 seed behavior, source-specified stream modes and first-two-F masks at zero key offset; it does not rule out other seeds, plaintexts or interruption rules.

scope.representation: Current GP29 transcription, first 12 decoded runes from each nonempty LP2-00–55 page, compared to nine fixed 12-rune published reading openings.
scope.procedure: Execute the pinned source's seed literals, date loop and six Python Random stream modes; apply two decode signs and each of four source-defined first-two-F removal masks; compare fixed openings with strict no-skip key alignment.
scope.parameters: 1,284 typed seed entries × six modes × two signs = 15,408 source configs; four F masks each = 61,632 paths. Key length 260, zero offset; 55 page starts and nine 12-rune cribs.
scope.exclusions: No Python 2 string seed implementation, source English scorer, reverse key stream, key-skip filter, nonzero offsets, other pages, other cribs or arbitrary new seeds.

uniform-additive-doublets.title: LP2-00–55: uniform additive keys and adjacent matches
uniform-additive-doublets.question: Does the observed number of within-page adjacent matches agree with independent uniform additive keys modulo 29?
uniform-additive-doublets.finding: The observed 86 matches among 12,901 edges strongly disagree with this uniform model: expected 12,901/29 ≈ 444.86; conditional P(D≤86) ≈ 1.0708e-98. This is not logical impossibility or a probability about language.
uniform-additive-doublets.limitations: Low count and prior claim known before replication. Conditional tail is not adjusted for prior feature selection. Archived transcription is assumed. Other key models and multiplicative running sums remain outside the result; human review pending.

scope.representation: Archived rune-only page streams; headings included; remove non-runes; count overlapping equal neighbors; never join pages.
scope.procedure: Recount all pages and evaluate the inclusive lower binomial tail using exact integer arithmetic; independently check by integer-mass recurrence and regex recount.
scope.parameters: 29-symbol alphabet; independent uniform additive keys, independent of fixed plaintext; fixed observed page lengths; lower tail includes ties; 80-digit Decimal rendering; 12 finite distribution controls.
scope.exclusions: Nonuniform or dependent keys, fixed-count shuffles, other cipher equations, altered boundaries, output filters, plaintext identification and correction for historical feature selection.

url-marker-affine-census.title: Literal web markers under every fixed affine rune map
url-marker-affine-census.question: Do fixed affine rune maps produce a literal web marker?
url-marker-affine-census.finding: One five-rune stretch on LP2-36 reads HTTPS. Its HTTP prefix is the same candidate, not a second hit. WWW and ONION have no matches under the tested maps. The short marker does not establish a web address or confirm the plaintext.
url-marker-affine-census.limitations: Only four fixed literal rune spellings and static affine maps were tested. No punctuation or hostname grammar was inferred, and no chance/significance claim is made. This reuses an already tested keyspace for a new marker readout.

scope.representation: Original archived line.raw rune order including headings; remove every nonalphabet character, including all word/line separators. Search within each page only, with no wrap or cross-page join. One rune is one position, including digraph-labelled runes.
scope.parameters: 812 maps; 56 original page files, 55 rune-bearing; 12,956 runes; fixed WWW/HTTP/HTTPS/ONION; every fitting zero-based rune start; 8-rune snippet flanks.
scope.procedure: Freeze 57 input hashes; run all 812 x 4 synthetic fixed-offset plants; decode every page under P=(aC+b)mod29 and scan all overlapping token windows; independently translate complete streams and compare every match field and source location; count original equal-rune triples.
scope.exclusions: No new keyspace, original punctuation interpretation, URL/hostname syntax, language score, chance estimate, p-value, changing substitution, alternate spelling, transposition or other layer.

wholepage-affine-gp29.title: Every static affine map on complete LP2 pages
wholepage-affine-gp29.question: Have Caesar, Atbash and the other fixed affine substitutions been checked on whole LP2 pages?
wholepage-affine-gp29.finding: Nine complete archived readings cleared the English-score gate and all nine planted affine encipherments ranked the true map first. None of 44,660 LP2 outputs reached the fixed −5.5 threshold. The highest score was −6.543, and 144 of 199 shuffled-page full-search controls had an equal or higher maximum.
wholepage-affine-gp29.limitations: The test covers one static affine map per complete page and English-like canonical GP transliteration. Pagewise rune shuffles are positional controls, not cipher models. Periodic or contextual maps, other languages and hidden layers remain open.

scope.representation: Original archived GP29 rune order including headings on each rune-bearing LP2-00–55 page. LP2-50 has no runes.
scope.procedure: Apply P=(aC+b) mod 29 for every a=1..28 and b=0..28 to each complete page. Score canonical GP Latin text with a pinned English quadgram table. Gate on nine complete archived readings and nine planted affine encipherments. For 199 null trials shuffle each page's rune order, run the whole census, and retain one global maximum.
scope.parameters: 812 maps, 55 pages, 44,660 candidate outputs; fixed English threshold −5.5; 200 shuffles per positive control and 199 complete-search null replicates.
scope.exclusions: No time-varying affine rule, general substitution, wordwise transforms, non-English score, altered transcription or hidden intermediate operation.

wholepage-known-vigenere-keys.title: Two known LP1 keys across complete LP2 pages
wholepage-known-vigenere-keys.question: Have the two known keys been checked on whole unsolved pages, not just opening words?
wholepage-known-vigenere-keys.finding: Nine 66-rune archived reading controls and nine planted-key controls passed. Across 2,310 whole-page outputs, the highest English score was −6.675 and none reached the fixed −5.5 threshold. A complete 2,310-setting search on each of 199 independently page-shuffled controls produced an equal or higher maximum 68 times.
wholepage-known-vigenere-keys.limitations: This bounds two specific repeating keys and canonical GP-to-English scoring. Pagewise rune shuffles preserve counts and lengths but are not a cipher model. Other keys, interrupted schedules, non-English text and hidden layers remain open.

scope.representation: The complete original GP29 rune sequence on each rune-bearing LP2-00–55 page, including headings; LP2-50 contains no runes.
scope.procedure: Decode every full page with the documented Welcome and second-koan keys under both signs and all phases. Score the complete canonical GP Latin transliteration with the pinned English quadgram model. Gate on nine archived 66-rune readings and nine planted encipherments. Compare the single maximum over all pages/settings with 199 full-search pagewise rune shuffles.
scope.parameters: 55 pages; two key lengths 8 and 13; 42 settings per page; 2,310 outputs; fixed −5.5 English-score threshold; 199 global-search shuffled controls.
scope.exclusions: No other keys, full-stop or word resets, skipped runes, cross-page state, other alphabet, transposition, or non-English score. No general rejection of Vigenère.

wholepage-progressive-caesar.title: Progressive Caesar shifts on complete LP2 pages
wholepage-progressive-caesar.question: Have progressive Caesar or Trithemius-style shifts been tested on whole LP2 pages?
wholepage-progressive-caesar.finding: All nine complete archived readings and all nine planted progressive-shift controls passed. None of 44,660 LP2 outputs reached the fixed −5.5 English threshold; the best scored −6.426. Seventy of 199 page-shuffled full-search controls had an equal or higher maximum.
wholepage-progressive-caesar.limitations: The test covers only Pᵢ=Cᵢ+k·i+b modulo 29, with a rune-by-rune page-local clock. Shuffles are positional controls, not a cipher model. Other schedule and alphabet rules remain open.

scope.representation: Original archived GP29 rune order including headings on each rune-bearing LP2-00–55 page. Non-runes do not advance the page-local position; LP2-50 has no runes.
scope.procedure: Apply Pᵢ=Cᵢ+k·i+b modulo 29 for every k=1..28 and b=0..28 to each complete page. Score canonical GP Latin text with a pinned English quadgram table. Gate on nine complete archived readings and nine planted schedules. For 199 null trials shuffle each page's rune order, run the whole census and retain one global maximum.
scope.parameters: 812 nonconstant schedules, 55 pages, 44,660 candidate outputs; fixed English threshold −5.5; 200 shuffles per positive control and 199 complete-search null replicates.
scope.exclusions: No k=0 static shifts, already covered in the affine census. No nonlinear clocks, word/line resets, arbitrary changing alphabets, transposition, alternate GP mapping or other language.

wholepage-public-wordlist.title: Public wordlist keys on complete LP2 pages
wholepage-public-wordlist.question: Do the public dictionary keys decode a complete LP2 page?
wholepage-public-wordlist.finding: Zero of 33,990 whole-page outputs reached the -5.5 solved-reading threshold. The best (-6.5023) was equaled or exceeded by 105 of 199 full-search shuffled controls; nine solved-text and nine planted-key controls passed.
wholepage-public-wordlist.limitations: This checks only the 43 pinned keys, page-local repeating GP29 arithmetic at all phases and both signs, canonical transliteration, and this English score. A shuffled-runic null is a control for the search maximum, not a cipher model.

scope.representation: All GP29 runes in archived order per LP2 page, including headings; non-runes ignored; LP2-50 runeless and excluded.
scope.procedure: Decode every complete rune-bearing page with all 43 pinned wordlist keys, all key phases and both additive/subtractive directions. Score canonical Latin output with pinned English quadgram model; compare the single best output with 199 full-grid within-page shuffle maxima.
scope.parameters: 43 keys; 618 key-phase-direction settings; 55 pages; 33,990 full-page scores; nine genuine and nine planted controls; 199 global-null replicates.
scope.exclusions: Other keys, non-English targets, resets at words, alphabet changes, Atbash, key layers, internal offsets, ciphertext segmentation.

wing-tree-eleven-rune-windows.title: LP2-27–32: eleven-rune sums of 563 and 569
wing-tree-eleven-rune-windows.question: Do sums 563 and 569 recur in eleven consecutive runes elsewhere in the Wing and Tree section?
wing-tree-eleven-rune-windows.finding: 563 occurs seven times across LP2-28, LP2-29, LP2-31 and LP2-32; 569 occurs ten times across LP2-27–31. Mean window sum: 784505/1373, approximately 571.38.
wing-tree-eleven-rune-windows.limitations: Targets and section were selected after the original observation. Overlapping windows share ten runes; hit counts are not independent trials or p-values. No unspecified image-only row claim is evaluated. Human review pending.

scope.representation: All alphabet runes in archived LP2-27–32 order, including headings; separators removed; each page remains a separate stream; Gematria Primus prime values.
scope.procedure: Enumerate every eleven-consecutive-rune window within each page and count sums equal to fixed targets 563 and 569; retain every window and its coordinates.
scope.parameters: Length 11; targets 563 and 569; one-rune steps; all 1373 eligible starts in six pages; no page crossing, wrapping, reversal or padding.
scope.exclusions: Grid columns and perimeters, manuscript-row selection, other lengths or targets, cross-page windows, file-dimension retesting, null-model simulations, image provenance and decryption.

word-internal-affine-all-lags.title: LP2: affine patterns across twelve distances
word-internal-affine-all-lags.question: If we try many rune distances and formulas, does the strongest pattern still stand out?
word-internal-affine-all-lags.finding: The selected relation repeats the same rune five positions later: 102 matches versus 60.6 expected. Four of 999 full 12-lag × 841-map shuffled searches equaled or exceeded its score (corrected p=0.005). The proposed lag-six formula was not the maximum.
word-internal-affine-all-lags.limitations: Other word boundaries, earlier exploratory choices, and realistic encryption models were not tested. A shuffled word is only one reference for ordinary sequence structure.

scope.representation: Archived 29-rune LP2-00–55 text; hyphens and full stops split words, while slash and newline are layout marks.
scope.procedure: For lags 1–12 and every a,b in 0–28, count c′ = ac + b modulo 29 inside visible words. Compute the exact fixed-multiset word-shuffle mean, rank by (count − mean)/sqrt(mean + 1), and retain the maximum. Repeat that complete selection on shuffled words.
scope.parameters: 12 lags × 841 affine maps = 10,092 scores; 999 independent within-word shuffles; seed 330112; at-least ties; plus-one corrected upper tail; predeclared alpha 0.05.
scope.exclusions: Other segmentations, page subsets or releases, lags beyond 12, nonlinear relations, key/decryption searches, prior unrecorded model searches, and realistic plaintext/cipher generators.

word-internal-affine-lags.title: LP2: a six-rune pattern inside words
word-internal-affine-lags.question: When two runes are six places apart inside a word, do they follow a specific rule more often than we would expect by chance?
word-internal-affine-lags.finding: A rule relating runes six places apart matches 77 of 1,267 pairs inside words; shuffling the same words gives about 45 matches. It is the strongest of 841 formulas checked at that distance.
word-internal-affine-lags.limitations: The formula and distance were chosen after examining the text. We do not yet know whether this pattern comes from the encryption.

scope.representation: Archived 29-rune LP2-00–55 text; hyphens and full stops split words, while slash and newline are layout marks.
scope.procedure: Count c′ = 24 − 2c at lag six within visible words; scan all 841 affine maps at that lag; compare with 2,000 seeded within-word shuffles.
scope.parameters: 56 unsolved pages; 1,267 word-internal opportunities; 841 affine maps c′ = ac + b modulo 29 at lag six; 2,000 shuffles.
scope.exclusions: Other page ranges or transcriptions, alternate word boundaries, other formula families, key-layer simulations, held-out prediction, and a complete decryptor.

word-reset-repetition.title: LP2-00–55: exact words and anagram repetition
word-reset-repetition.question: Do interior ciphertext tokens repeat exactly or as anagrams under two apostrophe policies?
word-reset-repetition.finding: Both boundary policies have zero exact pairs and four anagram pairs, all of length four. Shared deterministic word resets require distinct corresponding plaintext units; shared substitution plus shuffling cannot hide repeated longer words in this selection.
word-reset-repetition.limitations: Necessary model constraints, not a claim that plaintext repeats or all word ciphers fail. Page-edge tokens omitted. Same function/context for exact-repeat inference; same one-output-per-rune map for anagrams. Transcription dependent; human review pending.

scope.representation: Archived rune tokens, headings retained, slash and CR/LF transparent; apostrophe boundary and transparent policies; omit first and last nonempty token per page; select ciphertext length >=4 runes.
scope.procedure: Count exact-token and named-rune anagram collisions, preserving every selected token and source offset; independently verify with regex tokenization and alphabet-count vectors.
scope.parameters: LP2-00–55; no page joining; two apostrophe policies; all selected token pairs, including within-page pairs; anagram lengths >=4 and >=5; identical function/context or shared symbol map only for the respective logical implications.
scope.exclusions: Claims that plaintext must repeat, changing effective keys or state, different word maps, alternative boundaries, page-edge tokens, language significance tests, and a general rejection of word ciphers.

word-sum-corpus-control.title: LP1 square: dictionary candidate space for the selected phrase
word-sum-corpus-control.question: How many words in a pinned crib corpus fit the four reported GP totals and rune lengths before a meaningful phrase is selected?
word-sum-corpus-control.finding: The four fixed slots admit 38, 15, 10 and 38 corpus entries; their ordered product is 216,600, or 210,900 if the two GP-131 words must differ. Every printed corpus GP total verifies after the disclosed J-glyph mapping.
word-sum-corpus-control.limitations: This surviving GPL corpus is not established as the exact historical worddata.csv. Ordered products count many nonsentences and do not estimate chance discovery. Vocabulary and stored rune segmentation are corpus-specific; no unsolved-page decoding was tested. Human review pending.

scope.representation: Sixteen preserved CSV files from the pinned 1_grams-full directory, one word per row, original rune strings and GP totals; the source J glyph ᛂ is assigned the same 37 value as manuscript ᛄ.
scope.procedure: Hash-check all inputs, verify each row GP sum from its rune symbols, count all corpus words at totals 131, 151 and 809 and at the four fixed target lengths, then multiply ordered slot counts and draw complete-count-derived histograms.
scope.parameters: 138,466 unique rows across 16 files; targets 131/5, 151/7, 151/4, 131/5; additional 809 census; no frequency weighting; figure displays sums 80–220 while result stores all totals.
scope.exclusions: The historical worddata.csv attachment, alternative rune segmentations, semantic or grammatical scoring, dictionary expansion, a phrase-generation search, any LP2 key operation and statistical inference about author intent.

wulfic-adfgvx-fractionation.title: Does the fractionation reversal undo its own shuffle?
wulfic-adfgvx-fractionation.question: Does this grid-and-shuffle method work on LP2?
wulfic-adfgvx-fractionation.finding: The source names 1,260 settings; its own length rule skips 336, and 2 of the remaining 924 cross its vocabulary-score gate. Its raw IoC is bounded by 1, so the IoC >1.3 gate cannot fire. A separately labeled exact inverse produces 2 score-gated rows among 588 settings. Every gated setting has invalid grid cells. The correction repairs a transposition inverse; it does not identify the manuscript cipher.
wulfic-adfgvx-fractionation.limitations: Only 14 source keywords, six checked page streams, five split rules, seven natural-order column widths and two coordinate shifts. The source gate can reward a few words even when invalid cells were dropped; raw IoC is not normalized or controlled. No general fractionation or plaintext verdict.

scope.representation: Source GP29 rune order; 6×5 keyword-first table with the last cell empty. Archived source page_38/39/40/44/45/47 rune streams independently match the corresponding current LP2 pages under the source parser.
scope.procedure: Replay split, archived column reversal, direct and coordinate-shift routes exactly. Separately correct natural-order column lengths and compare 588 full-message planted round trips.
scope.parameters: 14 source keywords; six source-intended LP2 pages; split n/n−5/n+5/n//2/2n//3; widths 7,11,13,17,19,23,29; sub/add coordinate shifts.
scope.exclusions: Other widths, keys, keyed column orders, coordinate-stream encodings, alternate null handling, source bonus running-key methods and any decryption claim.

wulfic-advanced-running-keys.title: Four archived texts as running keys
wulfic-advanced-running-keys.question: Could Liber AL, solved text, Emerson or Deor be the key to these pages?
wulfic-advanced-running-keys.finding: This program found no established reading using its four proposed key texts. Its best manuscript score was matched or beaten by 41 of 49 shuffled searches. More importantly, it missed the same known message for all four texts when that message began between its sampled offsets.
wulfic-advanced-running-keys.limitations: The search samples every hundredth text position, then refines around only one selected candidate. These results do not rule out the key texts at other offsets or under different selection rules.

scope.representation: Exact pinned source rune files for global pages21–34,43,44,49,54 matched to LP2-04–17,26–27,32,37; three exact committed text corpora plus the authored SolvedLP literal.
scope.procedure: Replay the source method-5 100-step offset/direction screen, ±100 one-direction refinement, word-plus-coincidence ranking; test four corpus plants on and off the sampling grid, one complete synthetic grid, and 49 whole-grid page shuffles.
scope.parameters: 18 pages × 4 source texts = 72 returned page/text candidates, each selected from its exact adaptive offset search; 49 full 72-candidate controls.
scope.exclusions: Other source branches, unsampled offsets not promoted by the source, other corpora/editions, resets, interruptions, alternate scoring and complete decryptors.

wulfic-autokey-seed-families.title: Short seeds for autokey ciphers
wulfic-autokey-seed-families.question: Could a short word or rune seed drive an autokey cipher?
wulfic-autokey-seed-families.finding: None of the tested seeds passed the source’s screening rule. The distinct four-rune DEOR seed covered only ten pages, and the source did not test word resets. Its controls recovered a planted reading in all six feedback modes.
wulfic-autokey-seed-families.limitations: The screen assumes single-rune words mean I or A and uses a whole-page frequency score. It cannot identify every short seed or rule out autokey in general.

scope.representation: Pinned archived source GP29 page values verified against current LP2-04–37 text; source pages old21–54 map to LP2-(old−17). Source isolated-word positions retained.
scope.procedure: Replay six GP29 plaintext/ciphertext feedback recurrences for 22 source keyword seeds, every two-rune seed, every three-rune seed on source-eligible pages, and the one distinct four-rune P21–30 DEOR array. Preserve source gates, strict IoC threshold and page resets; compare 49 full-search shuffles.
scope.parameters: 4,488 named-keyword, 171,564 two-rune, 4,536,354 three-rune, and 60 distinct P21–30 DEOR settings; 49 within-page shuffled complete searches, seed 20261023.
scope.exclusions: Other seeds or lengths, alternate alphabets, word resets and segmentations, different singleton assumptions, English scoring, the P21–30 running-key/double-layer branches, and manuscript-derived numerical autokey rules without an exact recurrence.

wulfic-cicada-byte-key-phases.title: Archived Cicada numbers and byte streams as LP2 keys
wulfic-cicada-byte-key-phases.question: Do Cicada number and byte streams work as LP2 keys?
wulfic-cicada-byte-key-phases.finding: All 43,500 LP2 candidate rows and 200 control rows match the pinned source tables at published 0.01-nat precision. No LP2 setting reaches +30. The highest score, +2.41, is on the nine-rune title; its absolute score ceiling is only +11.19, so its 4,350 settings could never pass. The best other section scores −50.75, and the complete joined text peaks at −1,479.67. Correct-key planted controls score at least +169.09 and wrong-key controls at most −60.86. The compiled scorer agrees with the source on real and synthetic parity cases.
wulfic-cicada-byte-key-phases.limitations: The nine-rune title is too short for this +30 threshold under any key, so those 4,350 settings are not informative negatives. This screen uses only the source's 25 inputs, two GP29 mappings, ten transcript alignments, three arithmetic modes, 29 shifts, solved-LP1 unigram model, drift probabilities and uniform start-phase prior. Controls show power for this generated model at two longer lengths, not for every LP2 construction. Other preprocessing, keys, schedules, language models and cipher layers remain untested.

scope.representation: Source GP29 rune transcript in sections 7–15 and their continuous join, covering unsolved LP2-00–55; section labels are not manuscript page numbers.
scope.procedure: Read 25 pinned number/byte sources into modulo-29 and rejection-mapped key streams. For each of 50 keys and ten section alignments, score three arithmetic modes and all 29 shifts with the pinned phase-averaged stay/advance/skip HMM. Replay 200 planted positive/negative pairs with exact seed. Compare all serialized rows against the pinned Stage R tables.
scope.parameters: 50 mapped streams × 10 alignments × 3 modes × 29 shifts = 43,500 source settings; +30-nat pass line; uniform cyclic phase, transition 0.02/0.96/0.02, epsilon 0.1, pruning 1e−12. Control lengths 729 and 3316, fresh/next rekey, keep 0.19, RNG seed 3301.
scope.exclusions: Other source bytes, ordering, mapping, page segmentation, selected rather than averaged phase, alternative drift/rekey model, key operations, plaintext prior or downstream layer.

wulfic-crib-lfsr-recurrence.title: Can a guessed word seed a short feedback key?
wulfic-crib-lfsr-recurrence.question: Could a guessed word reveal the key for the following runes?
wulfic-crib-lfsr-recurrence.finding: The best continuation from the guessed words scored no better than many shuffled pages: 126 of 199 shuffled searches matched or exceeded it. A separate planted known reading was recovered correctly.
wulfic-crib-lfsr-recurrence.limitations: This covers 13 fixed words and short feedback rules on 11 pages. Other words, key clocks and feedback rules remain untested.

scope.representation: Pinned source page-number mapping separately preserves the source's J-dropping rune sequence on 11 LP2 pages plus solved LP1-15. Corrected scan uses canonical GP29 site arrays for the 11 LP2 pages; each source array equals its canonical counterpart with J removed.
scope.procedure: Replay the source's original crib-drag Berlekamp-Massey and IoC gate. Separately fit the first m-2 key symbols from each selected source crib, verify the last two, predict the next 128 runes and score only that continuation; rerun the complete page/crib/mode/offset selection on 199 shared seeded page shuffles.
scope.parameters: Original 21 source cribs length>=4, 3 directions and 12 mapped pages; corrected 13 source cribs length>=6, 3 directions, recurrence order 2–5, all offsets leaving 128 runes, 11 LP2 pages; 199 shuffle trials seed 20261023.
scope.exclusions: Other LP2 pages, other cribs, order>5, non-GP alphabets, key skips/resets, unrelated recurrence laws, a trained language model, and proof of full decryption.

wulfic-deor-interlocking-streams.title: Deor and interlocking rune streams
wulfic-deor-interlocking-streams.question: Can Deor unlock one stream and use it to unlock the rest?
wulfic-deor-interlocking-streams.finding: The original hit conditions cannot be satisfied: raw IoC is at most 1, while the program requires more than 1.3 or 1.5. On LP2-03, its selected first-stage candidate adds Deor at offset 47 and scores 0.0649; the second subtracts the selected key at offset 31 and scores 0.0404. A separate normalized comparison gives a second-stage maximum of 1.173, reached or exceeded by 110 of 199 whole-procedure shuffles. The first-stage maximum is 1.882, reached by 18 of 199 shuffles.
wulfic-deor-interlocking-streams.limitations: Zero original source HIT rows are not negative evidence because the gates cannot pass. The normalized test was frozen separately and measures only one page, one pinned Deor stream, a prime-index partition, the source direction/offset grids and one histogram-preserving shuffle model. Synthetic controls verify arithmetic, not power to detect English. Other two-stream ciphers remain untested.

scope.representation: Current LP2-03 canonical GP29 rune values, exactly matching archived old page_20 after filtering; split by whether rune index is prime.
scope.procedure: Replay original code in a temp folder; independently run all 1,800 first-stage Deor variants, select maximum raw IoC, then all 195 repeating-derived-key variants, retaining original unreachable HIT gates. Separately compare 29×normalized maxima with 199 whole-procedure page shuffles.
scope.parameters: 217 runes:65 prime-index,152 other; source Old English Deor parser yields960 values; 3 modes×600 offsets and3 modes×65 repeat offsets; 29 Caesar shifts; 199 seeded page shuffles, seed20261023.
scope.exclusions: Other pages, alternative prime definitions/partitions, modern Deor translation, other poems, word resets, variable key feedback, other language scores and all untested stream rules.

wulfic-doublet-leak-h-o.title: What separates LP2’s surviving doublets?
wulfic-doublet-leak-h-o.question: Do the surviving repeated runes reveal how LP2 was encrypted?
wulfic-doublet-leak-h-o.finding: All 16 selected H/O source assertions pass. The independent checker recreates 12,947 within-section pairs and all 86 doublets from site pages, then recalculates all 62 period/clock rows and remaining manuscript summaries. The strongest nonzero-difference z is −2.58, line breaks hold 4/585 repeats, best period p is 0.0355 versus 0.000161 corrected line, and nine-section p is 0.721. Two named key-switch constructions yield at most 10/2,898 repeats on solved text; the specified skip-next model has LP2 LLR −21.34 below its −10 line.
wulfic-doublet-leak-h-o.limitations: The source pairs join pages within nine sections, unlike the site's page-only 12,901-pair count. The H checks test chosen summaries and their declared selection rules, not all historical questions about doublets. H5 extrapolates from two named key pairs on solved text. O C14 assumes a 0.19 repeat parameter and solved-text difference profile. None decrypts LP2 or excludes arbitrary collision avoidance.

scope.representation: Source nine-section LP2-00–55 GP29 stream with written-line and page markers, 12,947 within-section adjacent pairs; site page text independently reconstructs all pair positions and marker flags.
scope.procedure: Run unchanged source H and O unittest classes with synthetic controls; preserve source pair/control input ledger; independently rebuild pairs from site raw pages and recompute H L1–L5 plus O C14.
scope.parameters: L1 28 residues, |z|=3.5; L2 line-break 2.5% rule; L3 31 periods×2 clocks and Bonferroni .01/62; L4 nine sections and 500-pair windows; L5 two named key pairs×ideal/literal switches; O fixed repeat .19 and LLR cutoff −10.
scope.exclusions: Other pair-boundary conventions, unspecified or adaptive key switches, other skip rates/plaintext models, decoder outputs, later cipher layers and any mechanism lacking an independently testable output.

wulfic-early-keyspace-diagnostics.title: Four early keyspace checks on LP2
wulfic-early-keyspace-diagnostics.question: Do LP2 rune patterns fit these running-key or autokey models?
wulfic-early-keyspace-diagnostics.finding: All thirteen pinned test assertions pass. The strongest C10 and C13 pooled frequency LLRs are −14.38 and −14.27, below the source's −10 line. C11's minimum p is 0.000559 versus 0.00000501 after 1,998 lag/sign checks; C12's minimum approximate p is 0.003916 versus 0.00001 after 1,000 lags. The 12,956 source GP29 runes match Liberpedia's LP2 page text; an independent checker recalculates all 3,029 source manuscript rows.
wulfic-early-keyspace-diagnostics.limitations: C10/C13 depend on the source solved-LP1 plaintext distribution, independent key/plaintext values, fixed mappings and mixture weights; pooled unigram mismatch is not a search over every real English running key. C11/C12 are specific within-section diagnostics, not full decryptions or exclusions of arbitrary ciphertext feedback/substitution. The C12 tail uses Wilson-Hilferty approximation. Wide 60/100/256-value key alphabets lack power in this frequency test and are not rejected.

scope.representation: Source GP29 canonical rune values in nine segments 7–15 over LP2-00–55; 12,956 positions, checked against all site page raw texts.
scope.procedure: Run unchanged pinned test_keyspace.py (13 assertions with synthetic controls); retain its exact C10–C13 manuscript score grids and model inputs; independently recalculate every score and compare source/site runes.
scope.parameters: C10: 3 maps×3 modes×3 mixtures, best of 29 offsets. C11: 999 lags×2 signs. C12: 1,000 lags. C13: four source key-value distributions, best of 3 modes×29 offsets. Source −10-nat and Bonferroni .01 thresholds.
scope.exclusions: Other plaintext corpora or distributions, key/plaintext dependence, alternate GP mappings, word/page resets, lag >1,000, nonlinear feedback, additional layers and direct decryption quality.

wulfic-grid-compression-source-replay.title: Complete-stream decompression of the LP2 number grid
wulfic-grid-compression-source-replay.question: Does the number grid decompress as a complete stream?
wulfic-grid-compression-source-replay.finding: Zero of 20 complete-grid decoder calls reaches EOF. All 24 pinned X4 rows reproduce exactly, including four absent offset-zero signature rows. The source's 100,000-block calibration yielded 552 raw-DEFLATE EOFs and zero observed for each other decoder; independent recomputation matches. Synthetic complete/truncated/trailing-junk controls pass as separately labeled post-replay diagnostics.
wulfic-grid-compression-source-replay.limitations: Only 256 exact printed-grid bytes, four source routes, five decoder APIs, offset zero, a single call and 1 MiB output cap. Source EOF does not require consuming all input; zero calibration hits is finite-sample evidence, not a true zero rate. Other byte constructions, offsets, keys, formats and larger outputs remain untested.

scope.representation: The 256 printed base-60 grid cells parsed to bytes in row/reversed-row/column/reversed-column order.
scope.procedure: Replay the pinned Stage X4 component with 100,000 seeded uniform-byte calibration blocks for each decoder. Test each complete grid route with raw DEFLATE, zlib, gzip, bzip2 and LZMA; also preserve Stage N offset-zero signature rows. Independently reconstruct the grid and every decoder result.
scope.parameters: Five source decoders × four routes = 20 complete-stream calls, plus four signature checks. One bounded call per decoder with 1 MiB output cap; source PASS requires EOF and empirical null rate ×20≤0.01.
scope.exclusions: Nonzero offsets, prefixes, modified grid cells, keys or other transformations, other compression formats, full-input-consumption requirement and larger decompressed outputs.

wulfic-grid-long-byte-sources.title: Archived byte streams against the LP2 number grid
wulfic-grid-long-byte-sources.question: Do archived byte streams reveal a low-diversity grid message?
wulfic-grid-long-byte-sources.finding: All 24 source planted positives pass and all 18 negative controls stay above the cutoff. None of 96 source/route/operation cells has a phase with D≤120 distinct bytes; the minimum is D=139 over 2,865,136 phase trials. Both pinned source tables were reproduced byte-for-byte, and an independent checker recomputed every LP2 phase from the site grid and bundled byte inputs.
wulfic-grid-long-byte-sources.limitations: This excludes low-diversity output under these six exact source bytes, four routes, four operations and all cyclic phases. It does not exclude a high-diversity plaintext, another key, different grid construction, altered key schedule, other decoding layer or another language.

scope.representation: The 256 printed 32×8 grid cells parsed as base-60 byte values from Liberpedia's exact token export.
scope.procedure: For each of six pinned source byte streams, all cyclic phases, row/row-reverse/column/column-reverse and XOR/grid-minus-key/grid-plus-key/key-minus-grid, count distinct values in the complete 256-byte output. Preserve source positive and negative gates and independently recompute all LP2 minima.
scope.parameters: Six source streams; 16 route/operation cells each; 2,865,136 source-phase trials. D≤120 passes. Twenty-four source positives at their planted cells, 18 uniform-grid negatives, and negative mean D within 162.0±0.5 are required for a valid run.
scope.exclusions: Other sources, partial or reordered bytes, offsets in grid or file structures beyond the source's cyclic key phase, alternate statistics and later decoding layers.

wulfic-grid-native-keys.title: Cicada-derived keys against the LP2 grid
wulfic-grid-native-keys.question: Do known Cicada numbers unlock the 256-cell grid?
wulfic-grid-native-keys.finding: The best byte output is 42.6% printable, below the source's 90% screen, with no named signature. The highest rune log likelihood is 4.63 nats, below +30. No source setting passes.
wulfic-grid-native-keys.limitations: The source uses one row-order grid and reversal, specified key starts/streams, a permissive byte-printability or offset-zero signature screen, and a solved-LP1 unigram detector. Planted controls were added after replay and do not establish power against all plausible LP2 messages.

scope.representation: Printed 32×8 grid as 256 base-60-derived bytes or 512 separate base-60 digits, conditionally using the site's pinned digit order; forward and full reverse only.
scope.procedure: Replay source Stage N all 456 rows, independently rebuild the grid from site export, repeat 72 byte transforms and 384 GP29 likelihood calculations, then run explicitly post-replay synthetic detector diagnostics.
scope.parameters: 12 finite byte keys×3 operations×2 directions=72; two GP29 grid encodings×2 directions×3 decode modes×(29 constant shifts+3 rune streams)=384; source thresholds 90% printable or listed signature, and log LR+30 nats.
scope.exclusions: Other grid layouts, ten disputed stems, later offsets, decryption-plus-decompression, other key derivations/starts, different scoring languages and plaintext interpretation beyond the source screens.

wulfic-grid-periodic-byte-invariant.title: Repeating-byte-alphabet invariant on the LP2 grid
wulfic-grid-periodic-byte-invariant.question: Could a repeating byte alphabet explain the number grid?
wulfic-grid-periodic-byte-invariant.finding: No grid reading/period cell exceeds the maximum of 100,000 uniform-byte nulls. Under the source's lower 0.1% control rule, 241/256 cells are excluded for Emerson English, 247/256 for solved LP1 runes, 247/256 for HEX, and 78/256 for Base64. No decoding is produced.
wulfic-grid-periodic-byte-invariant.limitations: The exclusions require a fixed bijection at each periodic residue and the source's exact plaintext-control classes and 256-byte representation. Other grid routes, transformations, layered ciphers and plaintext distributions remain outside scope.

scope.representation: The 256 printed grid tokens as base-60 bytes, traversed in printed 32×8 row order or column-major order.
scope.procedure: Replay only pinned Wulfic Stage X2 and independently reconstruct all 256 grid coincidence counts, pair capacities and source decisions; verify a planted residue-bijection invariant.
scope.parameters: Two readings × periods 1–128; 100,000 seeded uniform-null blocks; 9,024 Emerson, 2,646 solved-LP1, 10,000 HEX and 10,000 Base64 256-byte controls; source upper-maximum and lower-0.1%-quantile rules.
scope.exclusions: Other traversal routes, offsets, payload extraction, compression, non-bijective or changing alphabets, transposition, layered ciphers, and Stage X1/X3/X4 tests.

wulfic-grid-rsa-modulus-screen.title: Raw grid bytes and RSA-modulus readings
wulfic-grid-rsa-modulus-screen.question: What can the raw grid bytes tell us?
wulfic-grid-rsa-modulus-screen.finding: The grid has 161 distinct byte values versus 161.99957 across 100,000 uniform-reference blocks. None of seven fixed statistics rejects at 0.01/7. All four literal integer readings are divisible by 3 and 7; both big-endian readings are even, and both little-endian readings have 2,047 bits. All eleven source rows reproduce byte-for-byte.
wulfic-grid-rsa-modulus-screen.limitations: Passing seven statistical checks does not prove randomness or identify a cipher. The integer screen excludes only these literal conventional RSA-2048 modulus readings with large prime factors; it does not exclude weak RSA parameters, other layouts or using the bytes as RSA ciphertext or a signature.

scope.representation: The 256 printed grid cells parsed as base-60 byte values, unchanged; 32 rows by 8 columns.
scope.procedure: Independently parse every cell, measure seven fixed byte statistics against 100,000 iid uniform blocks, and test each row/column big/little-endian integer against every prime below one million. Run original pinned X1/X3 components and compare all eleven rows.
scope.parameters: NumPy default_rng(3311) in 10,000-block chunks; two-sided plus-one Monte Carlo tail; 0.01/7 cutoff; four literal integers; 78,498 primes below one million.
scope.exclusions: No decryption, keyed transform, alternate transcription or arbitrary route; no proof of randomness, general RSA exclusion or complete factorization.

wulfic-keyed-transposition-cohort.title: Archived keyword-and-route transposition search
wulfic-keyed-transposition-cohort.question: Does rearranging these keyed pages produce a reading?
wulfic-keyed-transposition-cohort.finding: All ten archived page files match LP2-04–13 rune for rune, although the program calls them pages 21–30. Its keyword-column and magic-square planted inversions, and six other permutation properties, pass 80 controls. None of the 585 reported route rows produces a word match under its own embedded-word scorer. The source still exhaustively scores short-key column orders before retaining one best row per eligible page.
wulfic-keyed-transposition-cohort.limitations: The page keywords are proposals. The source scores unbroken GP runeglish, has no optional external wordlist in the pinned tree, and does not actually call the Myszkowski or disrupted methods advertised in comments. Other key schedules, segmentation rules, languages, page mappings and transpositions are outside this result.

scope.representation: Exact GP29 rune sequence from pinned Wulfic global page_21–30 files, aligned to current LP2-04–13 JSON. Source unbroken runeglish and 95-word embedded fallback.
scope.procedure: Execute the pinned source's own solve_page loop for each aligned page with its fixed keyword/mode; retain every reported row and planted route controls.
scope.parameters: Ten fixed source page/key/mode assignments; all column permutations for source keywords of at most seven letters; source-listed fixed widths, rails, grid routes, prime extraction, every-nth and reversal.
scope.exclusions: No arbitrary key search, other current LP2 pages, new segmentation, alternative English model, Myszkowski or disrupted transposition, and no inference from a best score to a decipherment.

wulfic-keyword-lfsr.title: Keyword-seeded register shifts
wulfic-keyword-lfsr.question: Could an archived keyword seed a feedback shift register that decrypts these pages?
wulfic-keyword-lfsr.finding: None of the 400 tested keyword-seeded register settings produced an output that passed the program’s language screen. The search did recover a complete 209-rune known message under one of those settings.
wulfic-keyword-lfsr.limitations: This covers the ten fixed keywords and specified register rules on LP2-04–13. Passing the screen would not by itself establish a reading, and other feedback rules remain open.

scope.representation: Exact committed Wulfic rune files for old pages 21–30, matched rune for rune to current LP2-04–13.
scope.procedure: Replay the source keyword-seeded LFSR, strict normalized-IoC reporting gate, complete planted known-reading search, and 199 whole-grid page-shuffle controls.
