scope.parameters: 400 source settings, 396 distinct manuscript decoded outputs, 199 complete page-shuffle searches.
scope.exclusions: Other states/taps, other pages, interruption or reset rules, layered ciphers and alternate score gates.

wulfic-keyword-prime-layer-grid.title: Keywords paired with prime-derived streams
wulfic-keyword-prime-layer-grid.question: Could a keyword and a prime stream remove two cipher layers?
wulfic-keyword-prime-layer-grid.finding: Across 224,128 keyword/stream/sign/page settings on LP2-04–37, none scored above the source IoC>1.40 screen. The maximum was 1.2902 on LP2-32. A 515-rune established reading encrypted with one declared setting was recovered exactly and scored 1.7231. In 49 seeded page-wise shuffle controls repeating the full search, 42 reached a maximum at least as high as the LP2 maximum.
wulfic-keyword-prime-layer-grid.limitations: This is the exact finite source grid adapted to verified current text, not a replay of the archived script’s old results. Its directory and page-number assumptions were outdated; old page_21–54 means current LP2-04–37. A prior wrong-target exploratory run was discarded and documented. The 515-rune positive control is longer than any target page, so it does not establish equal power on short pages. IoC is not a language detector; 49 shuffles preserve page histograms but do not model every cipher. Other keywords, stream rules, phases, boundaries or layers remain outside scope. Keyword labels refer to literal source numeric arrays; the AETHEREAL array includes an extra H after TH, so a conventional re-encoding is not covered.

scope.representation: Current canonical GP29 rune streams for LP2-04–37, verified length and SHA256 identical to the archived source’s old page_21–54 rune streams. Each page is separate; no word resets.
scope.procedure: For each page apply all 16 source numeric keyword arrays, 103 source second streams and four keyword/stream sign pairs modulo29. Score source-normalized IoC; record each page maximum and IoC>1.40 count. Plant a complete known reading and rerun the full selection on 49 seeded within-page shuffles.
scope.parameters: 34 pages ×16 keyword arrays ×103 second streams ×4 sign pairs =224,128 settings. Second streams: 50 prime-minus-one offsets, 50 prime offsets, cumulative prime-minus-one, linear and Fibonacci. Source IoC screen>1.40; 49 page-wise histogram-preserving shuffles, seed20261023.
scope.exclusions: LP2 outside pages04–37; keyword phase changes, new words, transpositions, alternate prime orders/indices, feedback, page joins, null skipping, adaptive keys, additional layers and non-IoC language scores.

wulfic-keyword-quagmire-models.title: Named keyword Quagmire alphabets on LP2
wulfic-keyword-quagmire-models.question: Do named keyword alphabets fit LP2's rune frequencies?
wulfic-keyword-quagmire-models.finding: The source calibration gate passes and there are no +10 leads. Four key distributions have all 314,432 combinations both control-powered and below the source's −10 exclusion cutoff. Hexadecimal digits leave 135 powered non-exclusions; uniform A–Z leaves 10,197, while 272,640 A–Z combinations lack power. No plaintext or key is recovered.
wulfic-keyword-quagmire-models.limitations: This is a unigram frequency screen of fixed named alphabets and independent key-value distributions, not a decryption. It does not test arbitrary keywords, actual key order, alternative boundaries, non-independent keys or layered ciphers. Raw source exclusions must not be confused with control-powered exclusions.

scope.representation: Canonical GP29 LP2-00–55 stream represented by its pooled 12,956-rune frequency vector.
scope.procedure: Rerun pinned Stage V's G1 same-family model controls and G2 flat-key power screen, then audit all source family summaries and listed survivors. Independently reconstruct the site manuscript rune vector.
scope.parameters: 34 source-specified keywords yield 68 distinct alphabets including identity and inverse forms. All 68^3 alphabet triples for each of six key-value distributions, maximizing over three sign modes and 29 offsets; −10 exclusion, +10 lead, and at least 18/20 G2 flat-key exclusions for power.
scope.exclusions: Other keywords or alphabet constructions, dependent or ordered keys, page-specific resets, alternate statistics and sequence-level decryption.

wulfic-keyword-ramp.title: A keyword that shifts with each rune
wulfic-keyword-ramp.question: Could a page keyword change its shift at every rune?
wulfic-keyword-ramp.finding: The nine tested step sizes produced no established reading on LP2-04–13. The best word score was matched or beaten by 10 of 199 complete shuffled searches. The same search recovered a 209-rune known message when it used the tested key rule.
wulfic-keyword-ramp.limitations: Only the ten assigned keywords and nine fixed step sizes were tested. Other keywords, changing step schedules, resets and languages remain open.

scope.representation: Exact committed Wulfic rune streams for old pages21–30, rune-for-rune aligned to current LP2-04–13.
scope.procedure: Apply each source-assigned GP29 keyword with all nine called progressive steps; score with the source English-substring function. Check one full known-reading plant and 199 shared page shuffles of the entire 90-case grid.
scope.parameters: 10 pages × 9 source steps = 90 candidate outputs; 199 complete shared page-shuffle searches, seed 20261023.
scope.exclusions: Other branches of advanced_cipher_solver.py, pages without assigned keywords, other step values or scoring models.

wulfic-lag-reuse-models.title: Distant key reuse and ciphertext autokeys
wulfic-lag-reuse-models.question: Could a key or ciphertext segment repeat elsewhere in LP2?
wulfic-lag-reuse-models.finding: After correcting only an original one-row control-array allocation in memory, all six AC/AD source result tables reproduce byte-for-byte. AC's best whole-lag, forward-stretch and reverse-stretch scores are +7.05, +19.86 and +18.23; AD's are +5.30, +22.49 and +23.16. All are below +30. AD's +5.30 whole-lag maximum has only 14 pair opportunities and an absolute +17.41 ceiling, so cannot pass at any key. The 138 AC and 184 AD planted-control rows match; both four-null gates are valid. Source/site GP29 text agrees across 12,956 positions, with selected pair-law scores independently recomputed.
wulfic-lag-reuse-models.limitations: The source programs cannot run unchanged: both crash in one-row reuse controls. The in-memory shape correction is disclosed and all original tables must match before accepting a result. AC's whole-lag exclusions are calibrated only through gap 12,500 and its all-cell reused-stretch detection only from 3,000 runes; AD's corresponding bounds are 12,900 and 200. The AD maximum whole-lag score comes from an underpowered 14-pair tail. Other pair laws, word resets, changing keys, language models or later decoding layers remain untested.

scope.representation: The source's continuous 12,956 GP29 rune values for LP2-00–55, verified identical to the site page transcription.
scope.procedure: Repair only AC's one-row control cumsum allocation in memory. Reproduce AC and AD full original planted-control grids, four anti-doublet null streams each, all forward lags 11 through N−11 and all eligible reverse anti-diagonals. AC tests three pair laws ×29 shifts; AD tests four ×29. Compare every generated lag, top and control TSV byte with the pinned source; independently recompute representative scores.
scope.parameters: AC: 12,935 forward lags, 3 relations, 29 shifts, 138 control rows, Pmax 12,500/Mmin 3,000. AD: same 12,935 lag rows, 4 relations, 29 shifts, 184 control rows, Pmax 12,900/Mmin 200. Fixed +30 positive line and −10 calibrated exclusion line; four null streams per stage. Source-provided control draws and seeds retained.
scope.exclusions: Different text layers, page/word resets, lag under 11, other pair laws or plaintext priors, adaptive shifts, keys with nonlinear evolution, and reused stretches shorter than each calibrated control bound.

wulfic-letter-encoding-bounds.title: Two letter-encoding bounds on LP2
wulfic-letter-encoding-bounds.question: Could simple rules for repeated runes or homophones explain LP2?
wulfic-letter-encoding-bounds.finding: The marker rule narrows 29 plaintext runes to NG, IA and EA by repeat count, then none survives the word-position check. In a separate fixed, even-choice homophone model, the optimal expected frequency mismatch is 4,802 versus 26 observed on LP2; the source cutoff is 200. Six targeted source tests pass and independent checks reconstruct the manuscript statistics and optimum.
wulfic-letter-encoding-bounds.limitations: Both are conditional model exclusions, not statements about every cipher. The marker result uses solved-reading frequencies and word positions as plaintext proxies and assumes a fixed marker with nonzero multiplier. The homophone result assumes dedicated ciphertext symbols, even choices and the solved sample as a plaintext-frequency proxy. Context-dependent mappings, uneven choices and further layers are not tested.

scope.representation: Canonical GP29 rune indices from LP2-00–55; 2,901 solved plaintext runes for conditional frequency/position calibration. Nine LP2 section boundaries prevent a false adjacent pair.
scope.procedure: Replay original C3 and C15 source tests. Independently count LP2 repeats and word classes, run all 29 C3 marker candidates with the original Poisson and position cutoffs, and enumerate/verify the best C15 ciphertext-symbol allocation.
scope.parameters: C3: 12,947 adjacent opportunities, 86 doublets, count p<1e-6 and word-position LLR<=-10 exclusion gates. C15: 29 ciphertext symbols allocated to 26 used plaintext categories; 3,654 allocations including unused slots; even within-category choices; expected chi-square exclusion cutoff 200.
scope.exclusions: Other text layers, alternate word segmentation, changing marker runes, zero or adaptive multipliers, unequal or shared homophones, stateful alphabets, non-LP1 plaintext priors and additional cipher stages.

wulfic-lfsr-singleton-constraints.title: Can single-rune words pin down an LFSR key?
wulfic-lfsr-singleton-constraints.question: Can one-rune words reveal the key stream?
wulfic-lfsr-singleton-constraints.finding: Across all 29^L feedback tuples for each L=1–5, no selected page has a complete singleton fit at L1–2. At L5, the source's first-L invertible search yields four LP2-28 Beaufort fits, 27,424 combined subtraction/Beaufort fits on LP2-24 and 5,808,457 on LP2-21. Addition has exact signed-state symmetry with subtraction and is not counted again in that comparison. All four LP2-28 full-page example decodes have normalized IoC below the source's 1.3 shortcut; no full-page English selection claim is made.
wulfic-lfsr-singleton-constraints.limitations: Assumes every visible one-rune word is plaintext I or A, canonical GP indices, page-local continuous key and first-L invertible basis. Singular first-L systems are excluded by the source algorithm. Full-grid dictionary scoring is not calibrated or claimed. Fitting singleton slots does not identify a ciphertext generator or decryption.

scope.representation: Canonical GP29 page-local rune streams; source parser singleton positions: 12 on LP2-28, 9 on LP2-24, 7 on LP2-21. Pinned archived scan ordinals 45, 41 and 38 separately checked by unchanged source parser.
scope.procedure: Exhaust feedback tap tuples over GF(29), solve invertible first-L singleton constraints for all I/A assignments, test remaining singletons and decode example full pages exactly; independent small-grid oracle and planted controls.
scope.parameters: L=1..5; each coefficient 0..28; plaintext I=10 or A=24 at visible one-rune words; sub/add/Beaufort directions; first-L invertible systems only; 29^L tuples per length and target.
scope.exclusions: Different singleton plaintext, non-GP mapping, page-spanning or skipped clocks, singular source basis, other recurrence families, whole-grid calibrated English verdict and proof of decryption.

wulfic-liber-al-offset-sweep.title: Liber AL offset search on LP2-08
wulfic-liber-al-offset-sweep.question: Does the Book of the Law unlock this page?
wulfic-liber-al-offset-sweep.finding: The best LP2-08 score is 670; 154 of 199 shuffled-order controls score at least as high after the complete search. Four planted messages at coarse offsets 300 and 1700 are found in both modes; the same message at off-grid offset 137 is missed in both. The source search examines 2,104 refined offsets, not all possible positions.
wulfic-liber-al-offset-sweep.limitations: This is a new corrected-input variant because the source's archived optimizer outputs are disclaimed and its historical offset report is absent. Shuffling rune order is a descriptive control, not a cipher model. The score counts six English trigrams in unbroken runeglish and cannot establish a reading; missed offsets, other book editions, mappings, page identities and the follow-on substitution optimizer remain outside scope.

scope.representation: Exact 255 GP29 runes from pinned Wulfic global page_25 file, aligned to LP2-08; exact 11,837-byte committed Liber AL corpus greedily converted by the source to 8,187 GP values.
scope.procedure: Run the source's complete 102-row coarse search, take its six best tuple-sorted rows, examine both modes within ±200 of those offsets, keep duplicate coarse/refined rows and source top 100. Repeat the complete selection on 199 shuffled-order pages; run sampled and off-grid planted controls.
scope.parameters: Source offsets 0..5,000 in steps of 100 followed by source-selected ±200 neighborhoods; Beaufort and subtract modes; source weighted six-trigram score and IoC secondary ordering; shuffle seed 20261023.
scope.exclusions: LP2-25/current ordinal 42, unselected offsets, other corpus editions or encodings, the source's stochastic P25 substitution postprocessor, and a claim that all running keys or all offsets fail.

wulfic-local-codebook-invariants.title: Fixed local codebooks and repeat preservation
wulfic-local-codebook-invariants.question: Could a fixed local rule have produced the sparse repeats in LP2?
wulfic-local-codebook-invariants.finding: Five of 26 local-context width cells and 26 of 72 word/block-codebook cells are excluded. The other 67 cells are unresolved by their positive controls; no LP2 cipher or plaintext is identified.
wulfic-local-codebook-invariants.limitations: The invariant assumes a fixed position-independent local rule or fixed word/block mapping, with the source's anti-doublet redrawing model. Long contexts/blocks often have too few repeat opportunities; variable keys, state and altered boundaries remain outside scope.

scope.representation: Pinned 12,956-rune, 2,896-word LP2 section 7–15 transcription; nine sections, with within-section or joined-stream grouping; word/block equality in GP29 indices.
scope.procedure: Replay exact Wulfic Stage AA and Z source output tables; independently reconstruct manuscript words and recount every declared LP2 repeated-unit statistic; verify control verdicts and an injective planted invariant.
scope.parameters: AA widths 0–12, n-grams 3–7, two grouping modes; Z word comparisons and aligned blocks n=2–8 at every offset, two modes. Source seed 3301, 1,000 null draws and 200 positive draws per Emerson and LP1 source per cell, with 81% redraw of adjacent repeats.
scope.exclusions: Position-dependent or keyed mappings, arbitrary mutable state, different section/word boundaries, corrected transcription, other sources or control distributions, and claims of plaintext recovery.

wulfic-native-key-streams.title: Prime, solved-text and grid streams as LP2 keys
wulfic-native-key-streams.question: What happens when Cicada's own numbers are used as a key?
wulfic-native-key-streams.finding: No +30 threshold hits in 5,742 source settings. Finite keys of 256–726 values leave later emissions neutral in several arms; whole-section exclusions are inconclusive. Supplemental controls establish detection only at lengths within each key.
wulfic-native-key-streams.limitations: The source starts each key at zero and scores only until a finite key ends. The supplemental controls were designed after the LP2 source results, not preregistered. Results do not cover cyclic keys, other starts, alternate grid transcriptions, other languages or other ciphers.

scope.representation: Pinned 12,956-rune section 7–15 stream plus three grid-relative windows; Stage I key values from source-solved LP1 text or primes, Stage M grid representations matching Liberpedia's 256 tokens.
scope.procedure: Replay pinned Stage I and M complete candidate grids, then measure a separately identified post-replay planted-key diagnostic within each finite key's usable length.
scope.parameters: Three Stage I keys × 10 alignments and three Stage M keys × 12 alignments; all three sub/add/Beaufort directions and 29 shifts; start at zero; source reading threshold log LR >=30. Supplemental 20 planted and 20 wrong-key draws per stream.
scope.exclusions: Other start positions or cycling, arbitrary LP1-derived streams, different grid bytes or digit mappings, different scoring language, and Stage I's separate nine-rune vocabulary check.

wulfic-number-key-streams.title: Mathematical digit streams as LP2 keys
wulfic-number-key-streams.question: Could a mathematical constant or totient sequence be the key?
wulfic-number-key-streams.finding: All 19,140 source settings scored below the +30 reading threshold. Every 729-rune-or-longer stream/alignment/mode group met the source exclusion rule; the 66 undecided groups contain only nine runes each. The complete source outputs were replayed byte-for-byte.
wulfic-number-key-streams.limitations: This tests only the pinned digit/arithmetic streams, GP29 representation, three arithmetic directions, 1,000 starting positions and source frequency model. The source's score is not adjusted over the whole grid. A nine-rune section cannot decide the remaining groups.

scope.representation: Pinned source 12,956 GP29 runes in sections 7–15; Liberpedia LP2-00–55 pages independently reproduce the complete rune stream.
scope.procedure: Replay Wulfic Stages AG and AH, validate all source candidate/control tables byte-for-byte, and independently check the parameter grid, page stream, arithmetic prefixes and duplicate stream.
scope.parameters: 10 AG names and 12 AH names (21 distinct streams); nine separate sections plus one continuous stream; sub/add/Beaufort; 29 shifts; 1,000 uniform start positions; score pass >=30, cell exclusion <=-10 for all shifts after controls pass.
scope.exclusions: Other numeric representations, stream sources, key starts, boundary treatments, language priors, cipher directions and state equations; the short nine-rune section remains inconclusive.

wulfic-p08-hint-grid-keys.title: Keys from LP1-08’s hidden grid
wulfic-p08-hint-grid-keys.question: Can the earlier hint grid serve as a repeating key for Liber Primus?
wulfic-p08-hint-grid-keys.finding: Across 17,766 source-specified rotated-key cases, 99 of 103 IoC>1.25 hits are on solved LP1 pages. The four LP2 hits are all on LP2-32; three are algebraically related. A retrospective LP2-only shared-shuffle diagnostic has 0/199 maxima at the observed 1.382, but does not identify a reading or cipher.
wulfic-p08-hint-grid-keys.limitations: This is a corrected-path adaptation: the source script points at nonexistent tools/pages. The original old P08–54 range covers LP1-08–16 and LP2-00–37 only. The source screen tests rune frequency, not readable text. The LP2-only comparison was selected after inspecting the LP1/LP2 split; conditional shuffles and 199 trials do not account for the wider historical choice of clue interpretations and key families.

scope.representation: Exact committed Wulfic page_08–54 rune files, mapped to current LP1-08–16 and LP2-00–37; 14/28-value keys from source-embedded hint pairs independently matched to the saved LP1-08 OutGuess bytes.
scope.procedure: Verify source-grid rows against the 140-byte LP1-08 payload; correct the legacy page path, replay seven unrotated keys and five keys at all rotations in three GP29 modes using the source IoC/singleton gates; encrypt known LP1 readings as positive controls; shuffle each source page 199 times and repeat the whole phase sweep.
scope.parameters: 47 pages; 987 fixed and 17,766 rotated-key cases; 510 planted transforms; source fixed IoC>1.3 or IoC>1.15 with singletons I/A, rotated IoC>1.25; 199 shared page shuffles. A later LP2-only readout uses the same random stream.
scope.exclusions: Other grid interpretations, bigram substitution, Koan-text keys, later LP2 pages, non-GP29 encodings, alternative word scoring and any broader historical idea search.

wulfic-p20-prime-position-routes.title: Prime-position route search on LP2-03
wulfic-p20-prime-position-routes.question: Does the prime-position route give a reading?
wulfic-p20-prime-position-routes.finding: Pinned page_20 maps to LP2-03 with 217 runes, not the 646 claimed in the source comment. Its nonprime-position stream has 170 runes. The 11-column route leads the 58 executed routes with six source-style trigram hits, a score reached or exceeded by 57/199 complete shuffled searches. The original source reports ten routes under branch-specific filters but does not establish a readable passage.
wulfic-p20-prime-position-routes.limitations: The shuffle comparison is descriptive, not a cipher model. The source uses variable-width GP Runeglish, brief English trigram lists, and no validated full-passage criterion. Only source-retained routes passed an unmodified-script synthetic parity gate; all 58 saved manuscript routes have separate index-map reconstruction. Other pages, reading rules, languages and layouts are outside scope.

scope.representation: Exact GP29 runes in Wulfic pages/page_20/runes.txt at commit bf89d3d, aligned to current LP2-03; source Runeglish output and committed Deor poem.
scope.procedure: Partition by prime zero-based rune position, take the 170-rune nonprime stream, choose the source's first maximal-IoC Caesar shift, and execute its 58 literal routes and branch-specific trigram screens. Retain the separate prime rune-index-value split as an audit, then compare whole-search maximums with 199 seeded full-page rune shuffles.
scope.parameters: One pinned source page; 29 Caesar shifts; 58 executed routes; 199 whole-search shuffles at seed 20261023.
scope.exclusions: No broader transposition family search, new word segmentation, other page alignment or output language, and no claim of plaintext from a trigram count.

wulfic-p21-literal-f-masks.title: Pausing the key at selected F runes
wulfic-p21-literal-f-masks.question: Can treating selected F runes as literal fix these keyword decodes?
wulfic-p21-literal-f-masks.finding: Exact pinned Wulfic pages 21–30 align to LP2-04–13. The unmodified source enumerates 27,402 literal-F masks, and no page has a mask satisfying all of its singleton I/A constraints. Its 45 fixed second-layer rune routes per page on the unmasked decode also print zero gate-passing rows. Nineteen whole-selection shuffled searches likewise have zero gated pages, so this gate does not distinguish the manuscript from the stated shuffle control.
wulfic-p21-literal-f-masks.limitations: The source keyword parser drops V in DIVINITY and contracts EO in DEOR; this replay preserves its actual arrays. The source's narrow singleton separator rule and IoC/bigram score are not a general reading test. The 19 shuffles are a coarse descriptive reference, not a cipher model. Other keys, page ranges, interruption rules or downstream layers are not tested.

scope.representation: Exact source Git-object rune files pages/page_21–30, rune-aligned to current LP2-04–13; the source's word separators and keyword parser.
scope.procedure: For each fixed page keyword/mode, enumerate every subset of ciphertext F positions as literal, non-advancing key slots. Apply the original all-singleton I/A gate, source score or fallback IoC rank, and source-defined unmasked second-layer routes. Run 19 complete page-shuffle controls.
scope.parameters: Ten pages, 1–14 F positions each, 27,402 total source masks, 45 fixed rune routes per page, 19 pagewise shuffle repeats, seed 20261023.
scope.exclusions: Corrected keyword parse, alternate F behavior, source pages outside 21–30, word-boundary variants, other languages and uncalled prime permutation helper.

wulfic-p21-rearrangement-routes.title: Keyword decryption and rearrangement
wulfic-p21-rearrangement-routes.question: Could rearranging these keyword-decoded pages reveal a reading?
wulfic-p21-rearrangement-routes.finding: This replay found a problem with the old program’s test, rather than a reading. It removes spaces before scoring character rearrangements, so even a correctly recovered multiword message gets zero points. The best manuscript score was also matched or beaten in 85 of 199 shuffled searches.
wulfic-p21-rearrangement-routes.limitations: These results do not rule out rearrangement. They cover the program’s 45 routes and proposed keywords on LP2-04–13; a better scorer would need to recover complete planted messages first.

scope.representation: Exact committed Wulfic source rune files for old pages21–30 aligned with current LP2-04–13, its fixed page keyword vectors and its committed 370,079-entry wordlist.
scope.procedure: Execute all 45 called source route outputs for each page, preserving branch-specific spacing and the source dictionary scorer. Check frequency and word-order invariants, complete reverse-route planted recovery, and 199 seeded whole-grid within-page shuffle searches.
scope.parameters: 450 source rows; 390 full-length route rows, 60 shortened extract rows; 199 complete shared-corpus shuffles seed 20261023.
scope.exclusions: A separate source file transposition_solver.py is covered elsewhere. This replay does not test uncalled source helpers, arbitrary keyword or route invention, alternate transcriptions, a better language scorer or cross-page routes.

wulfic-p21-running-key-layers.title: Deor and Emerson as running keys on ten pages
wulfic-p21-running-key-layers.question: Did those two texts work as keys for these pages?
wulfic-p21-running-key-layers.finding: Neither Deor nor Self-Reliance produced a candidate that passed the program’s first language screen on LP2-04–13. The complete replay checked 24,639 combinations of page, text offset and decoding rule. Planted messages could pass the screen, but the manuscript behaved like the shuffled-page controls.
wulfic-p21-running-key-layers.limitations: This tests two particular editions, sampled text offsets and one assigned keyword per page. A reading rejected by the coincidence screen would be missed; other texts, offsets and key clocks remain open.

scope.representation: Exact committed source global P21–30 rune files, each independently aligned with current LP2-04–13; source GP29 greedy encoding of committed Deor and Self-Reliance text.
scope.procedure: Reconstruct every executed direct running-key and assigned-keyword-plus-running-key offset/mode cell from the pinned program. Check normalized 29×IoC >1.3 before source wordlist scoring. Repeat the entire grid on 49 common seeded page shuffles. Execute the unchanged source in an isolated legacy-path staging tree.
scope.parameters: 12,327 direct and 12,312 layered settings; two committed texts; three decode directions; keyword±running combinations for the layered branch; source offset step max(1,max_offset//200) or //100; 49 controls seed 20261023.
scope.exclusions: The same program’s autokey-seed branch (already published separately), unsampled offsets, unassigned keywords, other texts or editions, alternate runic alphabets, other scores, interrupted clocks and page ranges.

wulfic-page24-prime-columnar.title: Prime positions and column readings on LP2-07
wulfic-page24-prime-columnar.question: What if we take prime-indexed runes, rearrange them, then shift the alphabet?
wulfic-page24-prime-columnar.finding: The best source trigram score was 225 at width 10, shift 16 on 46 zero-based-prime runes from LP2-07. In 222 of 256 page-shuffled full searches, the maximum was at least 225 (add-one 223/257). All 377 settings share exactly the same GP29 IoC, 0.981, because columnar reordering and alphabet shifting preserve rune frequencies.
wulfic-page24-prime-columnar.limitations: Only source page 24/current LP2-07, its 46-rune zero-based-prime selection, widths 2–14, shifts 0–28 and the source short Runeglish trigram table were tested. Shuffles are a selection control rather than a cipher model. The source relative page path is broken in the pinned tree, so this is a replay of stated operations from verified page bytes, not verification of a saved upstream run. Other index origins, layers and language scorers remain open.

scope.representation: All 208 pinned source page_24 runes, GP29-indexed, byte-for-byte equal to current LP2-07; punctuation and separators excluded from positions.
scope.procedure: Record seven first-stage source views. From zero-based prime positions, replay widths 2–14 and all 29 GP shifts under the source weighted Runeglish trigram scorer, then rerun that full grid after each of 256 within-page shuffles.
scope.parameters: Seven source views; one subsequent 13×29=377-setting grid; 256 complete-search shuffles with Random(20261023+trial). Planted selector/columnar/shift/scorer control fixed before manuscript scoring.
scope.exclusions: Other pages, index origins, prime complements in the second stage, widths or shifts outside source bounds, other scoring models, second ciphers or selected fragments.

wulfic-periodic-alphabet-lags.title: Repeating-alphabet periods across LP2
wulfic-periodic-alphabet-lags.question: Could a repeating alphabet explain the rune patterns?
wulfic-periodic-alphabet-lags.finding: Stage AE's valid source run excludes 10,030 of 12,935 periods using its 5% plaintext-agreement model and binomial lower-tail rule. All 100 planted periodic controls passed and none was excluded; no LP2 lag passed the positive rule.
wulfic-periodic-alphabet-lags.limitations: The result assumes a fixed bijective alphabet at each periodic residue, the source's English/LP1 controls, anti-doublet simulation and transcription. Lag-pair dependence and selection over 12,935 periods limit probability interpretation; other stateful or layered ciphers are not tested.

scope.representation: The joined 12,956-rune LP2 sections 7–15 stream in canonical GP29 order, with punctuation and page/line breaks omitted for rune-lag counting.
scope.procedure: Replay pinned Wulfic Stage AE source; independently reconstruct every rune-lag agreement count from site page text, three named binomial lower tails and a planted periodic bijection.
scope.parameters: All 12,935 lags 11–12,945; p_H=0.050 lower-tail threshold exp(-10), positive threshold 0.01/12,935 against empirical p0; 20 anti-doublet flat nulls and 100 planted controls at five named periods from Emerson and LP1; source seed3301.
scope.exclusions: Lags below11 or above12945, per-page resets, non-bijective or changing alphabets, keyed/drifting state, additional encryption layers, alternate transcriptions and languages with a different equality baseline.

wulfic-periodic-word-crib-votes.title: Can word cribs predict a periodic key?
wulfic-periodic-word-crib-votes.question: Can familiar words reveal a repeating key?
wulfic-periodic-word-crib-votes.finding: Keys fitted to guessed words on LP2-10 and LP2-13 predicted no dictionary words in the parts kept aside for checking. The method also missed most words in messages with known answers, so this attempt cannot rule out repeating-key ciphers.
wulfic-periodic-word-crib-votes.limitations: Only two pages, two proposed key lengths and one dictionary were tested. The key lengths were examples supplied with the method, not periods established in the manuscript.

scope.representation: Pinned source page_27 and page_30 rune files, byte-checked against site LP2-10 and LP2-13. Source GP29 encoder and exact 335-entry dictionary (309 distinct encoded words).
scope.procedure: Replay original word-vote keys and source stdout on the two example page/period pairs. Separately train on alternating visible word slots, score exact dictionary words on untouched slots, run 12 planted known-message folds and 199 matched whole-selection shuffles.
scope.parameters: Source periods 43 and 17; SUB, ADD, BEAUFORT; visible 2–15-rune words; source-insertion-order vote ties; two train/holdout folds; 199 shuffles seeded 33014317.
scope.exclusions: Other pages, periods, dictionaries, language hypotheses, page-spanning clocks, the checkpoint-dependent validator scripts, linked-position phrase crib script, and a family-wide cipher rejection.

wulfic-position-alphabet-flatness-bound.title: Random-alphabet flatness bound on LP2
wulfic-position-alphabet-flatness-bound.question: Can LP2's flat rune counts rule out small sets of random alphabets?
wulfic-position-alphabet-flatness-bound.finding: All declared source control gates pass. The 12,956-rune pooled statistic is 26.36; the eight-section statistic is 194.14 across 12,947 runes. Under the independent-random-permutation model, effective class counts through 168 pooled or 174 sectioned meet the source's 0.0001 exclusion rule. No plaintext or key is identified.
wulfic-position-alphabet-flatness-bound.limitations: These are source-calibrated model bounds, not cryptographic impossibility results. The independent random-permutation assumption, solved-LP1 frequency calibration, and source section choices matter. Latin-square/additive ciphers, correlated alphabets and layers are outside scope. The reported 153/133 sensitivity is post-run, not the original decision rule.

scope.representation: Canonical 29-rune indices from LP2-00–55, pooled or grouped by the source's marked sections 7–9 and 11–15. The sectioned rule omits the nine-rune section 10.
scope.procedure: Run pinned Stage T's full synthetic gates and Monte Carlo reference; independently reconstruct manuscript rune counts and chi-square values from Liberpedia page records, check the pooled analytic boundary, and verify source decisions.
scope.parameters: 200 synthetic controls each at V=29,256,1024; source alpha 0.0001; eight selected sections; 2,000,000 seeded chi-square reference draws for the sectioned model; 20 named key-class schemes.
scope.exclusions: Vigenere/Latin-square or other structured alphabets, alternate plaintext distributions, different segmentation, transposition, additional layers and any key recovery.

wulfic-position-alphabet-long-keys.title: Long byte keys as position alphabets on LP2
wulfic-position-alphabet-long-keys.question: Could these byte streams select the alphabet at each rune?
wulfic-position-alphabet-long-keys.finding: The source's negative-control gate passes. No LP2 setting reaches its +30-nat threshold; all five positive controls detect 12 settings, while 38 lack that power. The best LP2 score is 0.84 nats, below threshold.
wulfic-position-alphabet-long-keys.limitations: The model requires the named byte key to remain in step with each tested rune stream, with a fixed one-to-one substitution for every byte value. Short settings without detected positive controls are untestable; key skips, other phase rules and layered transformations remain open.

scope.representation: Canonical GP29 rune streams for each unsolved marked section 7–15 and the joined LP2-00–55 stream; five byte keys from the source hint file, its reversal and three source byte files. The three files' puzzle-payload provenance was not independently verified.
scope.procedure: Replay the pinned Stage S LP2 dependency for these same 50 cells, then run unchanged Stage W source with its aligned controls; independently verify all control counts, phase bounds, source-score agreement and verdict rules.
scope.parameters: Five key classings × ten section alignments; all source key phases; five same-length positives and five flat negatives per cell, plus one shuffled-key LP2 null per key; anti-doublet keep 0.19; source score threshold +30 nats.
scope.exclusions: Other source Stage S classings, alternate byte encodings, offsets beyond source phases, key skips/restarts, changing alphabets, other plaintext distributions and composed ciphers.

wulfic-prime-keyword-stream-families.title: Prime and keyword stream families
wulfic-prime-keyword-stream-families.question: Can a word or prime sequence act as the missing key?
wulfic-prime-keyword-stream-families.finding: The repeating-keyword search produced zero all-singleton fits among 540 settings (best IoC 1.119; 18/49 full-search shuffles reached it). The prime-stream search tested 11,880 settings and yielded nine permissive sequential screen hits; its highest IoC was 1.174 on LP2-09 (1/49 shuffles reached it), but that output missed all six one-rune checks and did not read as a passage. The keyword-stepped search tested 5,285,280 settings; 2,270 passed its all-singleton gate, none exceeded the source IoC 1.3 hit threshold, and its best gated IoC 1.281 was reached by 12/49 shuffles.
wulfic-prime-keyword-stream-families.limitations: The prime IoC peak is exploratory and 49 complete-search controls provide coarse tail resolution. Within-page shuffles preserve rune counts but are not a cipher model. Source keyword lists, prime generators, old page selections, offsets and screens define the tested scope. Some stepped arithmetic duplicates a published combined-key grid; neither a high IoC nor a quick-word fragment proves decryption.

scope.representation: Pinned archived rune bytes verified against current canonical LP2 GP29 values. Old source page_N equals current LP2-(N-17); branch-specific source word parsers set singleton positions.
scope.procedure: Replay three archived finite searches as one shared batch: source keywords, source prime generators and F-skip, and keyword-stepped prime streams. Preserve each source screen and compare branch maxima against 49 full-search within-page shuffles.
scope.parameters: 540 repeating-keyword settings on ten pages; 11,880 prime-stream settings on eight pages; 5,285,280 stepped-keyword settings on eleven pages; three arithmetic directions; 49 seeded complete-search controls, seed 20261023.
scope.exclusions: Other keywords, prime orders, resets, page sets, languages, model scorers, source-defined but uncalled prime generators, and the optional unverified verified_keys.json input.

wulfic-quagmire-random-alphabets.title: Random Quagmire alphabet families on LP2
wulfic-quagmire-random-alphabets.question: Do random Quagmire alphabets fit LP2's rune frequencies?
wulfic-quagmire-random-alphabets.finding: All source model and calibration gates pass. Twenty of 24 settings meet its strict raw and anti-doublet-adjusted lower-tail exclusion rule with power on at least 18/20 flat-key controls. Four uniform A–Z settings are untestable because their positive-control power is insufficient. No plaintext or key is produced.
wulfic-quagmire-random-alphabets.limitations: This is a frequency screen for the source's random-alphabet Quagmire model and six key distributions. A–Z settings remain open under the source rule. Deterministic keyword alphabets, other key distributions or boundary rules, exact key order and layered ciphers are outside scope.

scope.representation: Canonical 29-rune LP2-00–55 stream; pooled across 12,956 runes or grouped into source sections 7–9 and 11–15 for a separate fresh-alphabet statistic.
scope.procedure: Run pinned Stage U's G1 model calibration, G2 flat-key power and G3 same-family false-exclusion checks, then score all 24 LP2 settings. Independently rebuild both manuscript chi-square statistics and audit each source verdict.
scope.parameters: Six declared key-value distributions x two tied/independent alphabet variants x pooled/sectioned statistics; 100,000 model draws per reference; 200 anti-doublet-factor ciphers per statistic; 20 power and 20 same-family controls per setting; raw and adjusted P<=0.0001, power>=18/20.
scope.exclusions: Other key distributions, nonrandom or named alphabets, key-order recovery, alternative boundaries, layers and decryption quality.

wulfic-separator-clock-alberti.title: A rotating alphabet with a separator clock
wulfic-separator-clock-alberti.question: Could the word separators tell a rotating alphabet when to turn?
wulfic-separator-clock-alberti.finding: Across eleven actual LP2 targets, all 1,682 distinct effective schedules per page yield zero outputs above the source's normalized-IoC 1.4 gate with either parser. The highest LP2 values are 1.164 (literal parser) and 1.159 (canonical correction). The source's twelfth named page is solved LP1-15; its literal parser yields two gated outputs but its corrected parser yields none. Eight known-reading plants recover and pass the gate; none of 49 whole-search page-shuffle controls passes either.
wulfic-separator-clock-alberti.limitations: The source parser omits canonical ᛄ; corrected parsing is a new bounded variant rather than unchanged historical execution. Its old page 15 is solved LP1-15 and excluded from the unsolved-page maximum. The 49 shuffles provide no calibrated probability with zero gated maxima. A constant starting phase cannot alter IoC; nonzero-phase readings were not separately scored. No plaintext language, extra layer or general changing-alphabet family is ruled out.

scope.representation: Pinned old Wulfic page files with exact source parser and a separate canonical-GP rune correction. Old page15 is solved LP1-15 control only.
scope.procedure: Enumerate all source directions, two shifts and three modes, deduplicate 5,046 named settings to 1,682 effective outputs, score source normalized IoC and above-gate bigrams/trigrams on each of eleven LP2 targets. Repeat complete search on 49 pagewise shuffled controls for each parser.
scope.parameters: 11 LP2 pages plus one solved LP1 source target; 2 parsers; 29 rune shifts × 29 separator shifts × 2 directions × 3 modes; 49 complete-search shuffles; seed 330123.
scope.exclusions: Other source pages, nonzero-phase readings (the IoC gate is invariant to constant phase), new separator rules, key switching, other alphabets, extra encryption layers and general Alberti disk mechanisms.

wulfic-session17-period-detectors.title: Two checks for a repeating key length
wulfic-session17-period-detectors.question: Do these pages show a repeating key length?
wulfic-session17-period-detectors.finding: The known-text lag screen found no source-defined hit. The split-column screen flagged many pages, but it flagged about as many after shuffling; both could detect a clean planted period.
wulfic-session17-period-detectors.limitations: Only source passages, sampled offsets, named pages and prime periods were checked. A flagged period is not a decipherment.

scope.representation: Exact committed Wulfic page21–54 rune files aligned to current LP2-04–37; eight source-literal candidate passages digraph encoded by the pinned rule.
scope.procedure: Replay source Test8 full candidate/offset/prime-period lag scan on 14 pages, Test9 split-column IoC and repeated-trigram divisor summaries on 34 pages, one period13 plant and 49 shared full-search page shuffles.
scope.parameters: Test8: 4,239 distinct page/text/offset lag grids, two equivalent key signs, prime periods through113 and strict >0.25; Test9: source prime periods through131, p≤page length/3, split mean IoC >1.3×base; 49 shared shuffles.
scope.exclusions: Test8 source fallback weak-output display and downstream word/phrase score after a passed gate, alternate candidate passages, nonprime periods, interrupted/restarted keys, and a decryptor claim.

wulfic-square-title-vocabulary.title: LP2-15 square-derived title keys
wulfic-square-title-vocabulary.question: Does the LP2-15 square decode its short heading?
wulfic-square-title-vocabulary.finding: The pinned source reports 0/30 complete two-word vocabulary passes. Its 20,000 seeded random nine-rune subtraction keys also yield zero passes. Independent site-text arithmetic reproduces every candidate output; optional full source replay reproduces the vocabulary verdicts and control byte-for-byte.
wulfic-square-title-vocabulary.limitations: A strict vocabulary miss for these 30 fixed candidates cannot exclude other square routes, shifts, spelling conventions, keys, vocabularies or a different cipher on the LP2-15 body. Zero hits in 20,000 random keys does not mean a zero chance probability.

scope.representation: First nine archived LP2-15 runes with the visible 4+5 word boundary, and its printed 16-value number square. GP29 zero-based indices.
scope.procedure: Run only the pinned Stage I title function; independently derive all five 16-value sequences, compare the constructed cell-value set with the printed panel and recalculate all 30 two-word outputs from Liberpedia page text.
scope.parameters: Five declared sequences x outward/inward x ciphertext-key, ciphertext+key and key-ciphertext, modulo 29; first nine key values; complete two-word vocabulary gate; 20,000 seeded random-key controls.
scope.exclusions: Alternate source routes, key starts, body text, vocabulary, GP spelling, punctuation choices and additional cipher layers.

wulfic-stage-ab-reset-alphabets.title: Restarted alphabets at five LP2 boundaries
wulfic-stage-ab-reset-alphabets.question: Could the key restart on each page or line?
wulfic-stage-ab-reset-alphabets.finding: Across 12,956 runes and five boundary types, LP2 repeats stayed near flat-rune expectations and below the conservative bound from both planted plaintext sources. The 1,000-null and 200-per-source-control run reproduced the public result and control tables byte-for-byte.
wulfic-stage-ab-reset-alphabets.limitations: This tests Wulfic Stage AB’s shared, position-dependent substitution alphabets with its anti-doublet postprocessing and two plaintext controls. It does not exclude every page- or line-reset cipher, feedback rule, other plaintext distribution, or independently chosen alphabet per unit.

scope.representation: All 12,956 GP runes on 55 rune-bearing LP2-00–55 pages; source boundary marks are preserved, including words that wrap lines or pages.
scope.procedure: Replay Wulfic Stage AB from pinned revision and count equal ciphertext runes at equal in-unit positions for five restart boundaries; compare with 1,000 flat anti-doublet nulls and two sets of 200 planted restart encryptions.
scope.parameters: Five unit types, seed 3301, GP29; original five-sigma log-count lower criterion.
scope.exclusions: Other reset locations, feedback, unique alphabets per unit, non-rune channels, distinct plaintext priors and alternative doublet handling.

wulfic-stage-af-unit-shifts.title: Unit shifts in a restarted LP2 key
wulfic-stage-af-unit-shifts.question: What if a page or line key restarts with a different shift?
wulfic-stage-af-unit-shifts.finding: All five within-unit difference counts sat near the source’s flat-rune null and below its planted shifted-restart bounds. The complete 200-null and 100-per-source simulation reproduced both original result tables byte-for-byte.
wulfic-stage-af-unit-shifts.limitations: This tests a shared restarting position key plus one constant shift per unit, additive or Beaufort, with within-unit gaps 2–300 and the source’s two plaintext controls. It does not exclude nonlinear feedback, changing shifts within a unit, other plaintext distributions or arbitrary restart schemes.

scope.representation: All 12,956 GP runes on 55 rune-bearing LP2-00–55 pages, with segment, paragraph, clause, line and page boundaries preserved.
scope.procedure: Replay Wulfic Stage AF from pinned revision. For each boundary type count equal within-unit mod-29 differences between positions separated by 2–300 runes; compare with 200 flat anti-doublet nulls and 100 planted draws from each of two plaintext sources.
scope.parameters: GP29, five unit types, gap 2–300, seed 3301; planted additive and Beaufort directions alternate; original five-sigma log-count criterion.
scope.exclusions: Different state equations, shifts changing inside a unit, other gap ranges or boundary marks, other plaintext priors and alternative doublet handling.

wulfic-structural-pip-ps-normalized.title: Prime-indexed-prime and P.S. keys with a corrected IoC screen
wulfic-structural-pip-ps-normalized.question: Can prime-derived numerical keys decode these pages?
wulfic-structural-pip-ps-normalized.finding: After the corrected score gate, 3,031 settings pass the source singleton filter and none exceeds 1.3. The global maximum is 1.226492057 on LP2-14. In 157/199 whole-search page shuffles, the maximum is at least as large. The two short P.S. encodings have no eligible page length and the digit encoding has no singleton-admissible setting.
wulfic-structural-pip-ps-normalized.limitations: This concerns one explicitly amended score screen and the finite called source grids. The shuffle distribution is a selection control rather than a cipher model, and neither the original zero-hit output nor this corrected variant excludes PIP/P.S. keys under other rules.

scope.representation: Pinned Wulfic source page_21–54 flat GP29 rune streams and separator-defined word lengths, verified equal to the corresponding LP2-04–37 site records.
scope.procedure: Generate the source PIP stream and three P.S.-number encodings, apply all eligible source offsets and three decode directions, require all one-rune words to be I/A, then screen by 29×raw IoC >1.3. Repeat the complete selected-max search on 199 page shuffles.
scope.parameters: Million-limit source sieve; PIP n bound 50,000 and offsets 0–999; P.S. digit/pair/base29 encodings and offsets 0–49 subject to source length check; sub/add/Beaufort. Source page ordinals 21–54 map to LP2-04–37. No 7×7 key execution.
scope.exclusions: The original impossible raw-IoC hit gate is an audit, not a negative cipher test. No new key schedule, padding, cycling, altered singleton rule, replacement English scorer, other page range or claim of plaintext.

wulfic-systematic-stream-source.title: Prime streams and a short feedback key
wulfic-systematic-stream-source.question: Could a prime sequence or short feedback key decode these pages?
wulfic-systematic-stream-source.finding: On 38 matched LP2 pages, 2,964 prime-stream settings yielded 644 source-threshold hits (19 shuffled-search range 625–702). On three selected pages, all 6,365,529 two-value LFSR settings yielded 38,826 hits (shuffled range 33,694–44,833). The best stream IoC 1.140 was reached or exceeded by 16/19 controls; the best LFSR combined score was reached or exceeded by 11/19.
wulfic-systematic-stream-source.limitations: The source's IoC/bigram/I-or-A-singleton score is a permissive candidate screen, not a reading test. Nineteen within-page shuffles supply only a coarse descriptive selection control and are not a cipher model. Old source page labels actually select LP2-01–38; the source-defined but uncalled Fibonacci stream and unfinished Berlekamp–Massey reconstruction are excluded. Other generator lengths, feedback clocks and page ranges remain open.

scope.representation: Pinned source Git-object rune text using its exact GP29 alphabet and period/hyphen/bullet/space/newline word separators. Source page_18..55 maps to current LP2-01..38; separate LFSR selection is LP2-28,10,17.
scope.procedure: Run every entry of the source's 26-stream dictionary in three modes over every eligible source page. Run all 29^4 ordered two-value LFSR state/tap tuples in three modes over the three highest-singleton pages, including zero/singular tap cases. Preserve the source IoC, bigram and I/A singleton score and hit thresholds. Repeat the entire selected grids on 19 within-page rune shuffles.
scope.parameters: 2,964 stream page-settings; 6,365,529 LFSR page-settings; source thresholds combined>2 or IoC>1.5 for streams, combined>3 for LFSR; shuffle seed 20261023.
scope.exclusions: Uncalled Fibonacci generator, incomplete Berlekamp–Massey key reconstruction, pages outside source selection, other prime rules, longer/nonlinear feedback or different alphabet/language models.

wulfic-two-time-pad-premise.title: Do the proposed two-time-pad regions match?
wulfic-two-time-pad-premise.question: Do the claimed identical rune spans actually occur?
wulfic-two-time-pad-premise.finding: The proposed matching passages do not match. Five of the six pairs extend beyond the supplied text; the remaining pair agrees at only 7 of 404 rune positions. The separate page-pair search also missed most known examples of key reuse.
wulfic-two-time-pad-premise.limitations: This rejects the specific claims of identical passages, not key reuse in general. Different messages can produce different ciphertext under the same key, and this search was not reliable enough to rule that out.

scope.representation: Corrected source old page_21–54 = LP2-04–37, GP29 rune-only, continuous 8,226-rune stream. Label-disambiguation check on LP2-27 and LP2-44. Four direct-reading LP1 pages provide matched-length planted pairs.
scope.procedure: Check all six source asserted identical regions, the claimed page27/page44 prefix and period bounds on the original committed Git page objects; replay the separate all-page-pair ±IoC source function, then 199 whole-search page-wise shuffles and all ten fixed 137-rune shared-key plants.
scope.parameters: Six asserted regions, one 6,726-rune period, 34 pages, 561 unordered pairs ×2 operations=1,122 screens, IoC>1.15, 199 seeded full-search shuffles (seed20261023), five 137-rune reading windows forming ten fixed pairs.
scope.exclusions: Unknown key-reuse alignments or periods, arbitrary key clocks, crib readability scoring under the failed source-copy assumption, alternative transcriptions, and separate solved/reference-text running-key branches.
